### `shopping_mall_admin`

Admin user accounts with credentials, permissions, and authentication
metadata.

Represents platform administrators with full system control and
moderation privileges across the entire shopping_mall ecosystem. This
entity serves as the authoritative source for administrative access,
enabling secure management of users, products, orders, configurations,
and system policies.

Each admin account is linked to a dedicated session table for
authentication tracking and security auditing. Admin accounts have the
highest privilege level and can perform any operation within the system,
including modifying other admins' permissions. Access is strictly
controlled through authentication and authorization mechanisms.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Admin email address used for authentication and communication. Must be
  > unique across all admin accounts.
- `password_hash`
  > Cryptographic hash of the admin's password for secure authentication.
  > Never stored in plain text.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the admin account was created. Used for auditing and
  > compliance tracking.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the admin account was last updated. Used for tracking
  > changes to admin metadata.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the admin account was logically deleted. Supports soft
  > deletion for audit trails while maintaining referential integrity.

### `shopping_mall_audit_logs`

Immutable audit logs recording all administrative actions, including
actor, timestamp, IP, and change details.

Stores a comprehensive and tamper-proof history of all operations
performed by platform administrators. Each log entry captures what action
was taken, which admin performed it, what record was affected, and from
which IP address the action originated. This table serves as the primary
audit trail for compliance, security investigations, and operational
transparency.

Logs are immutable - once created, they are never modified or deleted
(though they may be logically soft-deleted to maintain audit integrity).
The description field captures rich context about the action performed,
enabling forensic analysis and regulatory reporting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`
  > The admin user who performed the audited action. {@link
  > shopping_mall_admin.id}.
- `action_type`
  > Type of administrative action performed. Standardized values include:
  > create, update, delete, activate, deactivate, modify, approve, reject,
  > reset, export, configure, alert. Used for categorization and automated
  > alerting.
- `description`
  > Detailed textual description of the administrative action and its
  > context. May include specific values changed, affected record
  > identifiers, and reason for the action. Used for forensic analysis and
  > compliance reporting.
- `affected_table_name`
  > Name of the database table that was affected by this administrative
  > action (e.g., 'shopping_mall_users', 'shopping_mall_products',
  > 'shopping_mall_platform_configurations'). Enables quick identification of
  > impacted entities.
- `affected_record_id`
  > Primary key identifier of the specific record that was affected by this
  > administrative action, if applicable. Null when the action affects
  > multiple records or system-wide settings.
- `ip_address`
  > IP address from which the administrative action was initiated. Essential
  > for security monitoring, geolocation analysis, and detecting unauthorized
  > access patterns.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this audit log entry was created. Always populated at the
  > moment the action occurred.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this audit log entry was logically soft-deleted. Used to
  > maintain audit trail integrity while allowing compliance with data
  > retention policies and regulatory requirements.

### `shopping_mall_platform_configurations`

Platform-wide configuration settings including branding, payment,
shipping, and security parameters.

Stores core operational parameters that control system-wide behavior
across all components including customer experience, payment processing,
shipping integrations, and administrative security policies. This entity
represents the master configuration for the entire e-commerce platform
and is managed exclusively through the admin dashboard by platform
administrators.

Configuration values override default system behaviors and are loaded at
runtime by all services. Changes to this configuration are tracked in the
shopping_mall_config_history table to maintain audit trails and support
rollback capabilities. This table does not store historical versions but
rather the current active configuration state.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `branding_title`
  > Primary brand name displayed throughout the platform. Used in headers,
  > emails, and UI elements. Must reflect the official company brand
  > identity.
- `branding_logo_url`
  > HTTP/HTTPS URL pointing to the platform's primary logo image. Used in UI
  > headers and email templates. Must be a publicly accessible, properly
  > formatted URI.
- `payment_gateway_primary`
  > Primary payment gateway identifier (e.g., 'stripe', 'paypal',
  > 'razorpay'). Determines the default payment processing provider for all
  > transactions when not overridden per region or method.
- `payment_gateway_secondary`
  > Secondary payment gateway identifier for failover purposes. Used when
  > primary gateway is unavailable. Must be a valid identifier from supported
  > payment providers.
- `shipping_carrier_primary`
  > Primary shipping carrier identifier (e.g., 'fedex', 'ups', 'dhl',
  > 'usps'). Used for default shipping method selection and rate calculation
  > when no specific carrier is chosen by the customer.
- `shipping_carrier_secondary`
  > Secondary shipping carrier identifier for fallback purposes. Used when
  > the primary carrier is unavailable or has service disruptions.
- `currency_code`
  > Base currency code (ISO 4217) used for all financial transactions on the
  > platform. Common values: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY. All monetary values are
  > stored in this currency unless overridden by multi-currency support.
- `tax_calculation_strategy`
  > Method for calculating sales tax: 'origin', 'destination',
  > 'business_address'. Determines whether tax is calculated based on seller
  > location, customer location, or registered business location.
- `email_sender_domain`
  > Domain used as the sender domain for all platform emails (e.g.,
  > 'notifications.shoppingmallsystem.com'). Must be DNS-verified and
  > configured with correct SPF/DKIM records for deliverability.
- `default_locale`
  > Default language and region locale for users who haven't set preferences.
  > Format: ISO 639-1 language code plus ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code
  > (e.g., 'en-US', 'ja-JP').
- `max_session_duration_minutes`
  > Maximum session duration in minutes for all user types (customers,
  > sellers, admins) before requiring re-authentication. Enforces security
  > policy for session management.
- `session_inactivity_timeout_minutes`
  > Inactivity timeout period in minutes after which user sessions are
  > automatically expired. Applies to all actor types regardless of session
  > type.
- `password_complexity_min_length`
  > Minimum character length required for passwords across all user types.
  > Enforces basic password strength standards.
- `password_complexity_require_uppercase`
  > Indicates whether passwords must contain at least one uppercase letter.
  > Part of password complexity rules enforced during registration and
  > password changes.
- `password_complexity_require_lowercase`
  > Indicates whether passwords must contain at least one lowercase letter.
  > Part of password complexity rules enforced during registration and
  > password changes.
- `password_complexity_require_numbers`
  > Indicates whether passwords must contain at least one numeric digit. Part
  > of password complexity rules enforced during registration and password
  > changes.
- `password_complexity_require_symbols`
  > Indicates whether passwords must contain at least one special symbol
  > (e.g., !@#$%^&*). Part of password complexity rules enforced during
  > registration and password changes.
- `login_failed_attempts_threshold`
  > Maximum number of failed login attempts allowed before account locking
  > mechanism activates. Prevents brute force attacks on user credentials.
- `login_lockout_duration_minutes`
  > Duration in minutes that an account remains locked after exceeding the
  > failed login attempts threshold. Provides temporary protection against
  > automated attacks.
- `ip_blocking_enabled`
  > Enables or disables automated IP blocking system that detects and blocks
  > malicious or suspicious IP addresses based on behavior patterns.
- `fraud_detection_enabled`
  > Enables or disables real-time fraud detection system that analyzes
  > transaction patterns, shipping addresses, and device fingerprints for
  > potential fraudulent activity.
- `email_verification_required`
  > Requires all new customers and sellers to verify their email address
  > before their accounts can be fully activated and utilized for
  > transactions.
- `product_search_enabled`
  > Enables or disables the product search functionality across all
  > storefronts. When disabled, product discovery is limited to category
  > browsing.
- `review_submissions_enabled`
  > Controls whether customers can submit product reviews. When disabled, all
  > review submission features are hidden and disabled throughout the
  > platform.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration record was created. Immutable record of
  > when the current configuration set became active.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration record was last modified. Updated
  > automatically whenever any configuration field changes.
- `deleted_at`
  > Optional soft delete timestamp for audit purposes. When non-null,
  > indicates this configuration set has been retired and is no longer
  > active. Never deleted permanently.

### `shopping_mall_email_templates`

Email templates for administrative, customer, and seller notifications
with customizable content and trigger configurations.

Stores predefined email message templates used by the platform to send
automated notifications to users. These templates include subject lines
and body content that can be dynamically populated with user-specific
data. Admins can create, edit, and enable/disable templates for various
business scenarios such as order confirmations, password resets, policy
updates, and system alerts.

Templates are version-controlled through the platform's configuration
history system. The template content is separate from actual sent email
records to allow for template modifications without affecting historical
communications. Each template has a unique name used to reference it
programmatically.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`
  > Unique identifier for the template used in code and configuration. Must
  > be machine-readable and unique across all templates.
- `subject`
  > The email subject line that will be used. May contain placeholders for
  > dynamic content such as {{user_name}} or {{order_id}}.
- `body`
  > The complete HTML content of the email template. Supports dynamic
  > placeholders that will be replaced with actual values when the email is
  > sent.
- `trigger`
  > The business event that triggers this template to be sent. Examples:
  > 'order_confirmation', 'password_reset', 'new_product_alert',
  > 'policy_update'.
- `context`
  > The intended recipient category for this template. Values: 'admin',
  > 'customer', 'seller'. Determines which users should receive this
  > notification.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this email template was created in the system.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this email template was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp marking when this template was logically deleted. Null
  > indicates the template is active.

### `shopping_mall_security_policies`

Platform-wide security policies governing admin login and session behavior.

Defines mandatory rules for password complexity, authentication session
duration, and IP access restrictions for all administrators. These
policies are enforced system-wide and managed independently by senior
administrators.

The policy record is versioned to maintain audit history of security
changes. When updated, the new policy replaces the previous active
version, while old versions are preserved for compliance audits. The
policy can be disabled by setting deleted_at, but never deleted
permanently to preserve audit trail.

This table does not store admin credentials - those reside in
shopping_mall_admin. This table defines the security rules those
credentials must meet and how sessions behave.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `password_complexity`
  > Required password complexity pattern using regex (e.g.,
  > '^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[!@#$%^&*]).{12,}
  > '). Enforces mandatory character types and minimum length.
- `min_password_length`
  > Minimum number of characters required in admin passwords. Must be at
  > least 12 according to enterprise security standards.
- `max_password_age`
  > Maximum age in days before admin passwords expire and must be changed.
  > Enforces regular credential rotation for security.
- `session_timeout_minutes`
  > Duration in minutes of inactivity after which admin sessions will expire
  > and require re-authentication. Applies to all admin sessions.
- `ip_allow_list`
  > Comma-separated list of allowed IP addresses or CIDR ranges (e.g.,
  > '192.168.1.0/24, 203.0.113.10'). Admins can only log in from these IPs if
  > list is defined.
- `ip_deny_list`
  > Comma-separated list of denied IP addresses or CIDR ranges (e.g.,
  > '192.0.2.1, 203.0.113.0/24'). Admins are blocked from logging in from
  > these IPs.
- `version`
  > Sequential version number for policy changes. Higher numbers indicate
  > newer policies. Used to identify the currently active security policy.
- `is_active`
  > Flag indicating whether this policy version is currently active and
  > enforced. Only one policy can be active at a time.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this security policy version was created and initialized.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this security policy version was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this policy version was logically deleted (soft delete).
  > Used to maintain audit history without permanent removal.

### `shopping_mall_compliance_records`

Immutable audit trail of regulatory compliance documentation for GDPR,
CCPA, and tax jurisdiction requirements.

Records all compliance-related documentation timestamps, jurisdiction
codes, and administrative verification details. Each record represents a
point-in-time snapshot of regulatory compliance status at the moment an
admin or system process confirms adherence to specific legal frameworks.

This table is append-only and never modified after creation. Deleted
records maintain their data with deleted_at timestamps to ensure complete
auditability for regulators. The table serves as legal evidence of
compliance and must preserve historical accuracy regardless of subsequent
system changes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`
  > The administrative user who verified or recorded this compliance
  > document. [shopping_mall_admin.id](#shopping_mall_admin).
- `jurisdiction`
  > Regulatory jurisdiction code (e.g., 'GDPR-EU', 'CCPA-CA', 'Tax-GB')
  > identifying the compliance standard being documented.
- `document_type`
  > Type of compliance document (e.g., 'Data Processing Agreement', 'Privacy
  > Policy', 'Tax Registration Certificate').
- `document_reference`
  > Unique identifier or file reference for the compliance document (e.g.,
  > 'DOC-2026-001', 'GDPR-2026-ABCD').
- `effective_from`: The date and time from which this compliance record is legally effective.
- `effective_to`
  > The date and time until which this compliance record remains valid (null
  > if perpetual).
- `document_url`
  > URL to the stored document or digital certificate in the secure
  > compliance vault.
- `justification`
  > Detailed explanation provided by the admin or system regarding how this
  > record demonstrates compliance with the specified jurisdiction.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this compliance record was first created and recorded in
  > the system.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this compliance record was last updated (only for
  > metadata, never for document content).
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this record was marked as deleted (soft delete) for audit
  > trail purposes. Null if active.

### `shopping_mall_config_history`

Historical snapshots of platform configuration changes for audit and
rollback purposes.

Records point-in-time states of platform-wide settings whenever changes
are made by administrators. Each entry captures the previous and current
values of a configuration along with metadata about the changer and
timestamp. This enables full audit trails, rollback capabilities, and
historical analysis of configuration evolution.

Used to track system-wide changes including branding, payment, shipping,
security parameters, and other platform configurations. The table follows
append-only pattern with no updates to existing records - new snapshots
are created for each configuration modification.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `platform_configuration_id`
  > Configuration being modified. {@link
  > shopping_mall_platform_configurations.id}.
- `admin_id`: Admin who made the configuration change. [shopping_mall_admin.id](#shopping_mall_admin).
- `change_type`: Type of change performed: 'created', 'updated', or 'deleted'.
- `old_value`
  > JSON string representation of configuration values before the change.
  > Null for 'created' changes.
- `new_value`
  > JSON string representation of configuration values after the change. Null
  > only for 'deleted' changes.
- `description`
  > Human-readable description of the change reason or context provided by
  > the administrator.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this configuration snapshot was created. Never updated -
  > immutable record of change time.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete flag for compliance with audit trail requirements. Null
  > indicates active record.

### `shopping_mall_data_exports`

Admin-initiated data export requests for compliance, reporting, or
migration purposes.

Tracks requests made by administrators to export system data in specified
formats with filters and preferences. Each record represents a single
export job lifecycle from initiation to delivery. Export data is not
stored directly in this table but referenced via file paths or URLs.

Exports are triggered for compliance audits, data migration, analytics
reporting, or system backups. Administrators must specify format (CSV,
JSON, Excel), selection filters, and delivery method. System generates
the export asynchronously and records the outcome.

Export jobs may fail due to resource constraints, invalid filters, or
system errors. Successful exports are delivered via email attachment or
secure S3 link with optional encryption for sensitive data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`
  > Admin user who initiated this export request. {@link
  > shopping_mall_admin.id}.
- `request_metadata`
  > Additional JSON metadata about the export request (e.g., custom filters,
  > advanced options). Store as serialized JSON string.
- `format`
  > Target export format (CSV, JSON, Excel). Valid values: 'csv', 'json',
  > 'excel'.
- `requested_fields`
  > Comma-separated list of fields requested for export (e.g.,
  > 'id,email,created_at,order_total').
- `filters`
  > JSON string encoding filters applied to data (e.g., status='completed',
  > date_range='2024-01-01..2024-12-31').
- `status`
  > Current status of the export request. Valid values: 'requested',
  > 'processing', 'completed', 'failed', 'delivered'.
- `delivery_method`
  > Method used to deliver the exported file. Valid values: 'email', 's3',
  > 'download_url'.
- `email`
  > Email address to which the exported file was sent (if
  > delivery_method='email').
- `file_path`
  > Full S3 filepath where the exported file is stored (if
  > delivery_method='s3').
- `download_url`
  > Temporary secure URL to download the exported file (if
  > delivery_method='download_url').
- `encrypted`: Whether the exported file was encrypted for security purposes.
- `encryption_key_reference`
  > Reference ID for the encryption key used (if encrypted=true). Links to
  > key management system.
- `encrypted_at`: Timestamp when the file was encrypted (if encrypted=true).
- `completed_at`: Timestamp when the export generation completed successfully.
- `failed_at`: Timestamp when the export failed (if status='failed').
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when the file was successfully delivered or made available for
  > download.
- `error_message`
  > Detailed error message explaining why the export failed (if
  > status='failed').
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this export request was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this export record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp, used to mark records as logically deleted without
  > purging.

### `shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts`

System-generated alerts triggered by anomalies including inventory
errors, fraud detection, and performance thresholds.

Tracks critical system events that require administrative attention,
serving as a monitoring and alerting layer for platform governance.
Alerts are immutable system-generated events that are consumed through
administrative dashboards and reports, not user-managed entities.

Each alert includes type, severity, message, affected entity context, and
timestamps for detection and resolution. The system automatically
generates alerts based on predefined thresholds and anomaly detection
rules, creating an audit trail for operational oversight and incident
response.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`
  > Admin who resolved this alert, if applicable. {@link
  > shopping_mall_admin.id}.
- `alert_type`
  > Category of the alert (e.g., 'low_inventory', 'fraud_attempt',
  > 'payment_timeout'). Must be one of predefined system alert types for
  > consistent categorization.
- `severity`
  > Criticality level of the alert ('low', 'medium', 'high', 'critical').
  > Determines priority for administrative response and escalation paths.
- `message`
  > Detailed description of the alert including error codes, context, and
  > system-generated diagnostic information.
- `entity_type`
  > Type of system entity affected by the alert (e.g., 'product_variant',
  > 'order', 'payment', 'user', 'system').
- `entity_id`
  > ID of the specific system entity affected by this alert, if applicable
  > (e.g., product_variant_id, order_id). {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_variants.id} or other relevant entity. Null when
  > alert is system-wide.
- `detected_at`
  > Timestamp when the alert was detected by monitoring systems. This
  > represents the moment the anomaly was identified.
- `resolved_at`
  > Timestamp when the alert was resolved or acknowledged by an admin. Null
  > if still active. Indicates duration of alert exposure.
- `metadata`
  > JSON string containing additional structured context about the alert
  > (e.g., thresholds breached, metrics values, system state). For
  > machine-readable details beyond the message field.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this alert record was created in the database. Always
  > matches detected_at but represents database insertion time.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this alert record was last updated (typically when
  > resolved). Used for change tracking and audit.

### `shopping_mall_user_flags`

User activity flags raised by admin monitoring for suspicious behavior,
duplicate accounts, and policy violations.

Tracks administrative flags on customer and seller accounts when systemic
anomalies, policy violations, or potential fraud are detected. Each flag
represents a potential security or compliance issue requiring review by
platform administrators.

Flags are created manually by admins during monitoring activities or
automatically by system alerts. They link to the specific user account
being flagged and capture the reason, type, and current status of the
flag. This table enables comprehensive monitoring, audit trails, and
targeted investigations by the security team.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `flagged_by_admin_id`: The administrator who created this flag. [shopping_mall_admin.id](#shopping_mall_admin).
- `flagged_customer_id`: The customer account that was flagged. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `flagged_seller_id`: The seller account that was flagged. [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor being flagged: 'customer' or 'seller'. Used to determine
  > which foreign key field contains the targeted entity.
- `flag_type`
  > Category of the flag - e.g., 'duplicate_account', 'fraudulent_activity',
  > 'policy_violation', 'suspicious_behavior', 'inappropriate_content'.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the flagged activity, including observations,
  > evidence, and context for investigation.
- `status`
  > Current status of the flag: 'active', 'resolved', or 'cancelled'. Only
  > active flags are considered for operational purposes.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this flag was created by the admin.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this flag was last updated (e.g., status change).
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this flag was removed from active monitoring (soft
  > delete). If null, flag remains active.

operations.description:
Registers a new customer account by creating a user record in the shopping_mall_customers table. The operation requires email and password_hash fields to be provided. Upon successful registration, the system sets email_verified to false and generates a new JWT access and refresh token pair. The email_verified field is used to enforce email verification requirements before full account access is granted. Temporary guest sessions are converted to permanent customer accounts through this flow.

The email field is validated for uniqueness prior to account creation, and password_hash is stored using the platform's bcrypt implementation with a cost factor of 12. The password_reset_token and password_reset_expires fields are initialized as null during registration to ensure they are not accidentally pre-populated.

This is the only entry point for new customers to join the ecosystem. The operation is publicly accessible and does not require prior authentication.

Related operations: verifyEmail, login, refresh.

requestBody.description: Registration data for a new customer account.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and basic customer profile after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates an existing customer by validating their email and password_hash against the shopping_mall_customers table. If credentials are valid, the system verifies that the account is not suspended or deleted, and returns a new JWT access token and refresh token.

The email field is used to locate the customer record. The password_hash field must match the stored hash using bcrypt comparison. The email_verified field is checked to ensure the email has been verified, though in this system, login is allowed even before verification for usability purposes.

In case of failed authentication, no information is revealed about whether the email exists, protecting against enumeration attacks. The system logs authentication attempts in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table for security monitoring.

The login operation triggers the creation of a new shopping_mall_customer_sessions record that stores the device context and session expiration. This session will be refreshed automatically by the refresh operation.

Related operations: join, refresh, resetPassword.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for customer authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and basic customer profile after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Renews the customer's access token using a valid refresh token stored in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. This operation requires a valid refresh token, which is obtained after successful join or login operations.

The refresh token is validated against the customer session record. If the session is still active and has not expired (default 7-day expiration), a new access token is issued. The refresh token remains valid for future refresh operations until it expires or is explicitly revoked.

The operation ensures that only sessions originating from the same device/IP remain valid through a device fingerprint comparison. This prevents token theft attacks where credentials are intercepted.

This operation is designed to be used by mobile apps and SPAs that need long-lived sessions without requiring users to re-authenticate frequently. The refresh token rotation mechanism updates the refresh_token value upon each refresh to prevent replay attacks.

Related operations: login, join, enableTwoFactor, disableTwoFactor.

requestBody.description: Refresh token to renew access token.

responseBody.description: Newly issued access token and refreshed refresh token.

operations.description: Handles all non-authentication operations for the customer role including password reset, email verification, and two-factor authentication management. Only one null-type operation is permitted to comply with authorization rules. This single operation consolidates all customer self-service actions: resetting password via token (POST /auth/customer/password/reset/{token}), verifying email via token (POST /auth/customer/email/verify/{token}), enabling two-factor authentication (POST /auth/customer/two-factor/enable), disabling two-factor authentication (POST /auth/customer/two-factor/disable), and changing password (POST /auth/customer/password/change). Each sub-action is distinguished by the path and request body. The customer must be authenticated to perform changing password, enrolling or disabling two-factor auth. Password reset and email verification are public. This comprehensive single endpoint approach eliminates ambiguity in authorization type and abides by AutoBE's strict authorizationType = null uniqueness rule.

operations.description:
This null-authorization operation enables seller actors to browse available products and product categories on the shoppingMall platform.

Based on the shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_categories tables, this operation provides read-only access to product listings without requiring authentication. The product catalog is structured with primary categories and optional secondary category associations, enabling efficient product discovery.

This operation supports the critical business requirement for sellers to evaluate product offerings, understand market positioning, and identify potential inventory opportunities without needing to be authenticated. The product information accessed (name, description, category, images) is all publicly available data stored in the shopping_mall_products table.

As a member actor (seller), this operation is essential for their business workflow, allowing them to research market trends and competitor offerings before making inventory decisions. The operation follows a standard REST pattern for resource listing (PATCH method) to support potential filtering, sorting, and pagination requirements.

This authorizationType=null operation balances platform openness with security by only exposing non-sensitive product information while maintaining strict access control on all authenticated operations. It complements the join/login/refresh authentication operations by enabling initial platform exploration before account creation.

The operation adheres to the platform's information architecture where product catalog browsing is designated as a public-facing, non-authenticated activity that serves both potential sellers and customers alike.

responseBody.description: List of available products with their core information for display in the product catalog.

operations.description:
This operation allows a seller to register and create an account on the shoppingMall platform.

Based on the shopping_mall_sellers database table, this registration flow collects the mandatory credentials required for seller authentication: email address, password hash, and seller-specific metadata. The email field is required in the sellers table to ensure unique identity verification, while the password field stores a cryptographically hashed value for secure authentication.

Seller registration requires the seller's business name, contact email, and phone number as mandatory fields in the database schema, enabling comprehensive seller profiling and communication. The createdAt timestamp is automatically set by the system when registration completes, ensuring audit trail integrity.

This operation establishes the foundation for seller identity in the system, creating a persistent identifier that will be used across all subsequent seller-facing features. The generated refresh token is immediately issued to enable session persistence after registration, following the pattern established in the authentication architecture.

All data submitted in this operation maps directly to corresponding fields in the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring type safety and data integrity. The operation follows enterprise authentication standards with secure password encoding and email validation, consistent with the platform's security policy.

responseBody.description: Authentication token and seller identifier returned upon successful registration.

operations.description:
This login operation authenticates a seller using their registered email and password credentials.

The shopping_mall_sellers table contains the necessary fields for authentication: email (primary identifier) and password (hashed), which are validated during this process. The system cross-references the credentials against the stored data in the sellers table to confirm identity.

Upon successful authentication, the server generates a new access token and refresh token pair as specified in the authentication architecture. The seller's ID from the sellers table is embedded in the token payload, enabling role-based access control throughout subsequent operations.

The login operation maintains the system's security posture by enforcing rate limiting against brute force attacks and recording authentication events in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table for audit purposes.

This operation is specific to seller accounts and cannot be used for other actor types. It strictly validates data against the structure and constraints defined in the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring type-safe authentication flow.

responseBody.description: Access token and refresh token issued upon successful authentication.

operations.description:
This refresh operation allows a seller to obtain a new access token using a valid refresh token without requiring re-authentication.

The operation verifies the provided refresh token against the valid sessions recorded in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table in the database. When validated, a new access token is generated and issued with updated expiration settings.

Refresh tokens are designed to provide session persistence while maintaining security through token rotation. Upon successful refresh, the old refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued, following the security model described in the authentication requirements.

The system only accepts refresh tokens issued from the seller role, ensuring token isolation between actor types. The refresh operation does not require email or password re-submission, relying solely on the cryptographically validated refresh token from the session record.

This operation is critical for maintaining seamless user experience while upholding the security policy of time-limited access tokens, in alignment with the shopping_mall_seller_sessions structure.

responseBody.description: New access token and refresh token pair returned after successful rotation.

operations.description:
Creates a new administrator account through registration. The system validates the email format and uniqueness, requires password with minimum 8-character complexity, and sets initial account status to 'pending_email_verification'. An email verification token is generated and sent to the provided email address. The actual implementation uses the 'email' and 'password' fields from the shopping_mall_admin table to store user data. Subsequent email verification activates the account. This operation is publicly accessible and generates JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration. This operation is required for system administration access.

Account registration must occur through this endpoint; administrators cannot be created via database inserts or direct API calls for security compliance.

Security considerations include limiting concurrent registration attempts per IP, rate-limiting to prevent brute-force attacks, and mandatory password complexity requirements that enforce upper/lowercase, numbers, and special characters.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/login for authentication after registration and POST /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Email verification must be completed before full permissions are granted.

Account status and email fields must be populated correctly to ensure proper workflow integration.

Must reference email and password column expectations from the database schema.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens issued upon successful registration.

operations.description:
Authenticates an administrator user by validating their email and password against the stored credentials in the shopping_mall_admin table. The system checks for active account status and enforces security policies including account lockout after 5 failed attempts. Upon successful authentication, a secure JWT access token with 15-minute expiration and a refresh token stored in an httpOnly cookie are issued.

This operation uses the 'email' and 'password' fields from the shopping_mall_admin table for validation and the 'last_login_at' field to record authentication timestamp.

Security considerations include requiring HTTPS, implementing IP-based rate limiting, using time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) as secondary authentication where necessary, and invalidating all previous sessions after password change.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/join for initial registration and POST /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Account suspension or deactivation (is_active=false) prevents login attempts.

Must reference email and password column expectations from the database schema.

operations.description:
Renews the administrator's access token by validating the refresh token stored in the httpOnly cookie. This operation maintains session continuity without requiring re-entry of credentials. The system checks the validity of the refresh token and ensures it hasn't been revoked or expired. Upon success, a new access token is issued with a fresh 15-minute expiration while the refresh token remains unchanged, maintaining session state.

This operation references the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table for refresh token validation and ties expiration to the user's session context from the shopping_mall_admin table's 'id' and 'is_active' fields.

Security considerations include cookie flag security (httpOnly, secure, sameSite=strict), refresh token revocation on logout or password change, and refresh token expiration after 7 days of inactivity.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/login for initial authentication and POST /auth/admin/logout for explicit session termination. A refresh token must be present in the httpOnly cookie for this operation to succeed.

Must reference session and active status expectations from the database schema.

responseBody.description: New access token issued after successful refresh token validation.

operations.description:
Deactivates a specific administrator account to suspend access without permanently removing the record. This operation requires admin-level authorization. The system updates the 'is_active' field in the shopping_mall_admin table from true to false based on the admin's ID contained in the path. All active sessions for the target account are immediately invalidated. This is the only authorized null-type operation affecting account status.

Implementation uses the 'id' field from the shopping_mall_admin table to identify the account. Security considerations include requiring admin-level authorization, audit logging, and preventing unauthorized deactivation. An ID must be provided via the path.

Related operations: GET /auth/admin/account/{id} (to inspect status) and POST /auth/admin/account/reactivate/{id} (to reverse deactivation, if supported).

Based on the shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_categories tables, this operation provides read-only access to product listings without requiring authentication. The product catalog is structured with primary categories and optional secondary category associations, enabling efficient product discovery.

This operation supports the critical business requirement for sellers to evaluate product offerings, understand market positioning, and identify potential inventory opportunities without needing to be authenticated. The product information accessed (name, description, category, images) is all publicly available data stored in the shopping_mall_products table.

As a member actor (seller), this operation is essential for their business workflow, allowing them to research market trends and competitor offerings before making inventory decisions. The operation follows a standard REST pattern for resource listing (PATCH method) to support potential filtering, sorting, and pagination requirements.

This authorizationType=null operation balances platform openness with security by only exposing non-sensitive product information while maintaining strict access control on all authenticated operations. It complements the join/login/refresh authentication operations by enabling initial platform exploration before account creation.

The operation adheres to the platform's information architecture where product catalog browsing is designated as a public-facing, non-authenticated activity that serves both potential sellers and customers alike.

responseBody.description: List of available products with their core information for display in the product catalog.

operations.description:
This operation allows a seller to register and create an account on the shoppingMall platform.

Based on the shopping_mall_sellers database table, this registration flow collects the mandatory credentials required for seller authentication: email address, password hash, and seller-specific metadata. The email field is required in the sellers table to ensure unique identity verification, while the password field stores a cryptographically hashed value for secure authentication.

Seller registration requires the seller's business name, contact email, and phone number as mandatory fields in the database schema, enabling comprehensive seller profiling and communication. The createdAt timestamp is automatically set by the system when registration completes, ensuring audit trail integrity.

This operation establishes the foundation for seller identity in the system, creating a persistent identifier that will be used across all subsequent seller-facing features. The generated refresh token is immediately issued to enable session persistence after registration, following the pattern established in the authentication architecture.

All data submitted in this operation maps directly to corresponding fields in the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring type safety and data integrity. The operation follows enterprise authentication standards with secure password encoding and email validation, consistent with the platform's security policy.

requestBody.description: Seller registration data including authentication credentials and business information.

responseBody.description: Authentication token and seller identifier returned upon successful registration.

operations.description:
This login operation authenticates a seller using their registered email and password credentials.

The shopping_mall_sellers table contains the necessary fields for authentication: email (primary identifier) and password (hashed), which are validated during this process. The system cross-references the credentials against the stored data in the sellers table to confirm identity.

Upon successful authentication, the server generates a new access token and refresh token pair as specified in the authentication architecture. The seller's ID from the sellers table is embedded in the token payload, enabling role-based access control throughout subsequent operations.

The login operation maintains the system's security posture by enforcing rate limiting against brute force attacks and recording authentication events in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table for audit purposes.

This operation is specific to seller accounts and cannot be used for other actor types. It strictly validates data against the structure and constraints defined in the shopping_mall_sellers table, ensuring type-safe authentication flow.

requestBody.description: Authentication credentials for seller login.

responseBody.description: Access token and refresh token issued upon successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
This refresh operation allows a seller to obtain a new access token using a valid refresh token without requiring re-authentication.

The operation verifies the provided refresh token against the valid sessions recorded in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table in the database. When validated, a new access token is generated and issued with updated expiration settings.

Refresh tokens are designed to provide session persistence while maintaining security through token rotation. Upon successful refresh, the old refresh token is invalidated and a new one is issued, following the security model described in the authentication requirements.

The system only accepts refresh tokens issued from the seller role, ensuring token isolation between actor types. The refresh operation does not require email or password re-submission, relying solely on the cryptographically validated refresh token from the session record.

This operation is critical for maintaining seamless user experience while upholding the security policy of time-limited access tokens, in alignment with the shopping_mall_seller_sessions structure.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining a new access token.

responseBody.description: New access token and refresh token pair returned after successful rotation.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Creates a new administrator account through registration. The system validates the email format and uniqueness, requires password with minimum 8-character complexity, and sets initial account status to 'pending_email_verification'. An email verification token is generated and sent to the provided email address. The actual implementation uses the 'email' and 'password' fields from the shopping_mall_admin table to store user data. Subsequent email verification activates the account. This operation is publicly accessible and generates JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration. This operation is required for system administration access.

Account registration must occur through this endpoint; administrators cannot be created via database inserts or direct API calls for security compliance.

Security considerations include limiting concurrent registration attempts per IP, rate-limiting to prevent brute-force attacks, and mandatory password complexity requirements that enforce upper/lowercase, numbers, and special characters.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/login for authentication after registration and POST /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Email verification must be completed before full permissions are granted.

Account status and email fields must be populated correctly to ensure proper workflow integration.

Must reference email and password column expectations from the database schema.

requestBody.description: Credentials for administrator account creation.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens issued upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates an administrator user by validating their email and password against the stored credentials in the shopping_mall_admin table. The system checks for active account status and enforces security policies including account lockout after 5 failed attempts. Upon successful authentication, a secure JWT access token with 15-minute expiration and a refresh token stored in an httpOnly cookie are issued.

This operation uses the 'email' and 'password' fields from the shopping_mall_admin table for validation and the 'last_login_at' field to record authentication timestamp.

Security considerations include requiring HTTPS, implementing IP-based rate limiting, using time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) as secondary authentication where necessary, and invalidating all previous sessions after password change.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/join for initial registration and POST /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Account suspension or deactivation (is_active=false) prevents login attempts.

Must reference email and password column expectations from the database schema.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for administrator account.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens issued upon successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Renews the administrator's access token by validating the refresh token stored in the httpOnly cookie. This operation maintains session continuity without requiring re-entry of credentials. The system checks the validity of the refresh token and ensures it hasn't been revoked or expired. Upon success, a new access token is issued with a fresh 15-minute expiration while the refresh token remains unchanged, maintaining session state.

This operation references the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table for refresh token validation and ties expiration to the user's session context from the shopping_mall_admin table's 'id' and 'is_active' fields.

Security considerations include cookie flag security (httpOnly, secure, sameSite=strict), refresh token revocation on logout or password change, and refresh token expiration after 7 days of inactivity.

Related operations include POST /auth/admin/login for initial authentication and POST /auth/admin/logout for explicit session termination. A refresh token must be present in the httpOnly cookie for this operation to succeed.

Must reference session and active status expectations from the database schema.

requestBody.description: Refresh token from cookies for token renewal.

responseBody.description: New access token issued after successful refresh token validation.

operations.description:
Deactivates a specific administrator account to suspend access without permanently removing the record. This operation requires admin-level authorization. The system updates the 'is_active' field in the shopping_mall_admin table from true to false based on the admin's ID contained in the path. All active sessions for the target account are immediately invalidated. This is the only authorized null-type operation affecting account status.

Implementation uses the 'id' field from the shopping_mall_admin table to identify the account. Security considerations include requiring admin-level authorization, audit logging, and preventing unauthorized deactivation. An ID must be provided via the path.

Related operations: GET /auth/admin/account/{id} (to inspect status) and POST /auth/admin/account/reactivate/{id} (to reverse deactivation, if supported).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator account to deactivate. Must appear in path.

requestBody.description: Optional reason for deactivation. Used for audit purposes.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of account deactivation.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive channel information based on the requesting user's authorization level. Retrieve detailed information about a specific shopping mall channel by its unique business code.

This operation accesses the shopping_mall_channels table to return comprehensive details about a channel identified by its unique channelCode. The retrieval is read-only and returns a single channel object containing metadata such as channel name, description, status, and configuration settings that define its role and behavior within the shopping mall platform.

The operation supports enterprise use cases where channels represent distinct business segments, product categories, or regional storefronts. Each channel code is globally unique and serves as the canonical identifier for routing products, managing inventory, and configuring access controls at the channel level.

The response includes complete channel metadata to support comprehensive channel discovery and comparison. This information is cached for performance optimization and is used frequently by UI components such as channel selector widgets, merchandising dashboards, and channel comparison tools.

Create a new sales channel in the shopping mall platform. This operation allows admin users to establish new sales distribution channels for product listings and inventory management. The channel represents a distinct sales venue such as an online storefront, physical kiosk, or marketplace partnership.

The operation requires complete channel configuration data including name, description, sales type, and active status. All channels must be uniquely identified by a name that follows the pattern 'mainstore-<identifier>' for primary channels or 'partner-<partnername>' for third-party integrations.

Security: This endpoint is restricted to admin users only. Non-admin users will receive a 403 Forbidden response. The operation performs server-side validation to ensure the channel name follows the required naming pattern and no duplicate names exist in the system.

Business logic: Channel creation automatically generates a unique channel ID and assigns default permissions for associated seller groups. The channel's created_at and updated_at timestamps are automatically populated with server time. Channel status defaults to active unless explicitly set to inactive.

Related operations: List all channels (GET /channels), View channel details (GET /channels/{channelId}), Update channel configuration (PUT /channels/{channelId}), Disable channel (DELETE /channels/{channelId}).

operations.description:
Update a specific channel within the shopping mall platform's hierarchical content structure. This operation modifies the channel identified by its unique business code identifier, which is used in place of UUID identifiers for better human-readability in URLs. The channel entity represents a top-level organizational unit for products and content, enabling structured navigation and content grouping within the shopping mall platform.

Security considerations include rate limiting on update operations to prevent abuse of configuration changes and ensuring that only authorized administrators can modify channel settings. This operation updates metadata and configuration properties of the channel without affecting related products, categories, or content assignments.

Implementation note: The operation updates the shopping_mall_channels table using the channelCode field as the primary identifier, following the database schema definition which declares @@unique([code]) for this table. This design choice avoids exposing internal UUID identifiers in the API, promoting user-friendly URLs and reducing vulnerability to enumeration attacks.

Channel code identifiers are globally unique business identifiers, not internal database IDs, making them suitable for public-facing URLs. Examples of valid channel codes include 'electronics', 'home-and-garden', 'sports-outdoors', or 'fashion'.

The channel structure is fundamental to the shopping mall architecture, serving as the top-level organizational container for the entire product catalog. Multiple channels may exist to provide segmented shopping experiences for different customer segments or product categories.

Related operations:
- GET /channels/{channelCode}: Retrieve channel information
- DELETE /channels/{channelCode}: Soft-delete channel (mark as inactive)
- PATCH /channels: Search/list channels with filtering options

operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific channel from the shoppingMall platform. This operation targets the shopping_mall_channels table in the database schema and performs a hard delete, removing the channel record and all related data from the system. The channel's code identifier must be provided in the path parameter to precisely identify the target channel for deletion.

This operation immediately and permanently eliminates all content, settings, and relationships associated with the channel. All products, categories, and content that were assigned to this channel become inaccessible and are removed from the catalog structure. No recovery mechanism exists for deleted channels.

Authorization: This operation requires administrator privileges to prevent unauthorized deletion of critical platform components. The system validates that the authenticated user has sufficient permissions to remove channels before executing the deletion.

This operation has no request body, no response body, and no response status code. If the channel is successfully deleted, the server returns a 204 No Content status. If the channel with the given code does not exist, the server responds with 404 Not Found.

parameters.name: channelCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target channel (global scope)

The section code serves as a human-readable identifier for sections in the shopping mall platform, ensuring URLs remain readable and meaningful. This operation is used to display section content to customers on the storefront, loading all configurable properties such as banner images, section title, positioning, and display rules. The schema is designed around the shopping_mall_sections table, which contains all metadata for organizing the shopping mall catalog into distinct browsing areas.

Authentication is not required for this operation as sections are public content elements visible to all shoppers. The system retrieves section data directly from the shopping_mall_sections table without requiring user context, making this a truly public endpoint that supports anonymous browsing of the shopping mall structure.

The operation returns comprehensive section data including its name, display settings, content association, and positioning within the shopping mall hierarchy. operations.description:
Create a new section in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows administrators to create new organizational sections within the shopping mall ecosystem. Each section represents a distinct area of the platform that can contain products, services, or specialized content. The section creation process establishes the foundational structure for merchandise categorization and customer navigation.

The operation requires specification of section details including name, display order, and visibility settings. All sections must have a unique name to prevent conflicts in the platform's navigation hierarchy. Section names serve as both display identifiers and internal reference keys, ensuring consistent integration across customer-facing interfaces and administrative tools.

Administrative privileges are required to use this operation, as sections define the fundamental architecture of the shopping mall platform. Sections are not user-createable entities; their creation requires platform-wide strategic planning to maintain coherence and prevent organizational fragmentation. The system enforces strict naming validation to ensure all section identifiers follow camelCase conventions and avoid reserved keywords.

This operation integrates tightly with the shopping_mall_sections database entity, which maintains immutable records of all sections across the platform. Any attempt to create a section with a name that already exists will result in validation failure, ensuring data integrity of the platform's organizational structure. Once created, the section becomes immediately available in the platform's category navigation and can be populated with products through separate operations.

Note that section creation does not automatically assign products or sub-sections; these relationships are managed by separate operations. The created section's unique identifier is returned in the response for subsequent configuration and management operations.

requestBody.description: Details required to create a new shopping mall section.

responseBody.description: The newly created shopping mall section with system-generated identifiers and metadata.

Update operations must be performed by administrators only, as sections define the physical and organizational structure of the shopping mall. The section code is immutable and cannot be changed during an update - only other attributes like title, description, and layout can be modified. This ensures consistent reference identifiers in user interfaces, analytics, and external systems.

Security policy requires that only users with admin privileges can execute this operation. The system automatically validates that the specified sectionCode exists in the database and that the updated fields comply with data integrity constraints. Partial updates are supported - only the fields provided in the request body will be modified, leaving other fields unchanged.

This operation directly affects the hierarchical structure of the shopping mall. When a section is deleted, all products and categories that were associated with it become orphaned, which may affect product discovery and navigation in the user interface. There is no automatic cleanup or cascading logic performed by this operation.

This endpoint is exclusively for administrative purposes to clean up unused or deprecated sections. Only users with admin privileges can execute this operation due to the irreversible nature of the deletion. After deletion, section codes cannot be reused immediately as they remain in the system's audit logs.

operations.description:
Retrieve all system configurations for the shopping mall platform. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_configurations table from the database schema and returns all configured platform-wide settings including payment processing rules, shipping configurations, category hierarchies, and system-wide feature flags.

The platform uses shopping_mall_configurations to store critical operational parameters that affect all users and business processes across the shopping mall ecosystem. The configurations are managed exclusively by system administrators through the admin dashboard and are not directly editable by end users.

This operation returns the complete set of configuration settings as a single object containing all configurable parameters. The response includes settings for payment processing (supported methods, fee structures, currency conversion), shipping (carriers, methods, zone-based rules), product catalog (category hierarchy, search indexing, visibility rules), and system controls (feature flags, rate limits, maintenance modes).

The configuration data is cached at the application layer for performance optimization, and changes are propagated to all nodes in the distributed system. Configuration updates are handled through administrative workflows and require explicit deployment validation.

Key configurations include:
- payment: Defines allowed payment methods and their regional availability
- shipping: Specifies carriers and shipping methods available to customers
- catalog: Controls product category structure and visibility rules
- security: Manages rate limits, authentication policies, and audit settings
- features: Enables or disables platform features like wishlists and product reviews

Note: Configuration changes are not reflected in real-time for existing sessions. The system reloads configurations on a scheduled basis or following explicit administrator-initiated deployment events.

Related operations: Admins can update configurations through PATCH /admin/configurations with appropriate authorization and validation requirements.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Complete set of shopping mall platform configurations including payment, shipping, catalog, security, and feature settings.

operations.description:
Retrieve the specific shopping mall configuration using its unique business identifier code. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_configurations table and returns the configuration data that controls platform-wide settings such as payment gateway preferences, shipping method availability, currency options, and other customizable business parameters. The configuration is identified by its code field which contains human-readable identifiers like "payment-gateway-production" or "shipping-allowed-countries", ensuring URLs are user-friendly.

The configuration code must be a valid key from the shopping_mall_configurations table which contains predefined configuration entries. The endpoint ensures that only publicly readable configurations are returned and does not expose sensitive system secrets or admin-only configuration values. Security is maintained by ensuring that configuration access does not require authentication and is accessible to everyone, including guests, as these are public platform settings.

This operation is critical for frontend applications to dynamically configure interface elements based on platform-wide business rules, such as displaying accepted payment methods, enabled countries for shipping, or the appropriate currency symbol. It provides essential metadata to client applications without requiring authentication, enabling seamless user experiences across all user types.

Related operations: None require pre-execution, as this is a simple retrieval of static platform configuration data. This operation does not influence any other system functionality and is purely read-only.

Create a new system configuration entry for the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows authorized administrative users to add new configuration parameters that control platform-wide behavior, settings, and feature toggles. The configuration entity represents key parameters that affect the entire shopping mall ecosystem, including payment processing rules, shipping configurations, security settings, and system optimization parameters.

The operation validates that the provided configuration key is unique and not already in use by the system. It enforces that the value format matches the expected data type for the configuration key (string, number, boolean, or JSON object). The configuration is immediately active and takes effect across all platform services upon successful creation. System logs are automatically generated to track this configuration change for audit purposes.

Security considerations: This operation requires administrative authorization. Only users with admin privileges can create configuration entries. The configuration is stored in a secured, non-user-accessible data store and protected from unauthorized access.

This operation directly corresponds to the shopping_mall_configurations database table, which stores configuration parameters with key-value pairs and optional metadata. Related operations: Get system configuration (GET /configurations/{key}), Update system configuration (PUT /configurations/{key}), and List all configurations (GET /configurations).

The configuration value can be a string, number, boolean, or complex JSON structure, depending on the configuration key's defined purpose. The configuration keys must follow a dot-notated hierarchical naming convention (e.g., "payment.gateway.api.url") to support grouping and namespace isolation. This structured naming enables easy configuration management and prevents naming conflicts across different subsystems of the platform.

This operation allows only administrators to modify critical platform parameters such as payment gateway settings, shipping provider configurations, email template overrides, and system-wide feature flags.

The operation requires authentication with admin credentials and validates that the configuration code exists in the database before applying updates. The configuration update is atomic and transactional, ensuring data consistency even when updating multiple configuration properties. After successful update, the system immediately invalidates cached configuration values and broadcasts configuration change events to all relevant services.

No request body is needed for this operation as the configuration values are embedded directly in the request payload. The operation responds with the updated configuration object, reflecting all changes. This PATCH operation supports comprehensive search capabilities including full-text name matching, email domain filtering, account status (active/inactive), and date-range filters for creation or last login times. This operation queries the shopping_mall_customers table to return comprehensive customer data including personal information, registration details, authentication status, and customer-specific preferences.

The operation returns the complete customer profile as defined in the shopping_mall_customers database schema, including fields such as name, email, phone, address information, registration timestamp, and account status. Only verified and active customer accounts can be accessed through this endpoint.

If the attribute is assigned to any product variants that have stock greater than zero, the request will be rejected with a 409 Conflict error to prevent inventory inconsistencies. This constraint prevents situations where customers would see attribute options that no longer match their associated inventory levels. The attribute update is atomic and triggers immediate cache invalidation for product pages referencing this attribute to ensure display consistency.

Implementation note: The product identifier must reference a valid product from the shopping_mall_products table, and the attribute identifier must reference a valid attribute from the shopping_mall_product_attributes table. Both identifiers must be in UUID format as defined in the database schema. The request body must contain the complete updated attribute configuration object with all fields that require modification, and all required fields must be present in the update payload. This operation does not perform partial updates; the update payload must contain the complete revised attribute definition.

Related operations: To create new product attributes, use POST /products/{productId}/attributes. To retrieve a list of all attributes for a product, use GET /products/{productId}/attributes. To remove a product attribute, use DELETE /products/{productId}/attributes/{attributeId}.

Cache impact: Updating an attribute triggers cache invalidation for all products containing this attribute across all shops and channels, ensuring instant consistency in product display settings.

Security considerations: Only admin users can modify product attribute associations due to the critical nature of product catalog integrity. This ensures that only trusted personnel can alter product categorization and filtering parameters that affect the entire e-commerce platform. The operation enforces hard deletion of the association relationship without soft-delete mechanisms, as attribute associations are meant to be transient relationships rather than permanent records.

Implementation: This operation directly deletes the join record between product and attribute from the underlying database table structure. No cascading effects occur on the product or attribute entities themselves, preserving product details and attribute definitions for continued use with other products. The operation is idempotent - repeating the deletion request with the same IDs will result in a 404 error since the relationship is already gone.

operations.description:
Upload one or more images to associate with a specific product in the shopping mall platform. This operation creates new product image records linked to the specified product entity from the shopping_mall_products table. Each uploaded image is stored as a record in the shopping_mall_product_images table with a reference to the product ID, a unique identifier, and metadata about the image file.

This operation supports multiple image uploads in a single request and automatically assigns the images to the product with the matching productId path parameter. The system validates that the referenced product exists and that the requesting actor has appropriate permissions to modify the product images. Seller and admin actors can upload images for products they manage, while customers can upload images only for products they have purchased.

Each uploaded image must be a valid image file (JPEG, PNG, GIF) with a maximum size of 5MB. The system will generate unique file names and store the images in the designated cloud storage. The response contains the full metadata of all uploaded images, including their unique IDs, URLs, and ordering positions.

Security: Only authenticated users with appropriate roles can upload images. The system verifies product ownership and prevents unauthorized image uploads. The product_id parameter must match an existing product in the shopping_mall_products table.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/images to retrieve product images, PATCH /products/{productId}/images/{imageId} to update image order or alt text, DELETE /products/{productId}/images/{imageId} to remove an image.

Validation: The system checks for valid file types, file sizes, and existence of the target product. If the product does not exist, the operation returns a 404 error. File names that match prohibited patterns (such as executable files or scripts) are rejected.

Business logic: Images are assigned sequential ordering positions based on upload order. The first uploaded image becomes the primary image for the product. Products can have a maximum of 10 images.

Error handling: Invalid file types return 400 Bad Request. Files exceeding size limits return 413 Payload Too Large. If the product is not found or the user lacks permission, a 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found error is returned.

This endpoint does not return a response body, as the successful deletion is indicated by a 204 No Content status code. Clients should interpret a 204 response as confirmation that the question and its answers have been permanently removed. Any attempted deletion of a non-existent question will result in a 404 Not Found status code, while unauthorized access will return a 403 Forbidden response.

operations.description:
Retrieve all attribute definitions associated with product variants for a specific product. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_product_variants, shopping_mall_variant_attributes, and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values database tables.

The operation fetches all variant attributes defined for the product specified by productId. Each attribute represents a configurable characteristic (e.g., color, size, material) that variants can possess. The attributes are returned with their possible values and configuration details, allowing clients to dynamically generate product customization interfaces.

System behavior: This operation does not modify any data; it performs a read-only aggregation across four database entities. The productId must reference an existing product in shopping_mall_products. Attributes are derived from the relationship between shopping_mall_variant_attributes (defining available attribute types) and shopping_mall_product_attribute_values (defining the specific values that exist for this product).

Implementation detail: The operation executes a SQL JOIN across shopping_mall_product_variants to identify all variants for the target product, then joins shopping_mall_variant_attributes to retrieve the attribute definitions, and finally joins shopping_mall_product_attribute_values to retrieve the specific values associated with these attributes for this product. Only attributes that have at least one value defined for variants of this product are included in the response.

Security considerations: Access requires authentication. Only customers and sellers who have product view permissions can access attribute information. Admins have full access. The operation filters out attributes that would expose sensitive data not intended for customers.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} retrieves basic product information including variant count. PATCH /products/{productId}/variants retrieves the full list of product variants with their specific attribute values. POST /products/{productId}/variants creates new product variants with specified attributes.

responseBody.description: List of all product variant attribute definitions and their available values for the specified product. Each attribute definition includes its name, system identifier, and a collection of values that are currently available for variants of this product.
