operations.description:
Create a new product variant for the specified product in the shoppingMall platform. This operation allows sellers to add new product variants (such as different sizes, colors, or configurations) to an existing product listing. Each variant is uniquely identified by a generated SKU and maintains its own inventory, pricing, and attribute values independent of the base product.

The operation strictly adheres to the shopping_mall_product_variants database schema and requires the product to exist in the shopping_mall_products table. The product identifier is provided via the {productId} path parameter, which must correspond to a valid product in the shopping_mall_products table. When creating a variant, sellers must specify the variant attributes (size, color, etc.) that differentiate this variant from other variants of the same product, and provide unique pricing and inventory quantities. The system automatically generates a unique SKU based on the product's base SKU and the selected attribute values.

This API operation does not allow creation of variants with duplicate attribute combinations for the same product. The system enforces this constraint at the database level through a composite unique constraint on (product_id, attribute_values) in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. The operation validates that the specified variant attributes exist in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes table and that the attribute values provided are valid options from the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table.

Successive attempts to create variants with identical attribute combinations will be rejected with a 409 Conflict error. The variant creation process maintains data integrity by linking the variant to the correct product through foreign key relationships and automatically updates the product's variant count counter in the shopping_mall_products table.

Security: Only authenticated sellers can create product variants. The seller authorization is verified through the JWT token, and the product must belong to the seller's catalog (verified through the shopping_mall_products table linking the product to the seller).

Related operations: GET /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants (to list all variants of a product), PATCH /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} (to update variant details), DELETE /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} (to remove a variant).

The attributes field must be an object mapping attribute names (from shopping_mall_variant_attributes) to attribute value IDs (from shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values) to ensure compliance with the composite unique constraint on (product_id, attribute_values). Example: {"size": "7b8a3c4d", "color": "9e2f5a1b"}. Also include standard fields: price (numeric), and quantity (integer).

responseBody.description: The newly created product variant with assigned unique SKU and system-generated metadata. Includes the variant's ID, product_id, attribute_values mapping, price, quantity, SKU, created_at, and updated_at timestamp.

Update a specific product variant with precise inventory, pricing, and attribute configurations.

This operation allows authorized sellers to modify the pricing and inventory for individual product variants using their unique SKU identifier. Variants represent configurable options of a product such as color, size, or material combinations, and each variant has its own distinct inventory count and price.

The variant ID used in the path must correspond exactly to the unique SKU generated for that specific attribute combination. This ensures that updates are applied to the exact variant intended by the seller, preventing pricing or inventory mismatches that could lead to incorrect customer charges or stock inaccuracies.

Product variants are managed independently from the main product, enabling sellers to offer different pricing for different sizes or colors of the same product. This operation validates that the variant exists, belongs to the authenticated seller's product catalog, and has not been archived or discontinued.

Security measures include verifying that the authenticated user has seller privileges and owns the product containing the variant. The variant's SKU must be properly formed for the product and cannot be modified through this endpoint—the SKU serves as an immutable identifier.

The system records an audit trail of the modification, and real-time inventory changes trigger notifications to customers when a product moves from 'out of stock' to 'available.' This ensures accurate product visibility on storefronts.

Related operations: Get variant details (GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}), Create new variant (POST /products/{productId}/variants), List all variants (GET /products/{productId}/variants).

Security: Only admin users are permitted to perform variant deletion. This prevents unauthorized removal of product variations that could disrupt inventory management, sales reporting, and customer order history. The operation validates that the target product and variant exist in the database before processing, returning a 404 error if either cannot be found.

This deletion removes only the product variant record itself from the shopping_mall_product_variants table. Associated inventory records in shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory, pricing records in shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, and attribute associations in product_variant_attributes are not automatically deleted by this operation. The vote record contains information about the voting user, the target review, and the vote value (helpful/unhelpful) cast by the user. This operation supports retrieving vote data for display purposes in the product review UI, helping to surface the most valuable customer feedback through community voting.

Security and authorization: This operation is available to all authenticated users, including customers who voted on the review as well as non-voting users who wish to see the voting status. The vote is read-only and cannot be modified through this endpoint, as the voting system only allows a single vote per user per review.

Implementation details: The operation performs a direct lookup in the shopping_mall_review_votes table using the voteId path parameter. The vote record is associated with a specific review (shopping_mall_product_reviews) and customer (shopping_mall_customers) through foreign keys. The response includes only the vote value and timestamp, as no additional context is required for displaying the vote status.

Related operations: This operation typically follows a GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId} call, which retrieves the target review and its vote count. This operation provides granular, user-specific vote information.

The operation operates on the shopping_mall_review_votes table, which records individual votes on product reviews. Each vote is associated with a specific review ID, product ID, and user ID. The vote status is stored as an integer (1 for upvote, -1 for downvote, 0 for no vote). The user cannot vote on a review they did not create.

Security considerations include checking that the authenticated user is the original voter and preventing duplicate votes from the same user on the same review. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse. Historical vote changes are logged in the shopping_mall_review_votes table for accountability.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}/votes to retrieve the current vote count and status for a specific review, and POST /products/{productId}/reviews/{reviewId}/votes to create a new vote if none exists. This PUT operation only modifies an existing vote with the same user ID.

When a vote is updated, the associated review's overall rating is recalculated and cached in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table to maintain performance.

The system validates ownership using the JWT authentication token, ensuring users cannot delete votes they did not create. Any attempt by another user to delete a vote will result in a 403 Forbidden response.

This operation is idempotent - attempting to delete an already-deleted vote will result in a 404 Not Found response. The system fully supports atomic transaction processing for this operation to ensure data consistency between the vote deletion and review vote count update.

Update a specific answer to a product question on the shopping mall platform. This operation performs a PUT update on the shopping_mall_product_answers table, allowing the original answer author (a customer) to modify their own response to a product question.

The operation requires the customer to be authenticated and the answer must belong to that customer's profile. The system ensures data integrity by preventing unauthorized edits to other users' answers. Customers may only update their own answers and only before any seller response has been added to the question.

Security: The operation validates that the authenticated customer is the original author of the answer. The customer_id is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and matched against the answer's creator_id in the database.

Business rule: Customers can update their answers up to 3 times within 7 days of initial posting. After 7 days, updates are locked. If a seller has already replied to the question, no further customer updates are allowed.

The answer's updated_at timestamp is automatically incremented, and an audit trail entry is created in the shopping_mall_product_answers table to maintain historical records. The answer content must be between 5 and 2000 characters.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/questions/{questionId}/answers (to view answers), POST /products/{productId}/questions/{questionId}/answers (to create new answers).

The product answer deletion is irreversible and cannot be undone. This operation requires the full path context of the product, question, and answer identifiers to precisely locate the target record. Answer deletion occurs immediately without confirmation or recovery options.

Security: This operation is restricted to administrative actors only, as answer deletion represents a moderation action that could impact user content integrity. The system does not allow customer or seller actors to delete answers, maintaining content integrity and preventing abuse.

Business Logic: Answer deletion is used exclusively for content moderation purposes, such as removing inappropriate, fraudulent, or policy-violating answers. The system does not permit answer deletion for any other purpose, including customer dissatisfaction, answer correction, or content revision.

Audit Implications: All answer deletions are automatically recorded in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table, capturing the actor identity, timestamp, and associated answer ID for compliance and forensic analysis. This ensures a complete audit trail of all content moderation actions.

This operation allows authorized system administrators to register new product brands that will be available for sellers to associate with their product listings. Each brand must have a unique name and optional description, logo URL, and category alignment.

The brand entity is used to group related products under a single manufacturer or vendor identity, enhancing customer recognition and filtering capabilities. When a new brand is created, it becomes immediately available in the brand selection interface for sellers during product creation and editing workflows.

The system enforces unique brand names at the database level to prevent duplication. Brand names must not be empty and should follow standard business naming conventions. The brand logo URL, if provided, must point to a valid web-accessible image URL.

This operation is restricted to administrative users only, as brand creation is a sensitive maintenance function that affects the entire product catalog. The brand information will be displayed in customer-facing product listings and search filters. Related operations: Retrieve brand list (GET /brands), Update brand (PUT /brands/{brandCode}), Delete brand (DELETE /brands/{brandCode}).

operations.description:
Update an existing product brand in the shopping mall platform. This operation modifies the name, description, logo URL, and other metadata of a brand entity stored in the shopping_mall_product_brands database table. The brand identifier is provided via the path parameter {brandId}, which references a unique brand record. This operation supports full updates and requires all fields to be specified for consistency.

This operation requires that the user making the request is authenticated and possesses the appropriate permissions: either the request originates from the brand's own seller account (ownership verification), or the requester is a platform administrator with elevated privileges. The system performs ownership validation by matching the authenticated seller's ID against the brand's owner field before allowing modifications.

Implementation details: The endpoint accepts a payload where all fields must be provided for a complete update. Omitted fields will be treated as null and may result in data loss. This behavior aligns with PUT semantics for full resource replacement. The system automatically updates the last_modified_at timestamp to reflect the time of any successful modification. The brand's uniqueness constraint ensures that the provided name cannot conflict with other existing brand names, and duplicate names will result in a 409 Conflict response. Any attempts to modify a brand that has been flagged as archived or disabled will be rejected with a 403 Forbidden response.

Related operations: To create a new brand, use POST /shopping-mall-brands. To list all brands, use PATCH /shopping-mall-brands. To retrieve a specific brand by ID, use GET /shopping-mall-brands/{brandId}. To permanently delete a brand record, use DELETE /shopping-mall-brands/{brandId} which permanently removes it from the database.

Delete a product brand record from the shopping mall system. This operation permanently removes the brand entity from the database and affects all associated products, which will have their brand references cleared. The brand identification is based on the brandId path parameter, which corresponds to the brandId field in the shopping_mall_product_brands table. This is a hard delete operation that cannot be undone, with no soft-delete column configured in the schema. The operation requires admin-level authorization to prevent unauthorized deletion of brand entities that could impact product catalogs and customer purchasing decisions.

Product brands serve as critical identifiers for product categorization, customer trust, and marketing campaigns within the shopping mall ecosystem. Deleting a brand affects all products associated with it, causing those products to become unbranded and potentially impacting search, filtering, and customer expectations.

Given the business context of a shopping mall system, brand deletion should be strictly limited to administrators with full system control. This prevents accidental loss of valuable brand identities that may be associated with significant inventory, customer loyalty, and marketing investments. All brand-related products continue to exist in the system but have their brand field cleared to NULL, preserving historical data integrity while removing the brand identity.

The deletion operation is accompanied by the system automatically clearing the brandId reference in all related products to maintain referential integrity. This ensures no orphaned references remain in the product catalog. The system does not maintain audit logs of brand deletions through this endpoint since brand deletion is considered a rare administrative action, with broader administrative audit logs handling system-wide change tracking.

operations.description:
Retrieve all variants of a specific product identified by productId. This endpoint operates on the shopping_mall_product_variants table and returns a list of all variants associated with the given product. Each variant represents a distinct combination of attributes such as size, color, material, and other customizable features that a product may offer, with each variant having its own inventory, pricing, and availability status.

This operation is crucial for product detail pages where customers need to see all available configurations of a product before making a purchase. The system retrieves all variants from the shopping_mall_product_variants table and joins with related tables including shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory, shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes, and shopping_mall_products to provide comprehensive variant information. The response includes variant identifiers, attribute values, pricing information, inventory levels, and availability status for each variant.

Product variants allow customers to select specific configurations while maintaining a single product listing. Each variant is uniquely identified by a SKU (stock keeping unit), and inventory is tracked independently for each variant. The system applies business rules to determine variant availability based on inventory thresholds and product visibility settings. In cases where a variant has zero inventory but is still offered for sale (pre-order or backorder), it will be marked with appropriate availability status. Variants are returned sorted by attribute priority and value order as defined in the product configuration.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} which returns the base product information without variants, and PATCH /products/{productId}/variants which allows for bulk update of variant inventory and pricing.

Note: This operation is designed as a PATCH method because it uses a complex query structure with filtering, though it returns data. This is a design choice to allow future extension with search parameters while maintaining consistent pattern usage across the API.

The system logs all access to product questions and their answers for audit purposes, and rate limiting applies to prevent abuse by automated scripts. Users may flag inappropriate answers for moderator review, and these flagged responses are excluded from results until reviewed and approved.

This operation provides comprehensive sales analytics for the specified product, including total units sold, revenue generated, average sale price, sales volume trends over time, and customer purchase patterns.

The system aggregates sales data from the shopping_mall_order_items and shopping_mall_products tables to compute these statistics. The operation filters results by the specified productId and returns aggregated metrics across all completed orders.

Security considerations include restricting access to authenticated users and ensuring data privacy protections for sensitive sales metrics. This operation is designed to be called by sellers to understand product performance, by marketplace administrators for analytics purposes, and by internal finance teams for revenue reconciliation.

The response includes both summary statistics and historical trends, enabling users to identify patterns such as seasonal buying behavior, product popularity shifts, and pricing effectiveness. The implementation leverages computed aggregations from the underlying sales data rather than reading from a precomputed statistics table, ensuring data accuracy and real-time relevance.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive sales statistics for the specified product including aggregated sales metrics and performance trends.

operations.description:
Retrieve product snapshot history for the specified product. This operation queries the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table to return historical versions of product metadata including pricing, inventory, name, description, and category changes. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time record of the product's state when a significant change occurred, such as price adjustments, inventory updates, or attribute modifications.

The operation provides a pagination-compliant interface with comprehensive filtering, enabling users to analyze product evolution over time. Snapshot data is optimized for performance and includes timestamps, actor information, and change descriptions to support advanced analytics and audit requirements. This endpoint serves critical business needs for product history review, compliance auditing, and change impact analysis.

Security: Access to product snapshots requires the user to be an admin or to have explicit permission to view product details. Non-admin users can only access snapshots for products they own or manage. The request may specify start and end dates to limit the date range of snapshot records returned.

Implementation note: This operation does not map to any single entity's primary data; it serves as a read-only audit trail derived from real-time changes to the shopping_mall_products table. The system automatically creates snapshot records whenever product fields are modified via the IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate request.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} (current product details), PUT /products/{productId} (update product and trigger new snapshot).

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target product. This must be a UUID format string representing a valid product in the shopping_mall_products table.

requestBody.description: Search and filtering criteria for product snapshot records including date ranges, change types, and pagination parameters.

responseBody.description: Paginated response containing historical product snapshots with metadata including change dates, affected fields, actor information, and product state at each point in time.

operations.description:
Retrieve a detailed historical snapshot of a product at a specific point in time. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table to return a complete snapshot of product details, including pricing, inventory, attributes, and metadata as they existed at the time the snapshot was created.

The snapshot provides an immutable historical record that captures the exact state of the product when it was saved, which is critical for compliance, audit trails, and customer transparency in cases of price changes, inventory adjustments, or product specification updates. The operation ensures data integrity by returning data exactly as stored in the snapshot table, without modifying or interpolating any values from the current product state.

Examples of use cases include: displaying to customers the product details at time of purchase, generating compliance reports showing historical product configurations, and supporting dispute resolution with historical product specifications. The snapshot includes all product information available at creation time, such as the base product name, vendor, category, pricing, and all attribute values.

This operation does not return the current product information but instead returns the frozen state from when the snapshot was created. The returned data is completely independent of any subsequent changes to the product model or product_variants. The snapshot must be accessed via its unique snapshotId, which is the primary identifier for the historical record.

This operation exclusively reads from the shopping_mall_product_snapshots table and requires no write access. No operations modify snapshot data after creation - snapshots are immutable records. related operations: GET /products/{productId} (retrieves current product state), PATCH /products (updates current product state).

Verified brands receive enhanced visibility in search results and catalog listings. The returned attribute contains all metadata required to manage and configure product variants, such as whether it's mandatory, its display order, and validation rules. This endpoint is essential for product configuration workflows where users need to inspect or update individual attribute definitions.

Security: Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative roles. The operation does not require any request body as the identifier is passed through the path parameter. The response includes the complete attribute record with all fields as defined in the shopping_mall_variant_attributes database schema.

This operation adds a definable attribute type that can be used to specify characteristics of product variants such as color, size, material, or other customizable features. The attribute is stored in the shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes table and becomes available for selection when creating or managing product variants.

This operation requires administrative privileges because variant attributes fundamentally change product catalog structure and affect inventory management across all products using these attributes. System administrators must review and approve new attributes to ensure consistency in naming conventions, avoid duplication, and maintain data integrity across the entire product catalog.

The operation validates that the attribute name is unique and follows system naming conventions. The description must clearly differentiate the attribute from existing ones. The attribute type (string, number, boolean, etc.) determines how values will be collected and displayed in the product interface. All variant attributes are global across the platform and apply to all sellers.

Related operations: GET /product-variants/attributes (retrieve list of all attributes), PUT /product-variants/attributes/{attributeId} (update an existing attribute), DELETE /product-variants/attributes/{attributeId} (deactivate an attribute).

The attribute is identified by its unique ID and can be updated to modify its name, display label, input type, validation rules, and associated meta-information. This capability is critical for managing product catalogs where variant attributes (e.g., size, color, material) serve as key differentiators for customers. Changes to attributes immediately affect how products are presented and filtered in the storefront.

Security considerations require that only users with administrative privileges can modify variant attributes, as changes could impact product discoverability and catalog consistency across the entire platform. The operation validates that the target attribute exists and that the updated configuration maintains data integrity (e.g., unique attribute names, valid input types). 

This operation supports real-time catalog updates without requiring full product re-indexing.

Related operations: List attributes (GET /product-variants/attributes), View attribute details (GET /product-variants/attributes/{attributeId}), Create new attribute (POST /product-variants/attributes), Delete attribute (DELETE /product-variants/attributes/{attributeId}).

Support for multiple filter conditions enables efficient product administration and attribute management. Results are returned in paginated format with configurable page size and sorting options to handle large datasets efficiently.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of attribute data based on requester access levels. Only authenticated users with access to product variant management can retrieve attribute values. Audit logging records all search queries for compliance and security purposes. The operation returns the full attribute value details including the value text, associated attribute type name, and metadata about when this value was created and last updated. This information is critical for UI components that display variant options to customers, allowing them to see exactly what option they are selecting.

Security considerations: The attribute value is not considered sensitive data. Access to this information does not require authentication because product variant attributes are public product information available to all customers, including guests. This design aligns with the principle that product catalog data should be freely accessible to support customer purchasing decisions.

This operation supports the product variant selection workflow where customers browse products and select specific attribute combinations. It is used by frontend applications to populate dropdown menus, color swatches, size selectors, or other UI elements that present product variant options.

Related operations: GET /product-variants/{variantId} to get the parent variant, PATCH /product-variants to search multiple variants, and GET /product-variants/attributes to list available attribute types. This operation allows administrators to define specific attribute values (e.g., sizes, colors, materials) that can be assigned to product variants. The system enforces strict validation to ensure attribute values are correctly associated with existing attribute types and maintain data integrity across the product catalog.

This operation operates on the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table, which serves as the junction between variant attributes and their specific values. Each variant attribute value is assigned to a specific variant attribute type (e.g., "Color" or "Size") and may have optional metadata including display order, color codes, and usage guidelines.

Security and authorization are strictly enforced - only admin actors have permission to create new variant attribute values due to the critical impact on product categorization, filtering, and search functionality. The system requires that the referenced attribute type exists and is active before allowing creation.

Business rules include: attribute values must be unique within their attribute type, cannot be empty, must not exceed 50 characters, and must follow consistent naming conventions. The system automatically creates audit logs for all variant attribute value creations by admin actors.

Associated operations: GET /product-variants/attribute-values (index) to list existing values, GET /product-variants/attributes (index) to view available attribute types for assignment.

This operation will be used during product catalog management workflows when new product variants require new attribute values that weren't pre-defined in the system.

The operation operates on the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table, which stores specific attribute values for product variants.

This endpoint requires administrative authorization because variant attribute values are core configuration values that affect product display and filtering. Only system administrators can modify these values to ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized changes to product attributes. Changes to attribute values can impact product search, filtering, and display across the platform.

The attribute value must correspond to a valid attribute type defined in the system. The update operation modifies the value field and associated metadata without affecting the underlying attribute definition itself. Any changes made through this endpoint will be immediately reflected in product listings where this attribute value is used.

This operation is atomic and does not trigger cascading updates to related records. Product variants using this attribute value will continue to reference the updated value without requiring additional modifications.

Related operations: GET /product-variants/attribute-values to list all available attribute values, POST /product-variants/attribute-values to create new attribute values, DELETE /product-variants/attribute-values/{valueId} to remove attribute values.

This operation deletes the exact variant attribute value record identified by its unique ID from the shopping_mall_variant_attribute_values table. No confirmation or soft-delete mechanism is employed - the record is immediately and completely removed from the database with no possibility of recovery.

This operation is intended for administrative cleanup of obsolete, erroneous, or unused attribute values that are no longer referenced by any product variant. Before executing this operation, ensure that no active product variants still reference this attribute value by checking the shopping_mall_product_variants table, which maintains foreign key references to this table through the variant_attribute_value_id field.

Security: Only admins may delete attribute values. The system requires a minimum of one admin account to exist, so deletion should be reserved for truly obsolete values. When an attribute value is deleted, any product variants that previously referenced it lose their attribute association and may display as having undefined attributes in the UI.

Related operations: GET /product-variants/attribute-values to view all attribute values, POST /product-variants/attribute-values to create new attribute values, PUT /product-variants/attribute-values/{valueId} to update attribute values.

operations.description:
Create a new product listing in the shopping mall marketplace. This operation allows authenticated sellers to create new product listings by providing detailed information including title, description, category, pricing, and inventory details. The product is created in the shopping_mall_products table with an initial status of 'draft', which requires subsequent activation to become visible to customers.

Security considerations include identity verification of sellers through JWT authentication, mandatory validation of required fields, and adherence to product content policies. The seller's identity is automatically extracted from the authentication token and associated with the product creation. This prevents unauthorized users from creating products and ensures proper attribution for inventory and sales tracking.

Business rules require that all products have a unique SKU, a minimum product title length of 5 characters, and pricing that must be greater than zero. Category association is mandatory and must reference an existing category in the shopping_mall_categories table. Products cannot be created without at least one image reference.

This operation interacts with the shopping_mall_products table and triggers the creation of a corresponding entry in the shopping_mall_product_images table. Related operations include listing products (PATCH /products), viewing product details (GET /products/{productId}), and updating product information (PUT /products/{productId}).

requestBody.description: Complete product information required for creation, including all mandatory fields for product listing.

responseBody.description: The newly created product record with full details, including generated ID and creation timestamp.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific product variant by its unique SKU identifier. This operation queries the shopping_mall_variant_skus table and returns comprehensive product variant data including pricing, inventory status, and associated attribute values. The SKU serves as the primary identifier for product variants in the system, allowing precise access to specific product configurations.

The operation validates the SKU format and checks for existence in the system. If the SKU is valid and corresponds to an active product variant, the detailed variant information is returned. This includes the base product information, specific variant attributes (such as size, color, etc.), current inventory levels, and pricing details. The system ensures that only active and available variants are returned, excluding those that are discontinued or have zero inventory.

Security considerations include ensuring that SKU access does not leak information about products the requesting user might not be authorized to view. The system enforces product visibility rules based on category permissions and seller relationships. Unauthorized attempts to access SKUs will return a 404 Not Found response to prevent enumeration attacks on the product catalog.

parameters.description: Unique product variant identifier (SKU). This is a system-generated alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies a specific product configuration. The SKU follows the format PRDSKU-XXXXXXXX, where XXXXXXXX is a unique alphanumeric identifier. This fixed-length format ensures reliable pattern matching and indexing in the database.

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the requested product variant including pricing, inventory status, and attribute values. This response contains the full product variant object with all associated metadata including product name, final price, current stock quantity, and variant-specific attributes.

operations.description:
Create a new product variant SKU (stock keeping unit) for a product in the shoppingMall platform. This operation creates a unique identifier that represents a specific combination of product attributes such as size, color, material, or other variant options. The SKU is essential for inventory tracking, order fulfillment, and pricing management.

The operation requires that the product variant already exists in the system with defined attributes, and that pricing and inventory levels are specified. The system validates that the requested attribute combination does not create a duplicate SKU, and that the creator has appropriate permissions (seller or admin). Upon successful creation, the system generates a unique SKU code following the platform's encoding rules and initializes the inventory to zero.

Security considerations: Only sellers of the product and platform admins can create SKUs. The operation enforces that the SKU is tied to a product that the seller owns or manages. Rate limiting applies to prevent bulk SKU creation attacks.

This operation interacts with three primary database tables: shopping_mall_product_variants (which stores variant definitions), shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing (which manages variant-specific pricing), and shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory (which tracks inventory levels). The SKU creation triggers an initial zero-inventory record in the inventory table.

Related operations: PATCH /products/skus (search SKUs), GET /products/skus/{skuCode} (retrieve SKU details), PUT /products/skus/{skuCode} (update pricing/inventory), DELETE /products/skus/{skuCode} (deactivate SKU).

Only authorized users associated with the product's seller account can modify variant information, with access controls enforced through the authorization system. The system validates that the SKU exists before processing the update and returns the updated variant information upon successful completion.

The update may trigger inventory system events, including stock level adjustments and availability status changes (green/yellow/red/gray) displayed to customers on product pages. If the inventory count reaches zero, the variant's availability status transitions to 'out of stock'. If the price is updated, the change is reflected in product listings and shopping carts.

This update operation should be invoked when the seller needs to adjust pricing due to market conditions, update inventory levels after receiving stock shipments, or correct pricing/inventory errors in the system. This operation returns the current pricing information for a product including base price, variant pricing, and discount structures. The pricing data is stored in a dedicated schema that manages pricing tiers, currency conversions, and promotional discounts.

The pricing information for each product is maintained separately from the product's core metadata to support flexible pricing strategies. This enables different pricing models such as bulk pricing, seasonal discounts, membership tiers, and regional pricing variations without modifying the core product record.

The endpoint uses the product ID as a path parameter to uniquely identify the target product. The system retrieves the pricing record associated with the product based on the product ID. In the existing database schema, the shopping_mall_products table contains the product_id field that corresponds to the unique identifier used in this endpoint path.

This operation returns a structured pricing object that includes the base price, any active discounts, currency context, and pricing variants associated with the product. The product may have multiple variants each with their own pricing rules, which are referenced through the shopping_mall_product_variants and shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing tables. These relationships are referenced within the product's pricing context.

The pricing logic ensures accurate price calculations including tax implications, currency conversions for international customers, and promotional code application. Since pricing is often sensitive data, all users with product access can view pricing information. The endpoint does not require authentication since pricing information is public by nature and does not involve private user data.

This operation is primarily used by customers during product browsing to understand purchase costs, by checkout systems to validate total amounts before payment processing, and by analytics systems to track pricing patterns and discount effectiveness.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} retrieves product metadata including name, description, and availability, while GET /products/{productId}/variants retrieves the available product variants with their individual pricing and availability status.

The pricing information may differ from the base product price due to variant-specific pricing overrides, bulk discounts, seasonal promotions, or regional pricing strategies configured for different market segments.

This operation is primarily used by the product detail page UI to display the exact price for a customer-selected product variant. It is also referenced by the shopping cart and checkout processes to ensure price accuracy at the time of purchase. The pricing data is immutable at the time of pricing record generation and does not reflect real-time changes to pricing rules or inventory status.

The operation requires the productId parameter to validate that the pricing record belongs to the requested product, and the pricingId parameter to identify the specific variant pricing. A combination of both parameters ensures the operation returns the correct pricing context even when multiple pricing records exist for the same product across different variants or time periods.

operations.description:
Create compatibility relationships between products in the shopping mall platform. This operation enables sellers to define which product variants are compatible with a specified product, enhancing customer experience by suggesting complementary items for purchase.

The operation allows sellers to establish bidirectional compatibility relationships between product variants, with each compatibility entry referencing a source product and a target product. This functionality supports features like "Customers who bought this also bought" recommendations and cross-selling suggestions during checkout.

The compatibility relationship is stored in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table, which maintains references to product variants (not products) and captures metadata about the compatibility type (e.g., "complementary", "substitute", "bundle"). Each compatibility record is associated with a specific source product variant and a target product variant, enabling precise matching based on SKU-level details rather than product-level aggregations.

The system ensures data integrity through referential constraints: both source and target product variants must exist in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. The compatibility relationship is symmetric; if product A is compatible with product B, then product B is also compatible with product A, creating a bidirectional relationship that enhances recommendation accuracy.

Security and Authorization: Only authenticated sellers who own the source product can create compatibility relationships. This prevents unauthorized sellers from associating products with a rival's inventory. The operation validates that the source productId corresponds to a product owned by the authenticated seller and that the target product variants exist in the catalog.

Implementation Notes: The endpoint accepts a list of compatible variant IDs in the request body. For each variant ID, the system checks if the target variant exists and is not already registered as compatible with the source product. The system then creates a bidirectional relationship entry in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table, linking the source product variant to the target product variant. The compatibility type defaults to "complementary" unless specified otherwise in a future enhancement.

Related Operations: This operation complements GET /products/{productId}/compatibilities (list), which retrieves all compatibility relationships for a given product.

responseBody.description: Response containing the newly created compatibility relationships, including the source product variant ID and the target product variant ID for each newly established relationship.

The compatibility relationship is stored in the shopping_mall_variant_compatibility table, which tracks bidirectional product compatibility relationships. Since the database schema for shopping_mall_variant_compatibility contains no soft-delete fields (such as deleted_at, is_deleted, or archived), this operation performs a hard delete, permanently removing the association between the source product (identified by productId) and the compatible product (identified by compatibilityId). This deletion is irreversible and cannot be undone.

Security considerations include ensuring that only authenticated users with appropriate permissions can modify product compatibility relationships. The system automatically enforces data integrity, preventing orphaned records and maintaining referential consistency. No request body is needed as the relationship is uniquely identified by the path parameters.

This operation is typically used when a product is retired, its compatibility status changes, or an erroneous compatibility relationship needs to be corrected. After deletion, the product will no longer appear in the compatible products list of the source product, and the source product will no longer appear in the compatible products list of the target product.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/compatibilities (list all compatibilities), POST /products/{productId}/compatibilities (create new compatibility).

Create a new product template configuration for a specific product in the shopping mall system. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_variant_templates table and allows administrators to define standardized product variant configurations that can be applied to multiple products, ensuring consistency across product catalogs.

A product template defines a set of mandatory and optional variant attributes (such as size, color, material, etc.) that can be applied to products. When a new product is created, sellers can select an existing template to automatically populate the variant configuration, reducing manual input and minimizing errors. The template specifies which attributes are required, which are optional, default values for each attribute, and any compatibility rules between attributes.

Security: Only users with administrative privileges can create product templates. The operation validates that the referenced product exists and that the template configuration does not create incompatible attribute combinations. Template names must be unique across the system to prevent conflicts.

operations.description:
Update a specific product variant template for a given product in the shopping mall system. 

This operation allows administrators and sellers to modify the attribute structure and configuration of a product variant template associated with a specific product. The template defines the set of product attributes (e.g., size, color, material) that variants of this product can have, along with their permitted values and default behavior.

The operation validates that the template being updated belongs to the specified product, enforces consistency with existing product variants, and maintains catalog integrity. Any attributes added to the template will become available for new variants, while removed attributes will be deprecated but preserved for existing variants to maintain historical data integrity.

Security: Only authenticated sellers or admins (authorizationActors: ["admin", "seller"]) can update templates for products they own. The identity of the actor is extracted from the JWT token, and the product owner relationship is validated against the seller_id linked to the product record. Rate limiting applies to prevent template spamming. The operation triggers automatic inventory recalculations for variants affected by the change.

Implementation logic: The system first verifies that the product_id exists and optionally checks that the requester has ownership access. Then it validates the new template structure against the product's current variants to ensure no conflicts arise (e.g., removing an attribute that existing variants still use). The system then updates the template definition and propagates changes to any connected product variant records using the modified template. Historical template versions are maintained for audit purposes. Related operations: GET /products/{productId}/templates to retrieve templates, POST /products/{productId}/templates to create new templates, DELETE /products/{productId}/templates/{templateId} to remove templates.

Availability status reflects real-time stock conditions including available quantity, pre-order capacity, and backorder status. The availability information is updated continuously through inventory management processes triggered by order fulfillment and restocking activities.

Security and access controls ensure that only authenticated users can access availability data, preventing unauthorized scraping or denial-of-service attacks on inventory systems. The operation supports detailed filtering by variant-specific criteria and provides consolidated availability information across all variants of the specified product.

This operation is critical for customer purchase decisions and is used extensively in product pages, shopping cart logic, and checkout workflows to provide accurate stock information before order processing. The availability data is never cached in a way that would create stock discrepancies between what is shown to customers and the actual inventory status.

This operation integrates with inventory management systems to provide up-to-date stock levels across all warehouse locations and fulfillment centers. The availability status reflects the unified inventory view computed from all sources including primary stock, backorder capacity, and supplier lead times.

All cart item quantities are validated against current inventory levels in shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory. If any variant is out of stock or insufficient in quantity, the operation fails with a specific HTTP 409 conflict status. The system does not allow negative quantities or zero-quantity items to be persisted in the cart.

This operation may trigger real-time inventory adjustments in the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table, where inventory counts are temporarily reserved based on the updated cart quantities. These reservations are released if the cart is later abandoned or the order isn't completed.

Important: This operation does not create new carts. New cart creation requires POST /carts. This PUT operation only updates existing carts identified by their cartId.

The creation of wishlist items does not affect inventory or pricing as these are purely observational entries for customer use.

To prevent duplication, the system prevents adding the same product variant to the same wishlist more than once. Customers can later remove items from their wishlists using the erase operation on the same path with the DELETE method.

This business function supports customer decision-making by providing a persistent, organized way to track potential purchases without requiring immediate commitment. Customers can revisit their wishlists later when making purchasing decisions, potentially cross-referencing with reviews, price history, or inventory status. This improves customer retention by creating a continuous engagement channel between the user and the platform.

operations.description:
Retrieve or update the current shopping cart session for an authenticated user. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table from the database schema and represents the active shopping cart state for the current user. The cart session stores the relationship between a user and their selected products, including quantities and timestamps.

The operation supports retrieving the current cart state for the authenticated user, as well as updating the cart through the request body. This is typically used to initialize a shopping experience for a logged-in user, and to modify their cart contents.

The cart session is preserved across device sessions and browser refreshes when associated with an authenticated user account. Product variants are stored with their specific pricing and inventory state at the time of addition to ensure accurate pricing and availability information during checkout.

Security considerations include ensuring that users can only access and modify their own cart sessions. Authentication is required for this operation to associate the cart session with the correct user account. This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table as defined in the database schema, incorporating the cart_session_id and user_id relationship to ensure proper cart ownership.

Retrieve the active shopping cart session for the authenticated user.

This operation fetches the shopping cart session identified by the sessionId path parameter from the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table. The session is associated with the authenticated user through JWT token authentication. The result includes the session's cart items, creation timestamp, and last updated time.

The sessionId parameter must correspond to a valid cart session that belongs to the authenticated user. Unauthorized access attempts to sessions belonging to other users are blocked by the authorization layer.

This operation supports cart persistence across sessions and device switching. It is commonly called after user authentication to restore the user's cart state. The cart session may include items from previous visits and serves as the basis for order placement.

Related operations: POST /cart-sessions (create session), PUT /cart-sessions/{sessionId} (update session), DELETE /cart-sessions/{sessionId} (clear session).

operations.description:
Create a new shopping cart session for a customer to begin accumulating products for purchase. This operation initializes a cart record in the shopping_mall_cart_sessions table, which serves as the container for all items a user intends to purchase.

Authenticated customers (users with an active login session) will have their new cart recorded with their customer_id linked to the shopping_mall_customers table. Any previous guest cart will automatically be merged into this new authenticated cart if one exists. The system will preserve the cart state even if the user logs out, allowing for continuation of shopping in a future session.

Guest users (unauthenticated visitors) are assigned a temporary cart session with a unique anonymous cart identifier stored in browser localStorage. This cart persists across page refreshes and browser sessions until the user either logs in (triggering merge with authenticated cart) or exceeds the 30-day inactivity period, at which point the session expires and the cart is deleted.

The cart session does not store individual cart items — these are managed by the shopping_mall_cart_items table and referenced via cart_session_id. This operation only creates the cart container. Items must be added via POST /cart-items endpoint.

The cart session is considered active until explicitly cleared by the user, expired by inactivity (30 days), or merged with an authenticated user account upon login. This ensures uninterrupted shopping experience across devices and sessions, aligning with business requirement: "THE system SHALL persist cart data to database with customer identifier."

requestBody.description: Initial configuration and metadata for creating a new shopping cart session.

responseBody.description: The complete cart session record created by the system, including session identifier and timestamps.

Update the shopping cart items and quantities associated with the session, maintaining the session state.

This operation modifies the shopping_mall_cart_items table, which stores individual product variants and their quantities within a shopping cart session. The cart session (shopping_mall_cart_sessions) acts as a state container identifying the customer and session state, but the actual cart contents are managed through the cart_items subsidiary table.

The system validates that the session exists and belongs to the authenticated customer before updating cart items. If cart items are added, removed, or modified, the system performs real-time inventory validation against shopping_mall_variant_inventory to ensure sufficient stock availability.

Changes to cart items trigger notifications to sellers for inventory management and may invalidate previous pricing calculations. The operation updates the session's last_updated timestamp and maintains session state (active, checkout-in-progress) without altering the cart_items structure itself.

Related operations: Retrieve cart items (GET /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}), Add cart item (POST /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}/items), Remove cart item (DELETE /shoppingMall/customer/cart-sessions/{sessionId}/items/{itemId}).

operations.description:
Delete an active shopping cart session for the authenticated user. This operation permanently removes the cart session record from the database. When a cart session is deleted, all associated cart items are automatically cleaned up by the system's cascading relationship rules. This operation is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same sessionId will have no additional effect beyond the first successful deletion.

Security: This operation is restricted to authenticated users who own the cart session. The sessionId must correspond to an active session that was created by the authenticated user. If the sessionId does not match any session owned by the user, or if the session has already been deleted, the system will return a 404 error.

Behavior: The cart session is immediately removed from the database. This action cannot be undone. Any client-side cart state must be cleared by the frontend upon successful deletion. The system does not maintain deleted cart session records for auditing purposes, as cart sessions are considered ephemeral data.

Related operations: Users who wish to retrieve current cart contents should use GET /cart-sessions/{sessionId}. Users who wish to create a new cart for a new session should use POST /cart-sessions.

Note: This is a hard delete operation. The system does not use soft deletion for cart sessions since they are temporary, user-specific data that are not required for compliance, analytics, or auditing.

Implementation note: The cart session ID is uniquely identified by the sessionId path parameter, which must be a UUID format string generated by the system during session creation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of shopping mall orders from the system. This operation queries the shopping_mall_orders table and returns a collection of order summaries with support for advanced filtering by customer, status, date range, payment method, and total amount. Sorting is available by order date, total amount, or status.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100), cursor-based navigation, and sorting direction control. Each order summary includes essential details such as order ID, status, total amount, customer information, payment method, and creation timestamp.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive order information based on the requesting user's authorization level. Only authenticated users may access order data, and customers may only view their own orders through business logic enforced in the provider layer.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderId} - retrieves detailed information about a single order; POST /orders - creates a new order from a cart.

This operation accesses the shopping_mall_orders table and returns comprehensive order information including the order summary, billing and shipping addresses, payment details, order items, and current status.

The order code serves as the primary business identifier and is used in place of a UUID when available, as declared in the shopping_mall_orders table schema. The operation returns all fields from the order entity, with related data structures properly composed.

Security considerations are implemented through the user actor authorization. Only the authenticated user who placed the order (or an admin user with appropriate permissions) can access the order details. The system verifies that the requesting user has the necessary permissions to view this specific order through conditional logic in the implementation.

This operation is designed to be used on-demand by customers in their order history view or by customer support agents assisting with order inquiries. The response structure includes nested child objects (address, payment, items) for comprehensive context without requiring multiple API calls.

The request body contains the customer's selected shipping address ID and payment method ID. The system validates that the address belongs to the authenticated customer and that the payment method is registered and active. The operation rejects orders with items that are out of stock or have been discontinued since being added to the cart.

The response returns the complete order including the order ID, status, total amount, shipping address details, payment method, and all order items with their exact pricing and quantities at time of order creation.

The operation updates the order identified by its unique order code, which is a business identifier rather than a UUID for improved readability.

The order code serves as a human-readable identifier in the format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN where YYYYMMDD is the creation date and NNNN is a sequence number. Security considerations include verification that the authenticated customer owns the order being modified, and restriction of certain modification fields to administrative roles only. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of this operation.

The operation follows a PATCH semantics pattern to allow partial updates, with only specified fields being modified. Other fields remain unchanged. The system provides comprehensive error messages for invalid inputs, including validation failures for address formats, payment status transitions, and order state transitions.

Permanently removes an order record from the shopping mall system. This is a hard delete operation that completely eliminates the order and all its related data from the database without any possibility of recovery.

The operation targets the shopping_mall_orders table in the database schema and performs a cascade delete of all associated records from dependent tables including shipping, payments, order items, and audit logs.

Security protocol requires that only authenticated users with proper permissions (the order owner or admin) can initiate this deletion. The system automatically verifies ownership by matching the authenticated user's ID with the order's customer_id field before performing deletion. Admin users can delete any order regardless of ownership for support and compliance purposes.

This hard delete operation cannot be undone. Once executed, the order and all its associated data are permanently lost from the system.

The system maintains comprehensive audit logs of all operational events, including this deletion, for system integrity tracking, but the order record itself is permanently deleted from the active database.

The operation targets the shopping_mall_orders table in the database schema and removes all associated records from dependent tables including shipping, payments, order items, and audit logs. Because this is a business-critical financial transaction, the system enforces hard deletion to ensure data integrity and legal compliance for completed transactions.

Security protocol requires that only authenticated users with proper permissions (the order owner or admin) can initiate this deletion. The system automatically verifies ownership by matching the authenticated user's ID with the order's customer_id field before performing deletion. This hard delete operation cannot be undone. Once executed, the order and all its associated data are permanently lost from the system. The system maintains comprehensive audit logs of deletion events for compliance purposes, recording the actor, timestamp, and IP address of the deletion request.

This deletion pattern follows financial transaction integrity best practices where completed orders that have been fully processed, shipped, and paid are permanently archived in the database and removed from active records to maintain system performance and data consistency.

Note: Canceled or pending orders are managed through separate status-based workflows and are not affected by this hard deletion operation, which only applies to orders that have been fully completed and processed through the system.

The order and item codes are used as composite unique identifiers to locate the specific order item. The system uses the unique constraint defined on (order_id, code) in the shopping_mall_order_items table. The orderCode represents the shopping_mall_orders.code field, and itemCode represents the shopping_mall_order_items.code field. Both are human-readable business identifiers rather than system-generated UUIDs.

Security considerations include verification that the requesting user has permission to access this order (either as the order owner or as an admin). The system cross-checks the order's customerId field against the authenticated user ID. Access is denied to users who did not create the order and who are not administrators.

The operation also verifies that both the order and the item exist and are not marked for deletion. If the order status is 'cancelled' or 'refunded', the item data is still accessible for record-keeping and dispute resolution purposes.

In the event the order code or item code does not exist in the system, a 404 Not Found error is returned. Requesting invalid codes is strictly prohibited and will not return empty results.

This operation complements GET /orders/{orderCode} to provide deeper visibility into individual items within an order. It is used for order tracking, customer service inquiries, and return processing when customers need exact product details at the time of purchase.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderCode} (retrieves entire order summary), PATCH /orders/{orderCode}/items (lists all items in an order), and POST /orders/{orderCode}/items (creates new items in an order, though this typically happens during cart checkout).

Create a new order item associated with a specific shopping order in the e-commerce platform.

This operation allows customers or system processes to add individual product variants to an existing order. Each item must reference a valid product variant (SKU) and specify the quantity to be purchased. The order must already exist and be in a state that permits item addition (typically 'pending' or 'draft'), as items cannot be added to completed, cancelled, or shipped orders.

The system validates that the requested product variant exists, is available in the requested quantity, belongs to the same seller as specified in the order, and is active (not discontinued). If inventory is insufficient, the operation returns an error. Pricing is locked at the time of creation, using the current variant price from shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, ensuring price stability even if the product price changes later.

The item is immediately associated with the order and recorded in the shopping_mall_order_items table. Once successfully created, the order's total amount is recalculated, and inventory for the variant is reserved in the shopping_mall_variant_inventory table. This operation does not trigger payment processing; it only adds items to the order. Related operations include: updating order items via PUT /orders/{orderCode}/items/{itemId}, deleting items via DELETE /orders/{orderCode}/items/{itemId}, and retrieving order items via GET /orders/{orderCode}/items.

Security: The customer must be authenticated as the owner of the order or have admin privileges. The operation verifies order ownership via the orderCode and the authenticated user's identity, preventing unauthorized modifications.

The operation never returns deleted or purged events, preserving the complete audit trail per compliance requirements for e-commerce systems.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderCode} provides order summary, while POST /orders creates new orders with initial events.

operations.description:
Update an existing order refund request with new details or status.

This operation allows customers or administrators to modify the status or details of an order refund request. The refund request must be linked to an existing order by its unique code, and the refund itself is identified by its unique refund code. This operation can be used to approve, reject, modify refund amounts, update refund methods, or adjust refund reasons.

The system uses the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_refunds tables. The order_code parameter references the unique identifier in the shopping_mall_orders table, while the refund_code parameter references the unique identifier in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table. The refund_code follows a pattern of alphanumeric identifiers generated at refund request creation.

System checks ensure the refund exists, belongs to the specified order, and can only be modified based on its current state (e.g., rejected refunds cannot be modified). Business rules enforce that the refund amount cannot exceed the original order total and can only be modified by customer support or administrators. The original order's status must be confirmed as 'completed' or 'shipped' before any refund can be processed, ensuring refunds only occur after fulfillment.

This operation returns the updated refund record. If the refund status is changed to "approved", a financial processing job is initiated. If changed to "rejected", the customer is notified via email and the refund is cancelled. The operation is non-idempotent — repeated calls with different data will update the refund state accordingly.

Related operations:
- GET /orders/{orderCode}/refunds/{refundCode} - Retrieves refund details
- POST /orders/{orderCode}/refunds - Creates a new refund request
- DELETE /orders/{orderCode}/refunds/{refundCode} - Cancels a refund request

This operation requires authorization as 'customer' or 'admin' since only the order owner (customer) or administrators can modify refunds. System logic ensures refund ownership matches the authenticated user's account, or that the user has admin permissions.

Permanently erase a specific refund record associated with an order. This operation removes a refund request from the system's database, irreversibly deleting the refund record. The refund is linked to a specific order via a composite unique constraint between the orderCode and refundCode fields, ensuring each refund is uniquely identified within its parent order.

This deletion is permanent and cannot be reversed. The refund amount is not restored to the customer's payment method, nor is the order status modified. This operation is typically used for administrative cleanup of test refunds, erroneous refund records, or when a refund must be completely removed due to compliance or audit requirements. The system maintains an immutable audit log of this deletion in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table.

Only users with admin privileges can execute this operation. The operation validates that both the referenced order and refund exist, and that the refund belongs to the specified order. After deletion, all related records in shopping_mall_payment_refunds and shopping_mall_order_events are archived with a deletion marker in the database, maintaining referential integrity for financial reporting while removing the active record from the system.

This operation does not trigger notifications or update inventory levels, as refunds have already been processed before this deletion action is taken. Any customer-facing refunds are handled through the refund approval workflow before reaching this deletion state.

Retrieve detailed delivery tracking information for a specific order by its unique order code. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_delivery_trackings and shopping_mall_order_shipments tables to provide a comprehensive view of delivery status, carrier information, and estimated delivery timelines based on real-time carrier API updates.

The system aggregates delivery events from external carriers (FedEx, UPS, DHL, USPS, and regional providers) linked to the order through the shipping tracking number. Each tracking event is timestamped and automatically triggers the appropriate order status transition: 'Shipped' → 'In Transit' → 'Out for Delivery' → 'Delivered'. The delivery information is updated continuously every 6 hours through carrier API polls.

The response includes all delivery events in chronological order, the current delivery status, the carrier name and logo, tracking number, estimated delivery date calculated from processing time and transit time, and a persistent tracking URL. This endpoint is used by customers to monitor their order progress in real time and is accessed through the order tracking page.

Security: This endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication because delivery tracking information is considered non-sensitive and essential for customer experience. However, it only exposes data related to the specific order code provided in the path. No customer personal information beyond delivery status is included in the response.

This operation directly supports the Order Tracking System described in 08-order-tracking.md, implementing the delivery tracking link generation, status update logic, and carrier integration requirements. It fulfills the business need for transparency and customer reassurance throughout the delivery journey.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderCode} (retrieves general order summary), PATCH /orders (searches orders by criteria).

operations.description:
Create a new payment intent for processing customer payments through the shoppingMall platform's payment gateway system. This operation directly interfaces with the shopping_mall_payment_intents database table, which represents the initial request for payment processing before actual transaction completion.

Each payment intent represents a customer's intention to pay for goods or services and serves as the initial state in the payment processing lifecycle. The system generates a unique payment intent that contains all necessary payment details including amount, currency, customer information, and payment method preferences. This intent is then forwarded to the configured payment gateway for authorization and capture.

The operation requires the customer's identification (via JWT token), the payment amount, currency, and optionally specifies the payment method to be used. The system ensures PCI-DSS compliance by never storing full payment card details, instead relying on tokenized payment methods and encrypted payment vouchers. All payment intents are automatically persisted in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table with a unique ID and status of 'created'.

The payment intent created through this operation will be processed asynchronously by the payment gateway. Once processed, the system will receive a webhook notification from the payment gateway which will update the payment intent's status to 'authorized', 'captured', 'declined', or 'failed' based on the gateway response.

This operation does not immediately complete the transaction; it merely initiates the payment process. The subsequent steps include customer verification, gateway authorization, and final settlement. The payment intent ID generated by this endpoint must be used in subsequent operations to check payment status or to complete the transaction.

operations.description:
Update an existing payment intent with new configuration details or status changes.

This operation modifies the state or configuration of a specific payment intent identified by its unique identifier. Payment intents represent pre-authorization payment requests in the shoppingMall payment system that are pending completion. Updating a payment intent might involve changing its amount, adding customer details, updating payment method preferences, or transitioning its status (e.g., from 'requires_payment_method' to 'succeeded').

Important implementation note: All updates to payment intents must maintain financial consistency and auditability. Changes that affect monetary values or payment method references trigger system-level validation to ensure business rule compliance and prevent unauthorized modifications. The operation validates that the payment intent exists and belongs to the authenticated user (customer or admin with sufficient privileges). Only certain status transitions are allowed per payment lifecycle rules (e.g., cannot transition from 'succeeded' directly to 'canceled'; must use refunds instead). Changes to the amount, currency, or payment method after a payment intent has been paid are strictly prohibited.

Authentication: This endpoint requires the caller to be either the customer who created the payment intent or an admin with payment management privileges. The system verifies ownership using the JWT token's subject identifier. For admin users, the system additionally checks if the payment intent falls within their permitted merchant scope.

Security: The update operation is idempotent — multiple identical requests have the same effect as a single request. Any modification to a payment intent generates an internal audit log entry for security and compliance purposes. This ensures full traceability of changes for financial reconciliation and fraud detection.

Related operations: 
- GET /payment-intents/{paymentIntentId} — Retrieve current payment intent state
- POST /payment-intents — Create new payment intents
- POST /payment-intents/{paymentIntentId}/confirm — Process payment for intent
- POST /payment-intents/{paymentIntentId}/cancel — Cancel an unfulfilled payment intent
- POST /payment-intents/{paymentIntentId}/refunds — Issue refunds for fulfilled payment intents
