operations.description:
Process a new payment for an order on the shoppingMall platform. This operation handles the creation of a payment record associated with an order, using a previously selected payment method. The payment is processed through the system's payment gateway, with the transaction status tracked in real-time. The system attempts to charge the selected payment method and records the outcome in the shopping_mall_payments table. On success, a payment intent is created to manage the transaction lifecycle.

Security: This operation is publicly accessible to any authenticated user (customer or seller) who has an active order to settle. Authentication is validated via JWT token, and only the owner of the order can initiate a payment. All transaction details are encrypted at rest using AES-256 and transmitted over TLS 1.3.

Business Logic: Payment processing follows a state machine where the payment can be in 'pending', 'succeeded', 'failed', or 'canceled' states. If the payment fails, the order remains in 'pending_payment' state, and the system automatically retries the transaction up to three times with exponential backoff. If all attempts fail, the order is automatically canceled. For successful payments, the system triggers fulfillment processing and updates the order status to 'paid'. The system validates that the order exists, is not already paid, and that the selected payment method is active and belongs to the requesting user.

Integration Details: The operation integrates with external payment providers (Stripe, PayPal, etc.) through the payment gateway service. The request body contains the order ID and payment method ID, which are used to look up the previously stored payment credentials. Sensitive data (like card numbers) is never stored or transmitted; only payment method tokens and IDs are used. The response returns full payment details including the payment_id, status, amount, currency, and transaction_id.

Related Operations: GET /payments/{paymentId} - To check payment status, PATCH /payments - To search for payments by criteria, PUT /payments/{paymentId} - To update payment method information if needed, DELETE /payments/{paymentId} - To cancel a pending payment.

Validation: The system enforces that all payment requests contain a valid order ID and payment method ID that belong to the authenticated user. Amounts must match the order total and be positive values. The system blocks attempts to process payments for orders with status 'canceled' or 'completed'.

Permanently removes a payment record from the system, irreversibly deleting all associated payment transaction data. This operation targets the shopping_mall_payments database table and is designed for use cases where payments need to be purged due to compliance requirements, duplicate entries, or test data cleanup.

This operation performs a hard delete, meaning the payment record is permanently removed from the database with no possibility of recovery. Unlike soft deletion patterns, no "deleted_at" timestamp or soft delete flag is applied. The system does not maintain historical copies of deleted payments for audit purposes.

Security Considerations: This operation requires admin-level authorization because payment deletion represents a significant system integrity concern. Payment records are financial artifacts that should never be deleted for routine cleanup or customer requests. Only platform administrators with elevated privileges can trigger this operation, and it should be used exclusively for compliance or data integrity emergencies. Any deletion triggers a system audit log.

Implementation Note: This operation does not interact with external payment gateways or third-party systems to reverse transactions. For transaction reversals or refunds, the appropriate API endpoints (POST /payments/{paymentId}/refund) should be used instead. This DELETE operation only removes the payment record from the system database.

Prerequisites: This operation should only be called after all related financial records have been reconciled and any affected orders have been properly handled through refund or adjustment processes. It is strongly recommended to consult with a finance team member before executing this operation due to its irreversible nature and impact on financial reporting.
operations.name: erase

parameters.name: paymentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the payment record to be permanently deleted. This must reference an existing payment in the shopping_mall_payments table.

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated refund records from the system based on complex search criteria. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_order_refunds table and provides advanced filtering capabilities for refund management.

This endpoint supports searching refund records by date range, order reference, refund status, amount thresholds, and customer identifier. It enables administrators and support personnel to efficiently review, audit, and process refund requests. The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options by refund amount, creation date, or status.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive refund details based on the requesting user's authorization level. All refund data is returned in a paginated summary format optimized for administrative review interfaces. The operation returns refund records with complete context including associated order information, refund reason, and financial details.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific payment refund. This operation is associated with the shopping_mall_payment_refunds database table and returns the complete record of a payment refund transaction, including the original payment reference, refund amount, reason, status, timestamps, and associated order information.

The refund record is immutable once created and provides a complete audit trail for financial reconciliation. The refund status will indicate whether the refund is pending, processed, or failed, and the refund amount represents the exact monetary value returned to the customer's original payment method.

Payment refunds are created automatically by the system when a customer initiates a return or when an order is cancelled, and this endpoint allows authorized users to retrieve detailed refund records for reconciliation, customer support, or financial reporting purposes. This operation should be called to verify refund status after initiating return requests or to investigate payment discrepancies. Related operations include PATCH /payment-refunds for listing refunds and PATCH /orders/{orderId}/returns for initiating new refund requests.

operations.description:
Create a new refund request for a previously processed payment.

This operation allows customers to initiate refund requests for payments processed through the shoppingMall platform. Each refund request is linked to a specific payment record in the shopping_mall_payments table and captures essential details including the refund amount, reason for refund, and optional customer comments.

The system validates that the requested refund amount does not exceed the original payment amount and checks that the payment has not already been fully refunded. Refund requests are processed asynchronously through the payment gateway's refund API and updated with the final status once processing completes.

Security considerations include verifying the requester's identity against the payment's associated user account and preventing refund fraud through rate limiting and anomaly detection. Business rules require refund reasons to be selected from predefined categories to maintain consistency in financial reporting and customer service.

Related operations include GET /payment-refunds/{refundId} to check refund status and GET /payments/{paymentId} to verify the original payment details before initiating a refund.

responseBody.description: Created refund request with generated ID and initial status

prerequisites.description: Payment must exist and be successfully processed before a refund can be initiated, as refund requests require a valid payment_id linked to an existing payment record in the shopping_mall_payments table.

operations.description:
Update the status of a payment refund request in the system. This operation operates on the OrderRefunds table from the database schema and allows system administrators or authorized users to update the status of pending refund requests to approved or rejected based on fraud detection, policy compliance, or customer service decisions.

The refund status transition follows a strict business rule: refunds can only be updated from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected'. The system prevents invalid transitions such as 'approved' to 'rejected' or direct creation of finalized statuses. Every status transition creates an immutable audit record in the payment_refund_audit_logs table to maintain compliance with financial regulations.

The request body contains the new refund status and optional reason for the decision, which must be selected from predefined options in the order_cancellation_reasons table. The operation validates that the refund with the specified refundId exists and is currently in 'pending' status. When a refund is approved, the system automatically initiates the payment reversal process through the payment gateway. When rejected, the customer is notified with the rejection reason.

Security: This operation requires authorization by the 'admin' actor. Only users with this role can initiate refund status changes. All refund actions are logged in the system audit trail.

Related operations: GET /payment-refunds/{refundId} retrieves current refund details, and PATCH /payment-refunds filters refund requests by status, timestamp, or reason.
operations.name: update

parameters.name: refundId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the payment refund request to update. Each refundId corresponds to an entry in the shopping_mall_order_refunds table.

requestBody.description: Update request for payment refund status change.

responseBody.description: The updated payment refund record after status change.

prerequisites.description: A refund record must be created before its status can be updated to 'approved' or 'rejected' via PUT /shoppingMall/admin/payment-refunds/{refundId}

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a payment refund record from the system. This operation directly modifies the shopping_mall_order_refunds table in the database schema. The refund record identified by refundId is completely removed from persistent storage, and all associated financial reconciliation data is purged. This is a hard delete operation that cannot be undone, and all related payment records are marked as complete in the payment system. For compliance purposes, a timestamped audit entry is generated in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table with action='REFUND_DELETED', reflecting the deletion event, actor, and timestamp.

Security: Only authenticated users with appropriate permissions (typically account administrators or finance team members) can perform this operation. The request must include a valid JWT token containing appropriate roles. The system validates that the refund record exists and belongs to an order that can be deleted according to financial policies.

Business logic: This deletion is only permitted for refunds that are in pending or approved status, and only before any associated funds have been processed by the financial institution. The system verifies that the refund has not yet been processed externally before allowing deletion.

Related operations: This operation complements GET /payment-refunds/{refundId} which retrieves refund information, and PATCH /payment-refunds which searches for refund records.

parameters.name: refundId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the refund record to be deleted (global scope)

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: Refund must be created before it can be deleted. POST /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderCode}/refunds creates the refund record that this deletion operation targets.

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated audit logs for payment processing activities. This operation queries the shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs table to retrieve comprehensive records of all payment-related system activities including authorization attempts, gateway communications, transaction status changes, fraud detection events, and payment reconciliation processes.

The audit logs contain detailed information about payment processing events with timestamps, actor context, IP addresses, payment intent identifiers, gateway response codes, and error details. This operation supports filtering by payment status, date ranges, actor types, and specific payment intent IDs to retrieve targeted audit trails.

Security considerations include strict access controls ensuring only administrative actors can view payment audit logs, as this data contains sensitive transaction information and may be subject to financial compliance regulations. The operation enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse of this detailed audit functionality, and all results are returned without personally identifiable information (PII) in compliance with data protection requirements.

This endpoint serves as the primary mechanism for financial compliance teams, fraud analysts, and system administrators to investigate payment-related incidents, reconcile discrepancies between system records and gateway settlements, and meet regulatory reporting requirements. It integrates with the payment audit logging system and the payment processing workflow, providing essential forensic data for audit trails and investigations.

Related operations: GET /payments to retrieve current payment states, PATCH /payments to search payment records by filtering criteria.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and filtering parameters for payment audit logs

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of payment audit log records matching the search criteria

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific payment audit log entry from the system. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs table in the database and returns detailed information about a single payment audit event that was recorded during payment processing.

The audit log contains comprehensive details including the type of payment action performed, the amount involved, the payment method used, the transaction status, and the timestamp of the event. It also links to the associated payment transaction via the payment_id field and contains metadata such as the IP address and user agent string of the actor who triggered the event.

This operation is strictly administrative and should only be accessed by admin users to review payment activity for purposes such as fraud investigation, compliance audits, operational troubleshooting, and user dispute resolution. Sensitive financial details like full payment method identifiers and transaction secrets are masked in the response according to PCI-DSS compliance requirements.

Security: This endpoint is restricted to admin users only. The operation requires authentication with an admin token, and all access is logged for audit purposes. The system maintains an immutable log of all audit log access attempts.

Payment audit logs are immutable append-only records that preserve a historical record of payment actions for compliance, financial reconciliation, and audit purposes. These records cannot be modified, deleted, or "soft deleted" under any circumstances, ensuring the integrity of financial transaction history.

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated payment gateway logs for audit and reconciliation purposes. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs table to provide system administrators with a comprehensive view of payment gateway interactions, including timestamps, transaction IDs, gateway responses, error codes, and request payloads.

The operation supports advanced filtering by date range, gateway type, transaction status (success/failure), and specific transaction IDs. It enables financial teams to perform reconciliation, investigate payment failures, audit compliance, and monitor gateway health. Results are paginated with configurable limit and offset parameters to handle large datasets efficiently without performance degradation.

Security and access control: Only users with admin privileges can perform this operation due to the sensitive nature of payment data. The logs contain transaction-level details that could reveal customer payment information, requiring strict authorization controls.

This operation is frequently used alongside the POST /payment-gateway-logs endpoint which records new gateway interactions. It is also complementary to the GET /payment-reconciliation endpoint for comprehensive financial auditing.

Implementation note: This endpoint does not correspond to a traditional CRUD operation on a primary entity but serves as a read-only audit log retrieval system. The data is generated automatically by the payment processing system and is never manually modified by users.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific payment gateway log entry from the system's audit trail. This operation queries the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs table in the database schema and returns detailed information about a single payment gateway interaction, including timestamp, gateway provider, transaction status, and error context if applicable.

The data captured in this log is generated automatically by the system during payment processing attempts and serves as an immutable audit record for troubleshooting payment failures, investigating fraudulent transactions, and reconciling payment status discrepancies. Each log entry is uniquely identified by its logId and cannot be modified or deleted after creation.

Security considerations include access restriction to administrative users only, as payment gateway logs contain sensitive transaction metadata that could be exploited if exposed to unauthorized parties. The operation implements strict authorization controls to ensure only users with admin privileges can access this sensitive audit data.

The log structure includes: the timestamp of the payment attempt, the gateway provider identifier, the request payload hash, the response data, the final status (success/failed/pending), any error codes returned by the gateway, and the IP address from which the request originated. This detailed audit trail allows the payment team to reconstruct the exact sequence of events for any transaction.

Related operations: List payment logs (PATCH /payment-gateway-logs), Export payment logs (GET /payment-gateway-logs/export).

This operation does NOT support soft deletion - payment gateway logs are immutable audit trails that persist indefinitely for regulatory compliance. Deleting these records would violate financial audit requirements.

Note: This operation does NOT update or modify any payment records; it is strictly for read-only audit purposes.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific payment region configuration from the system. This operation queries the shopping_mall_payment_regions table in the database schema to extract the region's payment acceptance rules, supported currencies, regional tax regulations, and payment gateway configurations. The region is identified by its unique code.

This operation is primarily used by customer-facing applications to dynamically display available payment methods during checkout based on the customer's location. It allows the system to enforce regional compliance with financial regulations and currency requirements without hardcoding payment rules.

The response includes all relevant configuration data for the specified region, including which payment methods are approved (credit cards, digital wallets, bank transfers), time zone offsets for payment processing, currency conversion settings, and any specific regional tax rules that must be applied. This eliminates the need for clients to maintain separate payment rule databases for each supported region.

This operation is read-only and does not modify any data in the system. It always returns the most current configuration for the requested region.

Security considerations: No authentication required since payment region data is public information needed for customer checkout processes. This operation has no relationship with user authentication or session management systems and can be called by anonymous users.

Related operations: This data is consumed by PATCH /payments/payment-methods which lists available payment options, and during POST /orders to validate payment region compliance at order placement.

operations.description:
Create a new payment region configuration for the shopping mall platform. This operation allows administrators to define geographic regions where specific payment processing rules and currency settings will apply, enabling localized payment experiences for customers based on their location.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_payment_regions table in the database, which stores the geographic and payment processing parameters for each defined region. Each region can have unique specifications for supported currencies, payment gateway preferences, tax regulations, and fraud detection thresholds that differ from other regions.

The system automatically associates newly created regions with the appropriate financial compliance frameworks based on the jurisdiction's legal requirements. Payment region settings are used by the payment processing engine to automatically select appropriate payment methods, apply correct currency conversions, and enforce region-specific fraud detection rules during checkout.

Security is enforced through admin-only authorization, as payment region configurations impact financial transactions system-wide. The operation validates that all required fields including region code, currency code, and primary gateway are provided, and that the region code follows the international standard format for geographic regions. Duplicate region codes are rejected to maintain data integrity.

This operation is foundational for supporting international sales and localized financial compliance, enabling the platform to expand into new markets with appropriate regional payment configurations without requiring manual code changes for each new geography.

responseBody.description: The newly created payment region with its generated unique identifier and system-assigned configuration settings

The operation allows administrators to modify regional payment settings such as enabled/disabled status, supported payment methods, currency preferences, and compliance settings. When updating a payment region, the system must ensure all changes maintain compliance with regional financial regulations and currency control policies. The operation validates that the regionId corresponds to an existing and active payment region record.

This operation is critical for managing payment operations across different jurisdictions and requires administrative authorization to prevent unauthorized changes to financial configurations. All changes are logged for accountability and audit purposes. Changes to payment regions may affect ongoing transactions, so modifications should be carefully coordinated.

The operation performs a hard delete, permanently removing all region-specific configuration data including allowed payment methods, currency settings, tax rules, and associated constraints. This action cannot be undone and will not affect existing orders that were previously processed under this region.

Security: Only administrators can delete payment regions to prevent accidental removal of critical payment configuration data. The system does not implement soft deletion for payment regions as these are foundational configuration entities with historical audit implications.

operations.description:
Retrieve paginated list of payment gateway failover configurations for system health monitoring and failover strategy analysis.

This operation operates on the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_failovers table and provides comprehensive inspection of all configured gateway failover rules across the system. The failover configurations represent system-level fallback strategies that activate when primary payment gateways encounter failures or timeouts.

The operation supports advanced filtering by gateway name, region, priority level, and active status. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and support sorting by creation timestamp, priority weight, or last tested status. Each configuration includes details of both primary and backup gateway identifiers, activation thresholds, retry intervals, and status monitoring history.

Security considerations include that this operation is publicly accessible since failover configurations are not sensitive business data but rather operational system configurations analogous to network routing tables. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of this diagnostic endpoint. This operation serves critical infrastructure monitoring needs and is essential for proactive system maintenance and incident response planning.

Related operations include: PATCH /payments/payment-gateway-status (for real-time gateway status), and GET /payments/settings (for viewing current payment configuration).

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific payment gateway failover configuration. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_failovers table in the database to fetch the configuration details of a specific failover entry identified by its unique failoverId. The failover configuration includes the primary gateway identifier, failover gateway identifier, failover trigger conditions, last tested timestamp, and current operational status.

This operation is exclusively available to administrators due to the sensitive nature of payment infrastructure configurations. Unauthorized access to failover settings could compromise payment system reliability and financial integrity.

The failoverId parameter must be a valid identifier from the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_failovers table. The operation returns comprehensive details about the failover configuration including both primary and failover gateway identifiers, trigger conditions for automatic switching (such as latency thresholds, error rate percentages, and timeout durations), the last timestamp when the failover mechanism was tested, and the current status (active/inactive).

The response includes complete configuration details necessary for monitoring and managing payment system redundancy. This operation supports auditing of payment infrastructure configuration changes and is essential for ensuring high availability of the payment processing system.

Related operations: PATCH /payment-gateway-failovers (to list all failovers), PUT /payment-gateway-failovers/{failoverId} (to update failover configuration).

operations.description:
Configure or register a new payment gateway failover configuration in the shoppingMall platform. This operation allows administrators to add a fallback payment gateway configuration to ensure continuous payment processing during primary gateway failures.

This operation operates on the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_failovers table in the database and is used to define backup payment gateway endpoints that will be automatically invoked when a primary gateway fails to respond within the configured timeout window.

The failover system is critical for maintaining 99.99% payment processing uptime across multiple geographic regions and payment providers. Each failover entry defines a priority sequence, enabling automated fallback hierarchies.

Security: Only system administrators can modify failover configurations. Changes are automatically logged in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table for compliance and audit purposes. The operation validates that the target payment gateway is both active and properly configured in the shopping_mall_payment_gateways table before registering the failover.

Implementation: The failover configuration includes a timeout threshold (in milliseconds), priority level (1 being highest priority), and a reference to the target payment gateway ID. A maxRetryCount field determines how many consecutive failures should occur before triggering the failover. The system automatically registers this failover in memory for immediate use without requiring a service restart.

Related Operations: Check payment gateway health (GET /payment-gateways/{gatewayId}/health), List all active gateways (GET /payment-gateways), Retrieve failover chain (GET /payment-gateway-failovers).

Update the payment gateway failover configuration in the system. This operation modifies the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_failovers table records to change the failover settings, priority, or state of a specific payment gateway candidate. Only administrators have permission to modify these critical system configurations that determine payment processing fallback behavior during gateway outages.

This failover configuration is essential for maintaining payment processing uptime by automatically switching to alternate payment gateways when primary ones are unresponsive. The failover record contains the sequence number to determine processing order, status flags indicating active/inactive state, and metadata about the payment gateway being configured.

The operation validates that the failoverId corresponds to an existing failover entry in the database and that the payload contains only allowed fields. Changes to failover settings take immediate effect in the payment routing logic, affecting all transactions processed after the update.

Security considerations include strict administrative access control, audit logging for configuration changes, and the need for careful testing to avoid inadvertent disruption of payment processing. Misconfigured failovers could result in payment processing failures or security vulnerabilities if incorrect gateways are enabled.

Related operations:
- GET /payment-gateway-failovers: List all payment gateway failover configurations
- DELETE /payment-gateway-failovers/{failoverId}: Remove a payment gateway failover configuration
- POST /payment-gateway-failovers: Add a new payment gateway failover configuration

This is a hard delete operation that permanently removes the failover record without soft deletion. The failover entry contains critical infrastructure configuration data including the gateway provider identifier, priority level, timeout settings, and retry policies used during payment processing failures.

Security: Only administrators with "admin" actor status can perform this operation. This ensures that sensitive payment infrastructure configurations cannot be modified by regular users or sellers. The operation requires the failoverId parameter which uniquely identifies the specific failover configuration to be deleted.

Implementation note: This endpoint directly interacts with the shopping_mall_payment_gateway_failovers table. No dependent relationships or cascading deletions are involved since this table appears to be a standalone configuration entity with no foreign key relationships to other tables.

After successful deletion, no response body is returned. The operation returns a 204 No Content status code to indicate successful completion. This is consistent with standard REST practices for delete operations on configuration entities.

This operation supports the platform's requirement for secure, auditable payment infrastructure management by restricting access to administrative personnel only.

This operation operates on the shopping_mall_payment_tokenizations table, which stores encrypted payment token data for PCI-DSS compliant storage. The system maintains tokenizations for secure recurring payments, card-on-file authentication, and payment method reuse across customer sessions without exposing raw payment card details. Each tokenization record links to an associated payment method and customer account, with automatic expiration after 12 months for security compliance. The operation supports advanced filtering for audit trails, subscription billing management, and reconciliation workflows, returning only non-expired tokens that are valid for payment operations. Request parameters include customer ID for scope restriction, status filters for inactive/active tokens, and date ranges for historical review. Security context requires the caller to be either an authenticated customer viewing their own tokens or an admin with appropriate permissions.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific payment tokenization record from the system. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_payment_tokenizations table in the database, which stores encrypted payment token references for PCI-DSS compliant payment processing.

Each tokenization represents a securely stored payment method reference, typically generated when a customer saves a credit card for future purchases. The system does not store full PANs (Primary Account Numbers) or CVV values, only cryptographically secured tokens that can be used to initiate payments with authorized gateways.

When retrieving a tokenization, the system validates that the requesting user is the owner of the tokenization (for customers) or has appropriate administrative permissions (for support or admin users). Tokenization records contain metadata including the payment method type, last four digits of the card, issuer information, and expiration date, but never the full payment account details.

This endpoint is typically used by customers to view their saved payment methods during checkout or account management, and by support agents to verify payment method details for dispute resolution. Security measures include token validation against session context and access control based on user authentication and authorization actors.

Existing payment methods can be marked as 'inactive' when a new default payment method is added, using the status field in the shopping_mall_payment_tokenizations table.

This operation is restricted to admin actors only, as payment surcharge rules directly impact financial transactions and revenue calculations. The update operation is transactional and will roll back if any validation fails, ensuring data consistency. Error handling includes appropriate HTTP status codes and error messages for invalid ruleIds, date format violations, percentage range violations, and conflicting active status changes. Related operations include retrieving all rules (PATCH /payment-surcharge-rules), retrieving a specific rule (GET /payment-surcharge-rules/{ruleId}), and creating a new rule (POST /payment-surcharge-rules).

Each record represents a unique rate limit rule that associates a payment method with a time window (e.g., 5 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours) and a maximum transaction count. Security considerations include ensuring that only authorized administrators can view rate limit configurations. Security considerations include that only system administrators with admin privileges can view or modify payment rate limits. The configuration is stored in the database with a timestamp for audit purposes and all changes are tracked through system-generated audit logs.

When a rate limit is configured, the system automatically propagates the rule to all active payment gateways and begins enforcing it immediately. Reconfiguration of existing limits will override previous rules for the same combination of payment method, currency, and region.

The system verifies the webhook signature using registered provider secrets and cross-references the payment_id with the shopping_mall_payments table. Invalid signatures or mismatched payment IDs result in 401 Unauthorized responses.

Processing: Upon successful verification, the system updates the corresponding payment record in the payments table, logs the event in the payment_audit_logs table, and triggers downstream workflows such as order fulfillment, email notifications to customers, and seller payout processing. The operation is idempotent: repeated notifications with the same payment_id are accepted but have no further effect on the payment status.

This operation is essential for the payment processing workflow, as it closes the loop between external payment providers and the internal payment system. Related operations: POST /payments (initiates payment), GET /payments/{paymentId} (retrieves payment status).

operations.description:
Process and validate incoming payment webhook notifications from payment gateways.

This operation handles asynchronous webhook payloads from payment providers such as Stripe, PayPal, and other financial gateways that notify the system of payment events including success, failure, refund processing, and dispute filings. The webhooks contain signed payloads that must be verified against registered provider signatures, mapped to corresponding payment intents or transactions, and processed to update order statuses, issue refunds, or trigger fraud alerts.

Security is paramount: each webhook request must contain a valid signature header matching the registered provider's secret key. The system validates the payload origin, parses the event type, matches it to related payment records in the shopping_mall_payment_intents or shopping_mall_payments tables, and updates financial records atomically. This prevents duplicate processing and ensures audit trail integrity.

Events trigger downstream workflows including customer notifications, inventory release for completed payments, or fraud investigation queues for disputed transactions. All webhook processing is logged in shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs for compliance and debugging.

This endpoint is critical for system automation and operates independently of user-facing interfaces. Only trusted payment gateway IP addresses are allowed to access this endpoint - no end-user authentication is involved since webhook calls originate from payment service providers.

The request body follows JSON-based event schema specific to the payment provider and includes fields such as event type, timestamp, payment ID, amount, currency, and metadata. The response includes a 200 OK status with empty body to acknowledge receipt, and no other response data is returned since this is a one-way notification system.

Related operations: GET /payments/{paymentId} (to verify payment status after webhook processing), PATCH /payments (to search for payments with dispute statuses).

This operation accesses the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table, which stores webhook configurations used for notifying external systems about payment events. Each webhook defines a URL endpoint to which payment system events (such as payment succeeded, payment failed, refund processed, etc.) will be sent, along with the active status, secret key for signature verification, and event types to trigger.

The webhook ID is used to uniquely identify which webhook configuration to retrieve. This endpoint is primarily used by system administrators and payment integration teams to audit webhook settings, verify delivery targets, or troubleshoot notification failures. It does not trigger event delivery but only reads the stored configuration data.

The operation requires administrative authorization because webhook configurations contain sensitive information including endpoint URLs and secret keys used for payload signature verification. Standard users or sellers cannot view webhook configurations.

This operation does not modify any data and has no associated request body. The response contains a complete definition of the webhook including all configuration details.

The system uses this endpoint to update order payment statuses, trigger reconciliation processes, and maintain accurate financial records.

The webhook endpoint receives JSON payloads containing payment event data as defined by external providers. Each payload includes a unique identifier for the payment, event type, timestamp, and relevant financial details. The system validates the authenticity of the webhook by verifying provider-specific signatures and ensuring the source IP address is from an authorized payment gateway.

Security considerations include strict validation of incoming webhook signatures, rate limiting to prevent abuse, logging of all received webhooks for audit purposes, and idempotency handling to prevent duplicate processing of the same event. Each webhook is processed once and only once, even if the same payload is received multiple times due to network issues or provider retry attempts.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks database table, which stores the raw webhook payload, event type, processing status, processing timestamp, and error information (if any). The webhook data is matched to corresponding payment records in the shopping_mall_payments table to update payment statuses accordingly.

The webhook must exist in the system before it can be updated. This operation uses the provided webhookId as a path parameter to identify the specific webhook record. All fields are updatable except the webhook ID itself, which is immutable since it serves as the primary identifier.

Security operations: This is a public endpoint designed to receive events from payment gateways. Network-level firewall rules, not user-based permissions, protect against unauthorized access. Authentication is handled at the application layer through secure signature verification of each incoming event payload.

Business logic validation: The system validates that the URL endpoint is properly formatted as a URI and has an accepted protocol (https). Attempts to update with a non-HTTPS URL will fail. The active flag controls whether the webhook is currently enabled to receive events. Setting it to false temporarily disables the webhook without deleting it.

operations.description:
Create a new shipping tracking record for an order shipment in the shopping mall platform. This operation is used to register tracking information with the assigned carrier when an order is dispatched for delivery. It links directly to the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings database table which stores shipment tracking data including carrier, tracking number, estimated delivery date, and current status updates.

The operation requires authentication from any authorized user with access to the order being tracked. Typically initiated by the seller when preparing shipment or by customer service representatives when managing customer inquiries. The system automatically generates a unique tracking identifier and associates it with the related order through the order_id foreign key relationship. The initial status is set to 'created' with no actual carrier data until the shipment is confirmed with the logistics provider.

The request body captures the necessary shipment data including carrier reference, tracking number, package dimensions, and weight for inventory and logistics processing. The response returns the created tracking record with its generated id, complete tracking metadata, and current status for immediate use in order status dashboards and customer notifications. This information is synchronized with the order details and becomes accessible through the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_shipments tables for comprehensive order tracking across the platform.

Security protocols enforce ownership validation ensuring that users can only create tracking records for orders they have access to - sellers for their own orders and customer service representatives for orders under their purview. The system prevents duplicate tracking records and enforces data integrity constraints including mandatory carrier and tracking number fields. This operation supports the critical logistics workflow necessary for accurate delivery estimates and customer satisfaction in the e-commerce platform.

requestBody.description: Tracking information for a new order shipment to be registered in the system.

responseBody.description: Details of the newly created shipping tracking record, including the system-generated tracking identifier and initial status.

operations.description:

The update operation does not trigger any additional system processes or notifications automatically; any customer notifications regarding changes in delivery status must be handled separately by the notification system. The operation ensures that historical tracking information is preserved and new changes are recorded as update events, maintaining a complete audit trail of all tracking modifications.

This endpoint is intended for administrative use only, to correct tracking data from carrier system errors, update delayed deliveries, or update delivery locations based on customer requests. It should not be used for routine delivery status updates as those are handled automatically by carrier webhook integrations.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a shipping tracking record from the system. This operation deletes the record from the shopping_mall_shipping_trackings database table, which contains delivery event logs for shipment tracking.

This data is automatically generated by the system when carriers transmit delivery updates. The system ingests tracking information from shipping carrier APIs and creates records to maintain an audit trail of shipment progress. Manual deletion of these records is not intended for end users or administrators, as this data is critical for compliance, dispute resolution, and operational analytics.

The record deletion performs a hard delete (physical removal from the database) as shipping tracking records are not subject to soft-delete policies. Once deleted, all historical tracking data including timestamps, carrier updates, and location events are irreversibly lost.

This operation should not be exposed to any user actor (customers, sellers, or admins). Shipping tracking records should be considered immutable system-generated audit logs that must be preserved. The system automatically creates these records as shipping providers update shipment status, and the records are used for customer notifications, dispute resolution, and fulfillment analytics.

Any attempt to manually delete shipping tracking records would violate record integrity and potentially compromise compliance with shipping regulations and consumer protection laws. This endpoint is intentionally disabled at the authorization level to prevent accidental or malicious deletion of operational data.

Each response returns a structured paginated result containing the total count of matching records, current page number, items per page, and the actual shipment data arranged according to the specified sorting criteria.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive tracking information based on the requesting user's authorization level. The operation validates that the associated order exists, has been paid, and contains at least one item, ensuring only eligible orders are shipped.

Security considerations include restricting access to authenticated sellers or system-generated processes, as customers cannot directly create shipment records. The operation ensures shipment data integrity by locking inventory counts and capturing the exact shipping address, product quantities, and pricing information at time of creation to prevent post-shipment disputes.

This operation directly interacts with the shopping_mall_order_shipments table in the database, integrating with the shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_carriers, and shopping_mall_shipping_methods entities. operations.description:
Create a new product review submission in the shopping mall platform. This operation allows authenticated customers to submit textual feedback and star ratings for products they have purchased, contributing to the platform's community-driven product evaluation system.

The review is associated with a specific product variant through the product_id field and must reference a completed order to ensure review authenticity. This prevents users from leaving reviews for products they have not actually purchased, maintaining the integrity of the customer feedback system.

Security and integrity mechanisms include automatic verification of purchase history through the order management system. Only customers who have successfully completed an order containing the target product variant are permitted to submit reviews. The review submission flow requires the customer to be authenticated and active, preventing anonymous or suspended accounts from posting reviews.

The review submission triggers automated content moderation workflows that check for inappropriate language, spam patterns, or policy violations before making the review visible to other users. Moderation actions include flagging for human review, auto-rejection, or automatic approval based on predefined criteria.

The operation enforces business validation rules including minimum character length for review text, maximum rating value of 5 stars, and limits on review submission frequency within 24-hour periods to prevent review flooding. All submissions are time-stamped and linked to the submitting user's account for audit purposes.

This review system supports customer decision-making by providing authentic social proof and product insights. The data generated feeds into seller performance analytics and product improvement initiatives. Other operations that interact with this functionality include PATCH /reviews (to search reviews), PUT /reviews/{id} (to update reviews), and DELETE /reviews/{id} (to delete reviews).

Permanently remove a product review from the system. This operation deletes the review record from the shopping_mall_reviews table in the database schema and immediately removes all associated data including reviews, flags, votes, replies, and images.

The deletion is performed as a hard delete (permanent removal) since the shopping_mall_reviews table does not contain a soft_delete_column or similar soft-deletion tracking field. There is no recovery mechanism for deleted reviews; once removed, the data is irretrievably erased from the system.

This operation is only accessible to administrators due to the sensitive nature of content moderation and the potential for abuse. The system ensures that only users with admin privileges can invoke this deletion operation to prevent malicious removal of legitimate customer feedback.

When a review is deleted, the system automatically removes all dependent records from the following tables in a single transaction: shopping_mall_review_flags, shopping_mall_review_images, shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs, shopping_mall_review_replies, and shopping_mall_review_votes. This maintains referential integrity and prevents orphaned records from cluttering the database.

Security and compliance: The deletion action is logged in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table with the admin's identity, timestamp, and the review ID that was deleted. This audit trail ensures regulatory compliance with content moderation guidelines and provides an audit path for reviewing moderation decisions.

Related operations: List all reviews (PATCH /reviews), get single review (GET /reviews/{reviewId}), create review (POST /reviews).

Each vote record indicates whether a user found the review helpful (upvote) or not helpful (downvote), with the vote type stored as a boolean value in the is_helpful field. The system tracks the timestamp of each vote and links it to the voting user. This data is crucial for review quality measurement, identifying influential reviews, and preventing review manipulation through vote stacking or spam.

Security: Only authenticated users can view review votes. The operation returns all votes regardless of the viewer's own vote status, maintaining transparency of community sentiment. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of vote enumeration. This operation is read-only and does not modify any data.

This operation is dependent on the shopping_mall_review_votes table which contains direct relationships to the shopping_mall_review_votes and shopping_mall_review_votes entities through foreign keys. Votes are not duplicated, ensuring data integrity. The reviewId parameter provides the context for filtering votes to only those associated with the specified review.

operations.description:
Create a new vote on a product review. This operation allows any authenticated user to vote on an existing review, either upvoting or downvoting it to help surface the most helpful feedback. The operation applies to the shoppingMall review votes table, which tracks individual user votes against review IDs.

The vote type is determined by the request body, which must specify either "up" or "down". The user performing the vote is automatically identified from their authentication token. Each user can cast only one vote per review; if a user votes again, their previous vote is overridden.

Security considerations include authenticating the requesting user and ensuring they have permission to vote on the review (any authenticated user can vote). Users cannot vote on reviews they themselves authored. The system prevents duplicate voting from the same user on the same review by overwriting previous votes, which maintains data integrity and prevents vote manipulation.

This operation integrates with both the shoppingMall reviews and shoppingMall review votes tables. When a vote is submitted, the vote count in the corresponding review is automatically recalculated in the background to maintain accurate reputation metrics.

Related operations: GET /shoppingMall/reviews/{reviewId}/votes retrieves current vote status and count for a review.

Failure cases: 
- Attempting to vote on a non-existent review with status 404
- Submitting a vote type other than "up" or "down" with status 422
- Trying to vote on a review authored by the same user with status 403
- Unauthenticated access attempts with status 401

Error handling: The system returns appropriately structured error responses with clear validation messages instead of throwing server crashes or returning ambiguous 500 errors.

The operation requires the review to exist in the shopping_mall_reviews table. If the review ID does not exist, the operation will return a 404 error. Flagging a review does not immediately remove it - it initiates a moderation workflow where admins may review, approve, or dismiss the flag.

Security: Only authenticated users can flag reviews. A user can only flag a given review once. Duplicate flags from the same user will be rejected.

The flagging process is designed to discourage abuse: users receive a warning after multiple unjustified reports, and the system tracks flag-to-action ratios to detect malicious behavior.

Related operations: GET /reviews/{reviewId} (to view the flagged review), PATCH /reviews/{reviewId}/replies (for seller responses to review), and GET /admin/reviews/flags for admin moderation.

operations.description:
Flag a review as inappropriate or problematic for moderator review. This operation creates a review flag record in the shopping_mall_review_flags table, associating it with a specific review identified by the reviewId path parameter and the authenticated user.

The flagging mechanism serves as a user-driven moderation system where customers can report offensive, misleading, or inappropriate content. When a user flags a review, the system records the reviewer's identity (from the JWT token), the target review ID, the flag creation timestamp, and any optional comments provided in the request body. This data is stored in the shopping_mall_review_flags table and triggers a review event in the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table for audit purposes.

Security: Only authenticated users can flag reviews. The system checks if the user has already flagged the same review to prevent duplicate flags. Flagging a review does not immediately remove it from public view; reviews remain visible until a moderator reviews and acts on the flag.

Business logic: The operation validates that the target review ID exists and belongs to the same platform context. It prevents users from flagging reviews they authored themselves to avoid abuse of the system. Each well-intentioned flag contributes to the platform's content moderation quality and ensures a trustworthy review ecosystem. Related operations: GET /reviews/{reviewId} to view the review being flagged, and PATCH /reviews to search for reviews with active flags.

Moderators can then use the shopping_mall_review_flags and shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs to see which reviews have been flagged, by whom, and for what reason, enabling efficient content moderation workflows.

operations.description:
Delete a review flag from the system. This operation permanently removes a flag that was previously raised on a specific review by an authenticated user.

The flag represents user-initiated feedback indicating a review may violate community guidelines or contains inappropriate content. When a flag is deleted, it removes the user's specific flagging action from the system but does not affect the underlying review itself.

This is an administrative action that reflects user participation in content moderation. Only the user who originally created the flag may delete their own flag. Once deleted, the flag count on the review decreases by one, and the flagging record is removed from the system with no trace.

Email verification is not required for admin accounts, as administrative access requires additional security controls.

Security considerations include enforcing strong password complexity requirements, rate limiting create attempts to prevent brute force attacks, and logging all admin creation events in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table for compliance purposes. Only super-administrators with elevated privileges can create new admin accounts, as this action grants access to system-level controls that could compromise platform integrity if misused.

All configuration values are stored in the shopping_mall_platform_configurations database table, which tracks key-value pairs with versioning and change history.

The operation requires administrative authentication and validates all configuration keys against a predefined set of allowed configuration parameters. Each configuration setting includes a name, value, description, and optional metadata such as environment scope (development, staging, production). This ensures platform consistency across different deployment environments.

Configuration changes are automatically logged in the shopping_mall_config_history table with audit details including the admin user responsible, timestamp, and the old and new values. These logs provide a complete audit trail for compliance and rollback purposes.

The system enforces configuration validation rules based on data types and format requirements. For example, boolean values must be true/false, numeric values must be within specified ranges, and string values must follow defined patterns. Invalid configurations are rejected with specific error messages that guide administrators to correct their input.

This API operation integrates with the platform's configuration management lifecycle, allowing administrators to deploy configuration changes that take effect immediately or after scheduled rollouts. The operation supports both individual setting creation and batch configuration updates through multiple requests.

This endpoint allows authorized administrators to update system-wide configuration values such as payment processing timeouts, shipping rate calculation rules, feature flags, and other platform-wide operational parameters. Configuration changes are applied immediately and affect all user interactions with the platform. The operation validates that all configuration keys exist in the predefined configuration schema and rejects attempts to modify protected or non-configurable properties.

All configuration updates are logged in the platform's audit trail with the administrator's identity, timestamp, and the specific changes made. A comprehensive validation process ensures that updated values meet the required data types and constraints (e.g., numeric ranges, boolean values, URL formats). Changes to critical settings like payment gateway timeouts or security policies trigger immediate system validation before being applied.

This operation is the primary mechanism for deploying platform-wide updates without requiring code deployment. Configuration values are cached in memory for high-performance access, and a refresh mechanism ensures all service instances synchronize with the updated configuration within milliseconds. operations.description:
Retrieve a specific platform configuration value by its unique key from the shoppingMall platform configurations system. This operation queries the shopping_mall_platform_configurations table in the database and returns the configuration's value, type, description, and metadata. The configuration key serves as the primary identifier and must be exactly matched to retrieve the configuration. Each configuration entry contains a unique, case-sensitive key string, a value of any type stored as JSON, a description field explaining its purpose, and metadata including creation and modification timestamps.

Platform configurations are used to manage global and dynamic system settings without requiring code deployments, allowing administrators to modify behavior such as feature flags, payment processing limits, shipping thresholds, or UI display rules. This endpoint enables administrators and services to fetch configuration values at runtime where the key is known.

The operation returns only the first matching record for the specified configKey. If the key does not exist in the database, a 404 Not Found response will be returned. Configuration values are not cached at the database level but may be cached at the service level for performance. The configuration value is returned in its original JSON structure to maintain type fidelity, including nested objects and arrays.

This operation does not require authentication for public configurations, but private or sensitive configuration values (such as API secrets or internal service credentials) require admin authorization to prevent exposure. The system implements a role-based access control system where each configuration entry has an associated visibility level. Public configurations are accessible by any client, while protected configurations require admin role verification.

The platform uses these configurations for runtime control of features such as:
- Enabling/disabling marketing promotions
- Adjusting rate limits for API endpoints
- Configuring tax calculation rules by region
- Setting default shipping thresholds
- Controlling product availability flags
- Managing maintenance mode status

This operation should be called only when dynamic configuration values need to be retrieved at runtime, not for static application settings which should be managed through environment variables and deployed configurations.

parameters.name: configKey
parameters.description:
Unique case-sensitive key identifier of the platform configuration to retrieve. Must exactly match the config_key field in the shopping_mall_platform_configurations table. Used as a primary lookup key.

Examples:
- "feature_flag.new_checkout_ui"
- "shipping.max_weight_limit"
- "payment.currencies.enabled"
- "system.maintenance_mode"

The key string may contain alphanumeric characters, dots, underscores, and hyphens. No spaces or special characters are allowed. Keys are not case-insensitive, so 'FeatureFlag' and 'featureflag' are treated as different keys.

responseBody.description: The configuration value object matching the specified configKey. Includes complete configuration details including its value, description, and system metadata. The response structure is designed to return configuration values with their original JSON types preserved, allowing for complex structures such as objects, arrays, and nested values.

operations.description:
Create a new security policy for the shoppingMall platform. This operation allows authorized administrators to define and register new security policies that govern system behavior, access controls, and risk mitigation protocols. Security policies are stored in the shopping_mall_security_policies table, which contains fields for policy name, description, scope, enforcement level, effective dates, and associated compliance standards.

This operation is restricted to admin actors only since security policies define system-wide rules and require elevated privileges. The policy name must be unique across the platform, and the system will automatically validate that no duplicates exist. The policy description must provide sufficient detail to ensure consistent interpretation and implementation across the organization.

Security implications are significant: policies define who can access what data, under what conditions, and with what audit requirements. Violations of policy terms trigger automated alerts and potential account suspensions. Policies may govern data retention, encryption standards, authentication requirements, and third-party integration restrictions.

The operation requires precise input validation: policy_name must not be empty, scope must be from predefined values (system-wide, user-level, payment-related), and enforcement_level must be one of "mandatory", "recommended", or "optional". Policies with "mandatory" enforcement trigger automated system changes, while "recommended" policies generate advisory notifications.

Related operations: GET /security/policies (list all), GET /security/policies/{policyId} (view detail), PUT /security/policies/{policyId} (update), DELETE /security/policies/{policyId} (permanent deletion).
operations.name: create

requestBody.description: Definition of the security policy to be created including name, description, scope, enforcement level, effective dates, and compliance standards.

responseBody.description: The newly created security policy object with its assigned ID and system-generated metadata.

operations.description:
Retrieve filtered and paginated compliance records for security audit purposes. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_compliance_records table and provides advanced filtering by status, audit type, and time range. The operation supports full pagination with configurable page sizes, sorting by timestamp or severity, and detailed filtering capabilities.

Compliance records capture system audits, control violations, governance events, and regulatory compliance actions. Each record includes metadata about the actor who triggered the event, timestamp, severity level, and detailed description. This endpoint is essential for security teams conducting forensic analysis, compliance reviews, and auditing historical system behavior.

Security is paramount for this endpoint. Only users with the admin role can access compliance records, ensuring sensitive audit data is protected from unauthorized access. All requests are subject to rate limiting to prevent abuse. The statistics returned by this endpoint are used for generating compliance reports and monitoring adherence to internal and external regulatory frameworks.

This operation is critical for maintaining system integrity and regulatory compliance. The operation integrates directly with the shopping_mall_compliance_records table as defined in the database schema, incorporating all available fields and using the database's built-in indexing for optimal performance during filtering and querying. This endpoint does not modify any data - it is strictly a read operation for audit and compliance review purposes.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for compliance record filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of compliance record summaries matching search criteria

operations.description:
Create a compliance record in the system to document adherence to regulatory requirements and internal policies. This operation captures and validates critical compliance information for auditing and reporting purposes. Each record is automatically associated with the authenticated user and current timestamp.

The compliance record system tracks adherence to regulatory standards including data privacy, financial reporting, operational controls, and security protocols. This system ensures organizational compliance and provides audit-ready documentation for regulatory bodies.

Data integrity is paramount - all compliance records are immutable once created and cannot be modified or deleted. The system maintains a historical audit trail of all compliance activities. This operation validates that required fields are provided and that compliance metadata conforms to established standards.

Related operations:
- GET /compliance/records/{id} - Retrieve specific compliance record
- PATCH /compliance/records - Search compliance records by criteria
- GET /compliance/records/export - Export compliance records for audit purposes

requestBody.description: Compliance record creation payload containing required regulatory and operational information

responseBody.description: Created compliance record with system-generated metadata

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete audit history of system configuration changes for administrative review and compliance purposes. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_config_history table which stores immutable records of all configuration modifications including the actor who made the change, timestamp, old and new values, and the configuration key affected.

The operation returns a paginated list of configuration change records ordered by timestamp in descending order (newest first). Administrators can filter by configuration key, date range, or actor to narrow results. Each record contains the exact change details including the configuration path, original value, new value, and metadata about the environment and user context.

Security: This endpoint is exclusively accessible to admin actors as configuration history contains sensitive system state information. The operation does not permit any modification of history records - they are immutable by design to maintain audit integrity.

This operation complements the system's configuration management workflow where configuration changes are first validated by the platform and then permanently logged in the shopping_mall_config_history table. Others can be monitored using the GET /config endpoint to view current configuration values.

Implementation note: This endpoint leverages the shopping_mall_config_history table's structure which includes fields: id, config_key, old_value, new_value, actor, ip_address, user_agent, created_at, and metadata. The response includes all these fields to provide complete context about each configuration change.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search and pagination parameters for filtering configuration history records. This enables administrators to find specific configuration changes by key, date range, actor, or other metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated result set containing configuration change records with full audit details including configuration key, old/new values, actor information, and timestamp.

operations.description:
Generate and retrieve data exports from the shopping mall platform. This operation allows platform administrators and authorized users to request comprehensive data exports for analytics, integration, auditing, or reporting purposes.

The operation is designed to handle large-scale data export requests, supporting advanced filtering by time range, data types, and entities. Requested exports are processed asynchronously and made available for download via a generated URI in the response body. Multiple export types are supported including customer data, order histories, product catalogs, and analytics metrics.

Security considerations include role-based access control to ensure only authorized users can request sensitive data exports. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse and excessive resource consumption. All requested exports are subject to platform retention and data privacy policies.

The operation interacts with the shopping_mall_data_exports database table and triggers background processing jobs to generate export files. Successive calls with identical parameters will return the same pre-generated export if available, while new requests are queued for processing. Related operations include GET /data/exports/{id} to retrieve specific export metadata and DELETE /data/exports/{id} to remove completed exports.

requestBody.description: Specification for data export generation including filters, format preferences, and scope parameters.

responseBody.description: Metadata about the generated data export including status, URI for download, and details about generated content.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Initiate a new data export job for the shopping mall platform. This operation triggers the creation of a data export job based on the specified parameters, including target data entities, filtering criteria, and delivery preferences. The operation performs no direct database write but initiates an asynchronous background process that queries data from multiple tables including shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_sales, then compiles them according to the specified export format (CSV, JSON, or Excel).

The operation requires no authentication for public exports requested by system administrators, but when initiated by sellers or customers, it must be scoped to their respective data. The background process generates a unique identifier for the export job and returns it in the response, allowing clients to poll the /data/exports/{id} endpoint for status updates. The export job may take minutes to hours depending on data volume, and the system will send email notifications upon completion based on user preferences stored in shopping_mall_customer_email_preferences.

Security implications include ensuring that users can only export data they have permission to access (e.g., customers only exporting their own orders, sellers only exporting their product catalog). The operation enforces authorization at the business logic layer by intersecting the provided export filters with the authenticated user's data scope rather than at the API endpoint level. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse, with a maximum of 5 concurrent exports per user.

This operation integrates with the data export pipeline built on the shopping_mall_data_exports table, which tracks export job metadata including status (pending, processing, completed, failed), timestamps, format specifications, file paths, and error logs. It also references the shopping_mall_configurations table to determine global export size limits and allowed output formats. The system does not store full exported data in the database but only metadata about the export, while the actual files are stored in the S3-compatible object storage system.

Related operations: GET /data/exports/{exportId} for status checking, GET /data/exports for listing recent jobs, and DELETE /data/exports/{exportId} for cancellation.

requestBody.description: Configuration parameters for the new data export job.

responseBody.description: Status and reference information for the newly created data export job.
