operations.description:
Retrieve paginated monitoring alerts with filtering, sorting, and search capabilities. This operation is based on the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts database table and enables administrators to analyze system health events, performance issues, and security alerts.

The endpoint supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Alert records can be filtered by severity level, event type, timestamp range, and source component. Text search is available across message content and metadata fields.

Security considerations include rate limiting for administrative search operations and strict authorization controls. Only system administrators can access monitoring alerts, as they contain sensitive system status and potential security incident information. Alert data is never exposed to regular users or sellers.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table, incorporating all available fields including alert_id, severity, event_type, message, source_component, triggered_at, resolved_at, and metadata. The response includes summary information optimized for administrative dashboards, with options to include additional details based on authorization scope.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for alert filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of monitoring alert summary information matching search criteria

operations.description:
Retrieve or update the user's system flags for the shopping mall application. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_user_flags table and enables users to toggle or modify system-controlled flags that affect their experience and permissions. Flags can include preferences like notification settings, display preferences, or system-restricted toggles.

The operation accepts a list of flag updates through the request body, allowing users to modify multiple flags in a single request. Each flag has a defined name and boolean or string value that the system interprets based on business rules. For example, a flag named "disableNotifications" when set to true would suppress all system notifications for that user.

Security considerations include ensuring users can only modify their own flags and preventing unauthorized access to system-critical flag values. The operation validates flag names against a predefined set of allowed flags to prevent injection or abuse. If a flag name is not recognized, the system will ignore it and return a warning in the response.

This operation is critical for personalization and user control. It replaces multiple individual API calls for flag management with a single, efficient batch update mechanism. Related operations: GET /user/flags retrieves current flag states without modification.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Collection of user flag updates to apply. Each flag is identified by a name and should contain the new value to set. The system validates flag names against allowed values and applies changes based on user permissions.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of which flags were successfully updated and any warnings about unrecognized or unchangeable flag names. Includes success status, updated flags, and any errors encountered during processing.

operations.description:
Create a new user flag to denote specific status or condition for a user's account. This operation allows authenticated users to create flags that will be used for internal system tracking and administrative review. The flag is stored in the shopping_mall_user_flags table and linked to the authenticated user's ID from the JWT token.

The flag must be created with a valid flag key and optional description. The flag key is a predefined enumeration representing specific user states such as suspicious_activity, policy_violation, or account_alert. Only one flag of the same key per user can be active due to the database's composite unique constraint on (user_id, flag_key). This prevents duplicate flag entries while allowing multiple different flags per user.

Security: Only authenticated users can create flags on their own accounts. The user ID in the flag record is automatically populated from the JWT token authentication context and cannot be spoofed. Admins can view these flags for moderation purposes, but users cannot view or modify flags created by other users. Rate limiting applies to prevent spam flag creation.

This system enforces that flags are temporary markers for review purposes and do not immediately change user permissions or access levels.

Related Operations: GET /user/flags to retrieve active user flags, DELETE /user/flags/{flagId} to remove a user flag (admin only).
operations.name: create

requestBody.description: Creation data for a new user flag including the flag key and optional description.

responseBody.description: The newly created user flag record with system-generated metadata including ID and creation timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific audit log entry from the system's audit trail.

This operation retrieves a single audit log record from the shopping_mall_audit_logs table based on its unique identifier. Audit logs are automatically generated by the system as part of its security and compliance framework, recording all significant user and system actions including login events, configuration changes, user management activities, and administrative operations.

The system automatically generates these audit logs without requiring any external API calls for creation. Each log entry includes the timestamp of the event, the action performed, the actor responsible (user or system), the affected resource identifier, the client IP address, and a detailed description of the event. This immutable log serves as a critical security and compliance artifact that helps identify unauthorized access, troubleshoot system issues, and maintain regulatory compliance with data protection regulations.

The logId parameter uniquely identifies the specific audit record to be retrieved. Since audit logs are system-generated records, they are read-only and cannot be modified, created, or deleted by any API endpoint. Any attempt to modify or delete audit logs would violate system integrity and compliance requirements. This operation is specifically designed for administrative review, forensic analysis, and compliance auditing purposes, not for user-facing interactions.

Access to audit logs is restricted to administrative users only. The system generates these records automatically as side effects of other operations and they are preserved for compliance and security monitoring. This API endpoint provides a mechanism for administrators to review historical actions performed on the system, helping to detect suspicious behavior, investigate security incidents, and meet audit requirements. The operation returns only the exact record identified by the logId, preserving the integrity of the audit trail.

parameters.name: logId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the audit log entry to retrieve. This corresponds to the id field in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table and is used to locate the specific audit record.

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the single audit log entry identified by the logId parameter.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific email template by its unique identifier from the shopping_mall_email_templates database table. This operation allows administrators to access pre-defined email templates used for system communications such as order confirmations, password resets, and promotional announcements.

The template is identified by a unique template_id that maps directly to the template_id field in the shopping_mall_email_templates table. The system supports both system-generated templates and user-created custom templates, with access controlled by authorization settings.

Response includes the complete template structure: subject line, HTML and plain-text body content, variables used in the template, creation timestamp, and status flags. This data is used by the notification system to dynamically populate and send personalized messages to customers.

Security: Access to email templates is restricted based on user role - only administrators with authorizationActor: "admin" can view templates. The API enforces this authorization through the explicit authorizationActors field configuration, not through implementation-level controls.

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the email template in the shopping_mall_email_templates table. This is the template_id field that uniquely identifies each template record in the database.

responseBody.description: Complete email template structure with all content and metadata.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Update an existing email template in the system. This operation modifies the content, subject, and metadata of an existing email template stored in the shopping_mall_email_templates database table. The template can only be updated by administrators with full rights to the email system.

This operation replaces the entire template record with the new data provided in the request body. The template_id parameter in the URL must match an existing template in the database system. The operation validates the template exists before applying changes and ensures that sensitive fields like the template key and system identifier are not modified.

Security: This operation requires admin authorization to prevent unauthorized modification of email system templates. The system automatically logs this administrative action for compliance purposes as part of its internal audit trail, which is generated by the backend service and not through direct API calls. No user-facing actors are permitted to invoke this endpoint.

Response: The updated template object is returned in the response body, containing the complete modified record with updated timestamps and unchanged system identifiers. The operation does not trigger email delivery; it only updates the template definition.

Related operations: GET /email/templates/{templateId} for fetching a single template, GET /email/templates for listing all templates, and POST /email/templates for creating new templates.
operations.name: update

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the email template to be updated (global scope)

requestBody.description: Updated content and metadata for the email template

responseBody.description: The complete updated email template record

prerequisites.description: Email template must be created before it can be updated

operations.description:
Permanently removes an email template from the system's template library. This operation directly affects the shopping_mall_email_templates table in the database and performs a hard delete, removing the template record completely from persistent storage. No backup or recovery mechanism exists for deleted templates, and this action cannot be undone.

This deletion operation is restricted to administrative users only, as email templates are critical system configuration assets that influence all customer communications. The template is identified by its unique identifier (templateId), which references the primary key in the shopping_mall_email_templates table.

After successful deletion, the template is permanently removed from all systems and cannot be retrieved. This operation does not affect any emails that were already sent using this template, but future references to this template will return a 404 error. The system logs this deletion event in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table for compliance and audit purposes, recording the actor, timestamp, and template ID involved in the deletion.
operations.name: erase

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the email template to be deleted. This corresponds to the primary key in the shopping_mall_email_templates table. The templateId must be a valid UUID string format.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific security policy configuration from the system. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_security_policies database table and returns detailed configuration settings for a particular policy identified by its unique policy ID.

The security policy system governs access controls, authentication requirements, and compliance standards across the shoppingMall platform. Each policy defines rules for user authentication, session duration, password complexity requirements, multi-factor authentication enforcement, and data retention policies. This endpoint specifically retrieves a single policy record based on its unique identifier, allowing administrators to inspect current policy configurations.

The operation validates that the requested policy exists and returns its complete configuration including policy name, description, and enforcement rules. Only users with administrative privileges can access security policy details, ensuring sensitive configuration data is protected from unauthorized inspection. The response includes all policy parameters that determine how the system enforces security controls for users and transactions on the platform.

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the security policy to retrieve. This identifier corresponds to the policy_id field in the shopping_mall_security_policies database table and is used to locate the specific policy record.

responseBody.description: Complete security policy configuration details including policy name, description, and enforcement rules.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Security policy must be created before it can be retrieved by its ID.

operations.description:
Update a specific security policy in the shoppingMall platform's security management system.

This operation modifies an existing security policy identified by its unique policyId. The security policy defines access rules, authentication requirements, and behavioral constraints for platform operations, ensuring compliance with security standards and regulatory obligations.

The operation requires the admin actor to authenticate and authorize the update, as security policies govern system-wide access and are considered high-impact configuration items. Changes to security policies may affect permissions across the entire platform, requiring elevated privileges.

The policy operations interact with the shopping_mall_security_policies table from the database schema, which contains fields for policy name, description, status, scope, rules, timestamps, and metadata. The operation validates that the policyId matches an existing policy and that the provided update data conforms to validation rules defined in the schema.

Security considerations include audit logging of policy changes, protection against unauthorized modification, and ensuring policy changes maintain system integrity. A comprehensive audit trail is automatically generated to track who made the change, when it occurred, and what modifications were applied.

This operation is closely related to the GET /security/policies/{policyId} endpoint which retrieves policy details, and PATCH /security/policies which lists policies with search and filtering capabilities. Changes made here are immediately effective and affect all subsequent system interactions.
operations.name: update

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the security policy to update

requestBody.description: Updated security policy configuration with all fields to replace current values

responseBody.description: Updated security policy object with all fields after modification

operations.description:
Permanently delete a security policy from the system's enforcement configuration.

This operation removes the specified security policy record from the shopping_mall_security_policies database table. Security policies govern access controls, authentication requirements, and system-wide security configurations that enforce platform integrity. Once deleted, the policy is permanently removed from all enforcement contexts and cannot be recovered.

This is a hard delete operation that physically removes the database record. No soft delete mechanisms are implemented for security policies, as they are critical governing rules that require explicit and permanent revocation to maintain system security posture. Any system components relying on this policy will immediately lose its constraints upon deletion.

This operation requires admin-level authorization because security policies control system-wide security behavior. Deletion affects all users and services that rely on this policy for access control, session management, or threat mitigation. Only system administrators with explicit permissions can execute this action.

Related operations: GET /shoppingMall/admin/security/policies/{policyId} (retrieve policy details), PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/security/policies (list all policies), POST /shoppingMall/admin/security/policies (create new policy).

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific compliance record from the system. This endpoint accesses the shopping_mall_compliance_records table and returns detailed information about a single compliance audit record identified by its unique identifier. The compliance record contains comprehensive details about regulatory checks, audit findings, and compliance status.

This operation supports verification of regulatory compliance for e-commerce platforms and is used to ensure adherence to legal and industry-specific requirements. The response includes the compliance record's identification details, purpose, findings, status, associated audit information, and any related documentation.

Security considerations include appropriate authorization based on user role, since compliance records may contain sensitive information about system operations, user data handling, and regulatory adherence. Only authorized personnel such as administrators and compliance officers may access these records. Rate limiting and audit logging apply to all access attempts for security and accountability purposes.

These compliance records are immutable audit trails. Once created, they cannot be modified or deleted and serve as permanent historical evidence of regulatory compliance.

parameters.name: recordId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target compliance record (global scope)

responseBody.description: Complete compliance record details including identification, purpose, findings, status, related audit information, and documentation references

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Update an existing compliance record in the system.

This operation allows authorized administrators to modify the status and metadata of a compliance record associated with regulatory compliance tracking. The compliance record contains details about audits, policy violations, corrective actions, and enforcement history for platform governance.

The operation requires an existing compliance record ID in the path parameter and sends updated field values in the request body. Only users with administrative privileges can invoke this operation. The system enforces strict audit trail requirements: changes to compliance records are automatically logged in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table, capturing the actor who performed the update, timestamp, IP address, and old/new values.

The record is never deleted from the system; instead, its status may be updated from 'pending_review', 'violated', 'corrected', or 'archived' to reflect its current governance state. All updates must include a justification field explaining the reason for the change, which is required for audit compliance. The updated record must maintain historical consistency: any changes to date fields must not precede the record's original creation date.

This operation is part of the platform's compliance management subsystem and interfaces directly with the shopping_mall_compliance_records table. Related operations include: GET /compliance/records/{recordId} (retrieve single record), PATCH /compliance/records (search records), and GET /compliance/records/{recordId}/audit (view audit history).

parameters.name: recordId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the compliance record to be updated. This value identifies a specific entry in the shopping_mall_compliance_records table.

requestBody.description: Updated fields and metadata for the compliance record.

responseBody.description: The updated compliance record with its new state and timestamps.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: Compliance record must be created before it can be updated, as the update operation requires an existing record with a valid ID.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a compliance record from the system's audit trail. This operation directly deletes the compliance record from the shopping_mall_compliance_records table in the database.

The operation removes the record identified by the provided recordId parameter. This is a hard delete operation that completely removes all record data from the database with no possibility of recovery.

Security: This operation is restricted to admin actors only, ensuring that only authorized personnel with appropriate privileges can delete compliance records. The deletion is not reversible and will remove all associated metadata, timestamps, and audit information.

This operation is designed to support regulatory compliance requirements where records may need to be permanently removed under specific legal circumstances.

Related operations: GET /compliance/records/{recordId} (view record), GET /compliance/records (list records).
operations.name: erase

parameters.name: recordId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the compliance record to be permanently deleted

prerequisites.description: A compliance record must be created before it can be deleted to ensure the target resource exists in the system. This prerequisite validates that the compliance record has been properly established in the database as the first step in its lifecycle.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific configuration history entry from the platform's audit trail. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_config_history table which records all administrative changes to system-wide configurations, including feature flags, payment settings, shipping rules, and other platform-wide parameters.

Each history entry contains the exact configuration state at the time of change, the actor who made the change, timestamp, IP address, and a description of the modification. This allows administrators to audit changes, understand the evolution of platform settings, and rollback to previous configurations when needed.

The operation is read-only and does not modify any system data. Each history entry is immutable and retained for compliance purposes, with no soft delete capability. Access to configuration history is restricted to admin roles to maintain security and prevent unauthorized auditing.

This operation supports precise retrieval by the history entry's unique identifier, ensuring that administrators can quickly investigate specific configuration changes without needing to filter through the entire history log. The response returns the complete configuration state as it existed at the time of change, enabling accurate recreation of past system states when troubleshooting or performing compliance reviews.

parameters.name: historyId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the configuration history entry to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Complete configuration history entry including the configuration state at time of change, actor details, and metadata.

operations.name: at

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific data export record from the system's data export management system. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_data_exports table which stores metadata and status information about generated data exports for reporting, analytics, and data migration purposes.

The system maintains a comprehensive audit trail for all data exports, including the requester, export format, generation timestamp, file location, size, and status details. This endpoint provides access to a single export record by its unique identifier, allowing administrators to monitor export progress, retrieve export metadata, and access generated files through provided URLs.

operations.description:
Process incoming payment webhook events from payment gateways for transaction status updates and reconciliation.

This operation receives asynchronous notifications from external payment providers (Stripe, PayPal, Adyen, etc.) when payment status changes, including successful captures, declines, refunds, chargebacks, and authorization failures. Each webhook event includes payment intent ID, transaction ID, status, amount, currency, and payment method details.

The system validates the webhook signature using the registered provider secret, confirms the payment intent exists in the system, and updates the payment record with the new status. The operation ensures idempotency by rejecting duplicate events with the same transaction ID. For failed payments, the system automatically initiates retry logic based on configured policies.

Security: All webhook requests must be signed using the provider's secret key stored in payment_settings. Invalid signatures result in immediate rejection with HTTP 401. The system logs all webhook events for audit purposes and triggers appropriate notifications to customers and sellers.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table as defined in the database schema, which records all incoming webhook payloads with their validation status and processing history. The operation updates the associated payment intent record in the shopping_mall_payment_intents table based on the received status. Related operations: Payment intent creation (POST /payments/intents), Payment status retrieval (GET /payments/{paymentId}).

requestBody.description: Webhook payload from payment provider containing payment status update and transaction details.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of webhook processing with status and updated payment ID.

Receive and process webhook notifications from payment gateways and external services. This operation receives HTTP POST requests containing event payloads from external systems like payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal, etc.) and system integrations.

Upon receipt, the system validates the webhook signature and triggers corresponding business logic based on the event type (e.g., payment succeeded, subscription canceled, refund processed). The webhook endpoint is designed to be idempotent and fault-tolerant, with built-in retry logic and signature verification.

All incoming webhooks are automatically logged to the system's audit records for traceability.

The response is always HTTP 200 OK with empty body to acknowledge receipt and prevent webhook provider from retrying. Any error response status triggers automatic retry logic at the webhook provider.

Retrieve a specific payment webhook event record from the system's transaction notification logs. This operation queries the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks database table, which captures all webhook delivery attempts, including request payloads, response statuses, retry counts, and delivery timestamps.

The webhook event contains critical integration metadata for system-to-system communication between the shoppingMall platform and external payment processors, ERP systems, and fulfillment services. Each webhook represents a single delivery attempt of an event notification (e.g., payment_completed, order_shipped) to a registered endpoint URL.

System security requires that only administrative users can view webhook records, as these contain potentially sensitive system integration details. The operation returns the complete webhook record including payload, response headers, and delivery status for troubleshooting and debugging purposes. Admins can use this endpoint to verify that webhook deliveries have been successfully processed by external systems and diagnose integration failures.

When requesting a webhook by its ID, the system validates the existence of the specific webhook record in the database and returns it with all attributes. No pagination or filtering is supported for this single-record retrieval endpoint. The webhook ID is a UUID string that uniquely identifies the webhook record after creation by the system during event delivery attempts.

Related operations:
- PATCH /webhooks - List all webhook delivery attempts with search and pagination
- DEL /webhooks/{id} - Delete a webhook record by ID (administrative maintenance)
- GET /webhooks/{id}/resend - Resend a specific webhook delivery

The operation targets the shopping_mall_payment_webhooks table which records webhook endpoints configured to receive asynchronous notifications about payment events such as successful transactions, refund confirmations, processing failures, and dispute status changes. Each webhook entry has a URL endpoint, event type filters, authentication mechanism, active status, and metadata tracking when it was created and last modified.

This is not an audit or logging operation - it's a configuration update of an active notification mechanism. Only system administrators or privileged agents can update webhooks to prevent unauthorized endpoint manipulation which could compromise payment security. The update allows for changes to the target URL, enabled event types, authentication tokens, or activation state.

This operation relates directly to the webhook management workflow where platform administrators or technical integrators need to modify webhook configurations in response to changing payment processor requirements, server migrations, or security policy updates.

Security consideration: The webhook URL must be a valid HTTPS endpoint to ensure encrypted communication with the payment gateway. The authentication headers must follow secure token standards. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of webhook configuration updates.

operations.description:
Perform a unified global search across all products, product reviews, and categories on the shoppingMall platform. This operation aggregates search results from multiple data sources and returns a combined, paginated response optimized for consumer discovery.

This endpoint supports searching across product titles, descriptions, tags, brand names, category names, and product review contents. The search leverages full-text indexing on product catalog data and review text for performance. Search results are ranked by relevance, with product title matches weighted highest, followed by description matches, and category matches.

Security: This is a public endpoint with no authentication required. All results are filtered to show only approved products with available inventory and approved reviews. Seller-specific or personally identifiable information is never exposed in search results.

Implementation note: This operation does not map to a single database table. Instead, it performs a UNION query over three source tables:
1. shopping_mall_products (for product metadata, including title, description, brand, category)
2. shopping_mall_product_reviews (for review content, product association)
3. shopping_mall_categories (for category names and descriptions)

The results are combined into a unified format with a type discriminator to indicate the source of each result. Product results include product ID, title, brand, primary category, price range, and average rating. Review results include the review content, rating, and associated product ID. Category results include category name and description. This guarantees return of relevant data from all searchable entities.

The operation supports pagination with configurable page size, sorting by relevance (default), newest, or highest rated, and automatic highlighting of search terms in result snippets.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} for retrieving detailed product information, PATCH /products for category-specific product search, and GET /reviews/{reviewId} for reviewing individual feedback.

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive administrative dashboard overview displaying key system metrics and aggregated statistics for platform management. This operation consolidates data from multiple system tables including admins, customers, sellers, products, orders, and payments to provide a holistic view of platform health and activity.

The operation synthesizes real-time data from various system tables to generate a unified dashboard view for system administrators. Key metrics include total count of active administrators, registered customers, and active sellers, providing visibility into platform user base growth and distribution. Order and payment statistics display total transaction volume, completed order count, and revenue figures, ensuring administrators can monitor business performance and financial health.

The system maintains audit trail integrity through secure data aggregation - no individual user records are disclosed, only aggregated counts and summary metrics. This prevents privacy violations while enabling effective platform management. The data is refreshed in real-time to reflect current system status without requiring manual refreshes or periodic jobs.

The operation integrates with the shopping_mall_admins table to provide administrator count, shopping_mall_customers to provide customer count, shopping_mall_sellers for seller count, shopping_mall_products for product inventory count, shopping_mall_orders for order statistics, and shopping_mall_payments for financial metrics. All values are derived directly from the database schema definitions with appropriate aggregations.

Due to the sensitive nature of administrator data, access is strictly limited to users with admin privileges. The operation ensures no cross-privilege data leakage and follows the principle of least privilege in information disclosure. Response structure is optimized for dashboard rendering with minimal network overhead using pre-calculated aggregates rather than raw data.

Related operations: GET /admin/users, GET /admin/orders, GET /admin/reports, GET /admin/settings - these provide more granular views of the data aggregated here.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Aggregated administrative dashboard statistics including user counts, product inventory, order volume, and financial metrics.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated sales statistics for products across the shopping mall platform. This operation computes product-level sales analytics by aggregating data from the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table, which tracks sales volume, revenue, and customer engagement metrics for each product.

The operation provides comprehensive analytics for product performance, including total units sold, total revenue generated, average price per unit, and unique customers who purchased each product. The results are grouped by product and can be filtered by date range, category, brand, or other relevant dimensions.

Data is sourced exclusively from the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table, which aggregates sales data from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables. This prevents direct query of high-transaction tables and maintains system performance. The results are computed on-demand through a complex SQL aggregation that joins product information from shopping_mall_products with sales metrics.

Security considerations include rate limiting for analytics endpoints and data access restrictions based on user roles. Only authenticated users with administrative privileges (admin) can access this endpoint due to the sensitive nature of sales metrics and business intelligence.

This operation is designed to support dashboard visualizations, business intelligence reporting, and inventory decision-making. It complements other product operations including GET /shopping-mall/products for detailed product information and GET /shopping-mall/products/{productCode} for individual product retrieval.

responseBody.description: Aggregated sales statistics for products with key performance indicators

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive product analytics metrics for the shoppingMall platform, aggregating sales performance and customer viewing behavior across all products.

This operation computes aggregated statistics from the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats and shopping_mall_product_view_stats database tables to provide administrators with insights into product popularity, conversion rates, and market performance. The system combines sales data (total units sold, revenue generated) with view data (total views, unique viewers) to calculate key performance indicators such as conversion rate and sales per view.

Security considerations: This analytics endpoint is restricted to admin actors only because it exposes sensitive business intelligence that could inform competitive strategies or internal pricing decisions. All data is aggregated and does not reveal personally identifiable customer information. The operation is designed to be read-only and does not modify any underlying data.

Implementation notes: This endpoint does NOT map to a single database table. Instead, it executes two parallel aggregate queries:

1. SELECT
   SUM(units_sold) AS total_sales,
   SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue,
   COUNT(*) AS total_products_analyzed
FROM shopping_mall_product_sales_stats

2. SELECT
   SUM(total_views) AS total_views,
   SUM(unique_viewers) AS unique_viewers,
   AVG(view_duration_seconds) AS avg_view_duration
FROM shopping_mall_product_view_stats

The results are then combined into a single JSON response structure optimized for dashboard visualization.

Related operations: GET /analytics/products/top-sellers (returns ranked list), PATCH /analytics/products/trends (returns time-series data with date filtering), GET /products/{productId}/details (detailed view of single product).

responseBody.description: Comprehensive product analytics dashboard metrics containing aggregated sales and view statistics across all products

operations.description:
Perform a comprehensive search across all products in the shopping mall catalog using advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination. This operation queries the shopping_mall_products table and its associated entities including shopping_mall_categories, shopping_mall_product_attributes, shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes, shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, shopping_mall_product_images, shopping_mall_product_tags, shopping_mall_product_sales_stats, and shopping_mall_product_view_stats to deliver relevant product results.

The search is designed to handle complex user queries with multiple filter criteria including category hierarchy navigation, attribute value matching, price range constraints, stock availability status, and keyword-based text matching across product names, descriptions, and tags. The operation supports sophisticated sorting by relevance, price, rating, sales volume, or newest first.

For pagination, the service implements cursor-based paging with configurable page sizes up to 100 items per page. Results are returned as a paginated summary view to optimize performance and reduce bandwidth usage. The operation returns only essential product information intended for display in search result lists.

Security considerations ensure that only products marked as active and visible to the requesting user are returned, applying appropriate permissions based on user role. The system implements query rate limiting to prevent abuse and optimize performance. Order of operations follows parent-to-child relationship logic: categories first, then products, then variants, then pricing and inventory. This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table to incorporate real-time sales data and the shopping_mall_product_view_stats table for popularity-based ranking.

Related operations include: GET /products/{productId} to retrieve full product details after selecting from this search, and PATCH /products/{productId}/inventory to check real-time availability.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of product summary information matching the search criteria.

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive overview of product performance metrics for the e-commerce platform's administrative dashboard.

This operation aggregates data from the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats and shopping_mall_product_view_stats tables to generate a unified view of product performance across key business dimensions. The endpoint provides administrators with critical insights into product popularity, sales efficiency, and customer engagement patterns.

The data refreshes in real-time as new statistics are calculated by the system's analytical engine. Security and performance considerations include caching at the CDN level for frequently accessed products and rate limiting to prevent abuse of this resource-intensive operation. The response structure is optimized for front-end rendering with all necessary display data included, and no additional API calls are required to render the full product page. The operation reads from the database without writing, making it safe for high-volume read operations. Administrators can use this data to identify underperforming variants, detect inventory imbalances, spot pricing anomalies, and ensure comprehensive attribute coverage for product optimization.

This operation does not update or modify any data - it is strictly read-only for monitoring and analysis purposes. The underlying data sources are real-time inventory tracking and variant management systems, where inventory levels are automatically updated through warehouse integrations and sales transactions. Price information is synchronized from the pricing management system, while attribute data is maintained by product catalog teams through the admin interface.

Administrative access is required because variant-level data contains sensitive commercial information including wholesale pricing, competitor pricing comparisons, and inventory positioning strategies. This endpoint supports advanced filtering options, sorting by key metrics like inventory turnover, and pagination to handle the full scope of the product catalog which may contain tens of thousands of variants.

operations.description:
Search for product variants by attribute combinations and pricing criteria across the shopping mall platform.

This operation enables customers and administrators to find specific product variants based on multiple filtering criteria including attribute values (size, color, material), price ranges, availability status, and seller information. The system performs real-time aggregation across the shopping_mall_product_variants, shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes, shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing, and shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory tables to provide relevant results.

The search supports complex querying through a structured request body that allows filtering by multiple attribute-value pairs simultaneously, price ranges (minimum and maximum), inventory status (available, low stock, out of stock), and seller restrictions. Results are returned in paginated format with summary information including variant count, price statistics, and availability indicators.

Security: Only authenticated users can perform advanced variant searches. The operation validates that all requested attribute values exist in the system and are associated with active products. Rate limiting prevents abusive querying patterns.

Implementation note: This operation does not map to a single database table but instead performs a complex SQL JOIN across multiple tables:
1. shopping_mall_product_variants (primary variant records)
2. shopping_mall_product_variant_attributes (attribute-value mappings)
3. shopping_mall_product_variant_pricing (price overrides)
4. shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory (real-time stock levels)
5. shopping_mall_products (to verify product availability)

The system aggregates results while avoiding circular references between variant and product data. This enables users to find variants with specific combinations like 'Size: Large, Color: Blue, Price: $20-$50, In Stock' without requiring separate queries for each dimension.

operations.description:
Merge multiple shopping carts into a single consolidated cart.

This operation allows a customer to combine the items from multiple carts (e.g., guest cart and authenticated cart) into a unified shopping cart. The operation identifies duplicate product variants across carts, sums their quantities, and retains the highest quantity when duplicates exist. Any cart items from the source cart that do not already exist in the target cart are added individually.

Security is enforced by verifying the requesting user's ownership of all carts being merged. Only carts associated with the authenticated user can be merged. System validation ensures atomicity of the merge operation—either all cart items are successfully combined, or no changes are made if any validation fails.

The linked shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items database tables define the structure. The shopping_mall_carts table contains cart_id and user_id to determine ownership, while the shopping_mall_cart_items table links cart_id to product_variant_id and tracks quantity and session information. This operation reads from both tables to resolve active cart items.

Related operations: GET /carts to view current cart, POST /carts to create a new cart, and PATCH /carts/{cartId}/items to modify individual cart items.

The merge operation fully supports scenario of guest-to-registered-user conversion: a guest cart (session-based) is merged into the authenticated user's cart upon login or registration.
operations.name: merge

requestBody.description: Identifiers of source and target cart IDs to be merged. The target cart remains after merge. Source carts are deleted or set to inactive.

responseBody.description: Successfully merged cart with consolidated items and total count. Includes cart ID and total item quantity after merge.

prerequisites.description: A cart must be created before it can be merged, as the operation requires at least two valid cart IDs to combine.
Cart items must be added to source carts before they can be merged into the target cart, as the operation relies on existing cart item records to consolidate quantities.

operations.description:

This operation operates on the shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items tables from the database schema, aggregating cart data for the currently authenticated customer to provide a quick overview without retrieving individual line items.

The summary includes the total number of unique product variants in the cart, the combined monetary value of all items calculated at current variant pricing, and the cart's current state (active, abandoned, or pending checkout). The cart state is determined by the presence or absence of active order associations and the last activity timestamp.

To ensure performance and reduce data transfer, this operation does not return detailed line items or product information - it provides only aggregated metrics. For detailed cart contents, customers should use the GET /carts/{cartId}/items endpoint.

Security: This operation is restricted to authenticated customers only. The system automatically retrieves the cart identifier from the customer's authenticated session, ensuring that each user sees only their own cart summary. No cart ID parameters are exposed in the API since the cart is implicitly tied to the authenticated user's session.

Related operations: GET /carts/{cartId}/items (for detailed cart contents), POST /carts/checkout (to initiate purchase from this summary state).

responseBody.description: Summary data for the authenticated customer's shopping cart including aggregated statistics and state information.

The summary provides key metrics including the total number of wishlists, total items across all wishlists, and the count of wishlists containing out-of-stock items. This information enables the customer to quickly understand their overall wishlist engagement without navigating to individual wishlist pages.

Security considerations include ensuring the operation only returns data for the authenticated customer by matching the JWT token's user ID with the wishlist owner reference. operations.description:
Performs automatic cleanup of expired shopping carts and guest carts based on inactivity timeout periods as defined in system policy. This operation is triggered by scheduled system jobs to maintain database efficiency and compliance with data retention policies. It scans all cart records (both authenticated and guest) that have been inactive for more than 30 days and removes them from the database entirely, along with associated cart session records to prevent orphaned data.

This operation is essential for database performance optimization and regulatory compliance under GDPR and CCPA mandates, ensuring that abandoned user data is purged according to stated retention policies. The operation does not notify users as these carts were already considered inactive for over 30 days, as explicitly specified in the requirements document.

Security: This operation can only be triggered internally by scheduled system jobs and cannot be invoked by end users directly. It reads from the shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_sessions tables and removes records where last_updated_at is older than 30 days. No data is archived or moved to a backup; these records are permanently deleted.

This operation is complementary to the cart-to-order conversion process and ensures that only active carts are available for purchase. The 30-day inactivity period matches the business requirement specified in the shopping-cart.md document. Related operations: Update cart (PUT /carts/{cartId}), Retrieve cart (GET /carts).

Note: This is a system-initiated cleanup rather than a user-facing operation, and therefore is executed only by scheduled background jobs.

Examples of metrics include total jobs processed, average execution time, success/failure rates by job type, and recurring error patterns.

Non-administrative users, including authenticated customers and sellers, are explicitly forbidden from viewing this information to prevent potential leakage of system architecture details or operational patterns.

No authentication is required from non-admin users because they have no access rights to this endpoint. All queries to this endpoint are validated against the administrator role in the JWT token. Retrieve a paginated list of payment disputes for administrative review and resolution. Each reconciliation record tracks the status of payment matching between payment gateways and platform transactions, including timestamps, amounts, currency, reconciliation status, and associated transaction IDs.

These records are created by background reconciliation jobs and are never modified or deleted after creation, ensuring an immutable audit trail for financial compliance and regulatory reporting. Managers and accountants use this endpoint to monitor the health of the payment reconciliation system, identify processing failures, and resolve discrepancies.

operations.description:
Retrieve global shipping tracking information for all orders across the platform. This operation queries the delivery_trackings and order_shipments tables to provide comprehensive shipping status data. It supports advanced filtering by status, carrier, date range, and shipment method. The response includes all tracking details such as tracking number, carrier name, current status, location, estimated delivery date, and shipment date.

This operation is designed to support administrative monitoring and customer service functions by providing a comprehensive view of shipment statuses across the entire platform. It returns data from multiple related tables including shipping_mall_delivery_trackings for tracking events and shipping_mall_order_shipments for shipment details.

The system combines data from the delivery_trackings table (which records individual logistics events) with the order_shipments table (which stores shipment configuration details including carrier and method). This allows for a comprehensive view of shipments from order placement through delivery completion.

Security: This operation is publicly accessible to allow customers and support staff to track shipments. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse by automated scrapers. The operation does not expose sensitive customer information beyond what's necessary for tracking purposes.

Implementation note: This does not map to a single database table - it performs a JOIN between shipping_mall_delivery_trackings and shipping_mall_order_shipments:

SELECT
  ost.tracking_number,
  ost.carrier,
  ost.shipping_method,
  ost.created_at as shipment_date,
  dt.status,
  dt.location,
  dt.event_time as last_updated,
  dt.estimated_delivery_date,
  dt.actual_delivery_date,
  ost.order_id
FROM shipping_mall_order_shipments ost
JOIN shipping_mall_delivery_trackings dt ON ost.tracking_number = dt.tracking_number
ORDER BY dt.event_time DESC

This composite query serves the business need for real-time, comprehensive shipping visibility across the entire platform and integrates data from two separate system components.

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive shipping report that aggregates delivery status, carrier performance, and shipment timelines across all orders. This operation provides administrators and logistics managers with a holistic view of shipping operations, enabling data-driven decisions for carrier optimization, delivery benchmarking, and service improvement.

The report combines data from multiple interconnected database entities: shopping_mall_orders (order creation and status), shopping_mall_order_shipments (shipment assignments), shopping_mall_shipping_trackings (real-time carrier tracking events), shopping_mall_delivery_events (timestamped delivery milestones), and shopping_mall_carriers (carrier service details). Through SQL JOINs and aggregation, it calculates key logistics metrics including average delivery duration per carrier, on-time delivery rate, shipment volume by region, and carrier performance trends.

This is a computed analytics operation - it does not map to any single database table but synthesizes information from 5+ tables to deliver strategic logistics insights. The results are generated dynamically by querying the full shipment history, filtering by date ranges, and applying business logic for classification of on-time/delayed/failed deliveries.

Security considerations: Only admin actors are permitted to access this report as it contains sensitive operational data, internal carrier performance metrics, and confidential shipping cost information that could impact business relationships. The operation is rate-limited to prevent excessive database load from frequent polling by automated systems. Related operations include GET /reports/shippings/daily (for daily summaries) and GET /reports/shippings/carrier/{carrierCode} (for detailed carrier analysis).

operations.description:
Retrieve estimated delivery timeframes for a specific order. This operation queries the shopping_mall_order_shipments and shopping_mall_delivery_trackings tables to compute realistic delivery timelines based on the order's shipping method and current transit status.

The system calculates delivery estimates by combining the historical performance data of the assigned carrier with real-time tracking updates from logistics providers. When an order is shipped, the system automatically creates a shipment record with the carrier's estimated delivery window, which is then refined as tracking data becomes available through carrier APIs.

Delivery estimates are presented in a human-readable format (e.g., "3-5 business days") and include a specific date range based on the shipment's processing status. The estimate updates dynamically as tracking information is received. For example, if a package is confirmed to be at a sorting facility, the estimate may update to "Delivered by next business day".

The system ensures delivery estimates comply with carrier SLAs, and provides different estimates based on shipping tier (standard, expedited, overnight). All estimates are calculated with business days only, excluding weekends and public holidays according to the customer's shipping region.

This operation returns comprehensive delivery timelines that help customers plan for receipt of their order, and also supports customer service operations by providing accurate information to address inquiries about delivery status. The estimates are not guaranteed delivery dates but are probabilistic projections based on historical carrier performance and current transit status.

The operation is read-only and does not modify any data in the database. The delivery estimates are computed from the existing shipment records and tracking events in the system.

Note: If no shipment has been created for this order yet, the delivery estimate will be "Processing - Shipping details pending.".

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target order. This parameter is used to look up the related shopping_mall_orders record in the database. The system verifies that the order exists and that the requesting user has appropriate permissions to view its details.

Security considerations are minimal since the endpoint returns aggregated statistics and does not include any personally identifiable information from individual reviews. The operation returns a paginated result set of reviews with key information including the review text, rating, product details, customer information, and submission timestamp. This endpoint is exclusively accessible by administrative users with 'admin' privileges, as this data requires careful moderation and handling.

Reviews are returned in reverse chronological order (newest first) to prioritize recent submissions. The system supports pagination with configurable page sizes and provides total count metadata to facilitate pagination controls in the admin interface.

This operation is critical for the product review moderation workflow outlined in the requirements. It enables administrators to efficiently review customer feedback for compliance with community guidelines, identify potential fraudulent reviews, and ensure product ratings accurately reflect customer experiences.

The operation is designed to work with the shopping_mall_reviews table structure where reviews have a status field that can be pending, approved, or rejected. This endpoint specifically targets the 'pending' status reviews that require human review before being made visible to customers.

This endpoint does not modify any data - it's a read-only operation that helps maintain the integrity of the product review system by allowing administrators to process potentially problematic reviews before they become public.
operations.name: index

operations.description:
Flag a product review for moderator review due to potential violations of community guidelines. This operation creates an entry in the review_flag table linking the flagged review to a reporting user and a reason code, triggering a moderation workflow. The review remains visible to all users during moderation, but is hidden from public view if flagged as inappropriate by an administrator.

This operation corresponds to the product_review_flags table in the database schema, which stores flags on reviews for moderator review. The system allows any authenticated user to flag reviews they consider inappropriate, while only admin users can resolve flags. The flagged status is recorded permanently in the audit log.

Security: Only authenticated users can flag reviews. The user's identity is derived from the authentication token. Each user may flag a specific review only once, and repeated flagging attempts are rate-limited. Admin users can view all flagged reviews but cannot flag reviews themselves.

Implementation: This operation inserts a record into review_flags with the review_id, reporter_id, reason_code, and timestamp. It does not modify the original review record. The moderation system processes flagged reviews asynchronously, and reviewers can update the flag status to approved or rejected with associated notes.

Related operations: GET /reviews/{reviewId} (view review), PATCH /moderation/reviews (admin to resolve flags).

Moderate a product review by approving, rejecting, or flagging it as inappropriate. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table to record moderator actions on product reviews.

This endpoint allows authorized administrators to take action on customer reviews that violate platform guidelines or contain inappropriate content. Each moderation action creates an immutable audit log entry that tracks the moderator who took action, the timestamp, the review being moderated, the action taken (approve/reject/flag), and any optional comment explaining the decision.

Security considerations include strict authorization controls that limit this functionality to administrators only. The system maintains an immutable audit trail of all moderation actions for compliance purposes. The operation validates that the referenced review exists and is in a modifiable state.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs entity to create an audit trail of reviewer actions, and with the shopping_mall_reviews entity to ensure the review exists and to update its status accordingly. The export supports filtering via request parameters to subset results by date range, product category, review status, or customer segment.

Security: This export operation is restricted to admin actors only, as it exposes sensitive customer data, including potentially personally identifiable information. Audit logging is automatically generated for all export requests, recording the admin user identity, timestamp, IP address, and requested parameters.

Implementation Note: The response contains a pre-processed CSV or JSON file with all review data, including nested structures for reviewer and product information. This export avoids circular references by using ISummary variants for associated entities. Dates are formatted in ISO 8601, and all text fields are properly HTML-escaped to prevent injection vulnerabilities.

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive sales analytics for all sellers across the shopping mall platform. This operation aggregates sales data from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables to provide performance metrics for each seller, enabling strategic business decisions and targeted platform support.

The operation calculates key metrics including total sales revenue, number of completed orders, average order value, and total units sold for each seller. The analytics pipeline joins these tables based on order_id to ensure accurate aggregation while filtering out orders with status other than 'completed' to maintain financial accuracy. Security constraints ensure sellers can only view their own data, while administrators have visibility across all sellers.

This endpoint is critical for seller management, platform growth initiatives, and personalized seller support. Refers to the shopping_mall_orders table which tracks completed order transactions and the shopping_mall_order_items table which contains line-item details for each order, including quantities and prices. The operation does not expose individual customer information, maintaining privacy compliance with data protection regulations.

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive performance analytics for all sellers on the shoppingMall platform. This operation aggregates and calculates key performance indicators from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics table, providing a holistic view of seller performance across multiple dimensions including sales volume, customer ratings, order fulfillment rates, and inventory health.

The analytics are computed in real-time by aggregating data from the seller performance metrics table, which tracks all seller activity including sales volume, customer reviews, fulfillment times, stock levels, and operational efficiency scores. The metric calculations incorporate business logic to normalize and weight different performance factors according to platform-wide seller evaluation standards.

This operation serves administrative and operational purposes by providing visibility into seller performance trends, enabling proactive management of underperforming sellers, identification of high-performing sellers for promotional opportunities, and data-driven decisions regarding platform policy adjustments. Performance metrics are calculated to reflect the true operational health of sellers rather than simplistic metrics that could be manipulated.

The operation responds with detailed performance analytics that represent a composite score based on multiple weighted factors, which helps platform administrators make informed decisions about seller support, tier upgrades, or potential restrictions. This data enables strategic management of the seller ecosystem to ensure high-quality customer experiences across the platform.

This operation does NOT map directly to a single database table but is instead a computed analytical view that synthesizes data from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics table. The implementation involves complex data aggregation and weighted scoring that is performed on-demand rather than through pre-computed summaries, ensuring dynamic responsiveness to changing seller activity patterns.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive aggregated performance analytics for all sellers on the platform, with weighted composite scores and individual metric values.

operations.description:
This operation provides an analytical overview of seller communication patterns and interaction metrics across the platform. It aggregates data from the shopping_mall_seller_communication_logs table to reveal engagement trends, response efficiency, and seller-customer interaction dynamics.

The analytics include: total communication volume, average response time, communication channel distribution, response rate by seller, and communication volume by date range. This information helps identify sellers with high engagement, those needing support in responsiveness, and overall platform communication health.

The operation does not expose individual communication records but presents aggregated metrics optimized for analytics dashboards. It returns a summary structure with statistical metrics, trend indicators, and performance benchmarks. This ensures data privacy while providing actionable insights for administrator oversight.

This operation is read-only and does not modify any data. It complements direct communication endpoints by providing a high-level performance view. The data is computed on demand from communication logs and represents the most recent available analytics (current day and previous 30 days).

Key metrics include: total communications, average response time in hours, response rate (percentage of messages responded to within 24 hours), communication diversity score, and seller engagement index.
operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive compliance analytics for all sellers on the platform. This operation aggregates data from the shopping_mall_seller_compliance_history, shopping_mall_sellers, and shopping_mall_compliance_records tables to provide a holistic view of seller compliance status, historical violations, and overall trustworthiness.

The analytics endpoint generates a unified view by joining seller profile data with compliance records and history logs. It computes key metrics including total compliance violations, recurring violation patterns, severity distribution, and resolution rates across all active sellers. The data is aggregated at the seller level and presented with detailed breakdowns by violation type, time period, and resolution status.

Security considerations require admin-level authorization since this data contains sensitive compliance metrics and historical records that could be used for competitive analysis or manipulation. The endpoint protects against data mining by limiting time-range aggregation and requiring explicit admin authentication.

This operation complements other administrative endpoints such as GET /sellers/{sellerId} for individual seller details and PATCH /sellers for bulk management actions. The compliance analytics provide the enterprise-level overview that administrative dashboards require for risk assessment and policy enforcement.

Consider this operation as the authoritative source for platform-wide seller compliance reporting, with all data captured from immutable audit logs, avoiding any real-time calculations that might be manipulated.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive compliance analytics for all sellers, including total violations, violation types, resolution stats, and seller-level compliance scores.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated analytics on seller subscription tiers across the platform. This operation compiles data from the shopping_mall_seller_subscription_tiers and shopping_mall_sellers tables to provide insights into subscription adoption patterns, revenue distribution by tier, and seller distribution across subscription levels.

The system calculates key metrics including total active sellers per tier, percentage distribution of sellers across tiers, monthly recurring revenue (MRR) by tier, and churn rates between subscription levels. Historical trends are not included in this endpoint as they require separate time-series analysis operations.

This operation is only accessible to administrators who require high-level business intelligence about seller monetization patterns. The data presented serves product and business teams for subscription strategy decisions, pricing adjustments, and tier optimizations.

No filtering or pagination is supported as this operation returns a consolidated summary of the entire seller base. For detailed analysis of individual sellers or historical trends, use the dedicated seller performance analytics endpoint.

Implementation note: This operation performs a SQL JOIN between shopping_mall_seller_subscription_tiers and shopping_mall_sellers, grouping by subscription tier and aggregating seller count and revenue metrics. Results are computed on-demand without dedicated materialized views to maintain data freshness.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive subscription analytics summary for sellers across all tiers

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive executive overview for system administrators. This operation aggregates key metrics from multiple database sources including administrative activity, system health, resource utilization, and pending approvals to provide a unified dashboard view for platform governance.

The operation combines data from the shopping_mall_admins, shopping_mall_audit_logs, shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts, shopping_mall_configurations, shopping_mall_order_events, shopping_mall_product_sales_stats, and shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics tables. It calculates current operational status, identifies anomalies requiring administrator attention, and presents summary statistics for decision-making. The response includes administrative user counts, system health indicators, transaction volumes, pending verification requests, and performance benchmarks for sellers.

Security protocol: This endpoint is restricted to admin actors with elevated privileges, and all field access follows principle of least privilege. The operation does not return personally identifiable information about individual users, focusing instead on aggregate metrics. Rate limiting and monitoring alerts are triggered if the endpoint is accessed abnormally frequently or by non-admin actors.

operations.description:
Retrieves a comprehensive sales overview dashboard with aggregated metrics from completed orders across the entire platform. This operation combines data from the shopping_mall_orders and shopping_mall_order_items tables to provide key performance indicators for administrative decision-making. The operation calculates total revenue, order volume, average order value, and sales trends over specified time periods.

The system retrieves completed orders and their associated items, computes total revenue by summing the product of unit price and quantity for all line items, and aggregates these values by time period (daily, weekly, monthly). The data is processed to exclude orders with statuses of "pending", "cancelled", or "refunded" to ensure only real transactions are counted.

Security considerations require this endpoint to be accessible only by admin users due to the sensitive nature of revenue and transaction data. The operation implements internal rate limiting to prevent excessive data extraction, and logs all access attempts as part of the audit trail.

This operation is a core component of the administrative dashboard and integrates with other analytics endpoints including /analytics/sales-by-month and /analytics/sales-by-category. These related operations provide more granular breakdowns of aggregated data, and should be referenced when an admin user needs to drill down into specific segments of sales data. This overview endpoint provides the high-level summary that contextualizes those detailed reports.

The implementation requires complex SQL joining and grouping operations: orders are joined with order_items on order_id, filtered by status="delivered", and grouped by time period to compute SUM(total_price), COUNT(*), and AVG(total_price) for each period.

Error handling includes returning a 403 Forbidden status if non-admin users attempt access and a 500 Internal Server Error if database aggregation fails due to data inconsistencies or connection issues.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Comprehensive sales overview statistics for the administrative dashboard containing aggregated metrics across the entire platform.

operations.description:
This operation retrieves comprehensive performance analytics for products across the e-commerce platform, combining sales statistics, view metrics, and inventory data to provide insights into product performance trends.

The operation aggregates data from three core database entities: shopping_mall_product_sales_stats (sales volume, revenue, conversion rates), shopping_mall_product_view_stats (page views, click-through rates, dwell time), and shopping_mall_products (product metadata, category, pricing). It computes key performance indicators by joining these pre-computed aggregation tables to create a holistic view of product success.

This is not a direct table query but a complex analytical operation that transforms pre-aggregated data into business intelligence. The endpoint supports filtering by date range, category, seller, and product status (active/inactive) to allow administrators to analyze performance across different dimensions.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent abuse of analytics queries and authorization restricted to admin actors only, as this data contains sensitive business metrics. Performance optimization is achieved through daily batch jobs that compute statistics from transactional data, so this endpoint provides rapid access to pre-computed metrics rather than real-time computations on raw transactional data.

The response structure follows the IPageIShoppingMallProductPerformance.ISummary pattern, providing paginated results with pagination metadata and a summarized view of product performance metrics. This enables efficient rendering of dashboards and allows for client-side filtering and sorting without overloading the server with excessive data transfers.

Related operations: GET /analytics/products/top-sellers (for top performing products), GET /analytics/products/low-stock (for inventory alerts).

responseBody.description: Paginated summary of product performance analytics including sales volume, revenue, conversion rates, view metrics, and inventory status.
