source.description:
System component or service that generated the alert.

Identifies the origin of the monitoring event, such as:
- payment_gateway
- inventory_service
- product_catalog
- order_processing
- delivery_tracking
- analytics_engine

This helps administrators quickly identify affected subsystems during incident response.

Must be a valid system component name registered in the platform configuration.

message.description:
Human-readable description of the alert condition.

Provides context about what was detected, including relevant metrics, thresholds breached, and affected entities.

Example: "Payment gateway response time exceeded 5s threshold (current: 8.2s) for 5 consecutive requests".

details.description:
Structured JSON object containing diagnostic information about the alert.

This field contains machine-readable metadata for automated response systems and detailed analysis.

Examples of data:
- timestamps of triggered events
- affected resource identifiers
- error codes from downstream systems
- request/response sample data
- performance metric values

External systems can consume this data for automated remediation workflows.

detected_at.description:
Timestamp when the monitoring system first detected the alert condition.

This represents the exact moment the threshold or pattern was matched.

Used for chronological ordering, trend analysis, and correlation with other system events.

Stored in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 format.

This field is immutable once set - it records when the detection occurred, not when it was processed.

created_by.description:
Identifier of the system component or service that created this alert.

This represents the monitoring agent or service that detected and initiated the alert.


This is NOT a user ID - it identifies automated systems like:
- payment_monitoring_agent
- inventory_sync_engine
- security_analyzer_service

The actual admin who later acknowledges or resolves the alert is tracked in audit logs.

resolved_by.description:
Identifier of the administrator who marked the alert as resolved.

Only populated when status transitions from 'acknowledged' to 'resolved'.

Stores the admin's unique identifier from the shopping_mall_admins table.

Provides accountability and traceability for resolution actions.

This field remains null until an admin explicitly resolves the alert.

resolution_notes.description:
Free-form comments documenting the resolution process.

When an alert is marked as resolved, the administrator may provide additional context:
- Actions taken to fix the issue
- Root cause analysis
- Temporary workaround details
- Follow-up tasks created
- Preventative measures implemented

This field provides valuable knowledge for future incident reviews and training.

suppressed_reason.description:
Justification for suppressing the alert.

Only populated when status transitions to 'suppressed'.

Must include:
- Reason for suppression (e.g., scheduled maintenance, known issue)
- Expected duration of suppression
- Contact information for escalation if needed
- Date/time when suppression will be lifted

Used to prevent alert fatigue while maintaining visibility of intentional silencing.

related_alerts.description:
List of IDs for related alerts that may be part of the same incident.

Used to group alerts that are causally linked or part of a system-wide failure.

Example: A payment gateway failure might generate alerts in:
- payment_gateway
- order_processing
- customer_notification_system

These would be linked via this array to facilitate coordinated response.

correlation_id.description:
Global identifier for a multi-component incident.

Used to trace alert relationships across distributed services.

All alerts generated during the same incident event share the same correlation_id.

Provides end-to-end transaction visibility for complex system failures involving multiple components.

tags.description:
List of keyword tags for categorization and filtering.

Allows administrators to group alerts by:
- Service: "payment", "inventory", "shipping"
- System: "database", "cache", "redis"
- Severity indicator: "high-impact", "regulatory"
- Environment: "production", "staging"

Tags are used for dashboard views, alert routing, and automated response filtering.

additional_properties.description:
Expanded object for custom metadata not covered by standard fields.

Used for extensibility to accommodate future monitoring requirements without schema changes.

Examples:
- vendor-specific error codes
- third-party system response headers
- custom metrics generated by plugins
- regional or compliance-specific data

Keys are dynamically determined by monitoring integrations.

client_ip.description:
IP address from which the associated user or system action originated.

If the alert was triggered by a user action, this records the client's IP.

If triggered by an internal system service, this records the service's server IP.

Used for security analysis, abuse detection, and geolocation-based alert routing.

user_agent.description:
User agent string from the client or system that triggered this alert.

Collects technical details about the requesting entity:
- Browser type and version
- Operating system
- Device type (mobile, desktop, etc.)
- Library or framework version

Helps diagnose issues specific to certain client configurations.

http_method.description:
HTTP method involved in the request that triggered this alert.

Value examples: "GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE".

Used for analyzing trends related to specific API operations.

Relevant when alerts are triggered by unusual API behavior like excessive POST requests or abnormal DELETE patterns.

http_status_code.description:
HTTP status code returned by the service that triggered this alert.

Used to correlate server responses with system events.

Common codes: 500 (internal server error), 429 (rate limit exceeded), 503 (service unavailable), 403 (forbidden).

Helps distinguish between application-level issues and infrastructure problems.

url_path.description:
URL path that was accessed when this alert was triggered.

For alerts related to API access, this is the exact endpoint that caused the issue.

Example: "/shoppingMall/api/v1/orders/{orderId}/cancel"

Helps pinpoint the affected service endpoint for targeted troubleshooting.

error_code.description:
Specific error code returned by the service or component that generated this alert.

Standardized codes defined by each system component:
- Payment: "PAY-5001" (authentication failed)
- Inventory: "INV-4004" (stock inconsistency)
- Order: "ORD-5008" (processing timeout)

Used for automated alert classification and routing.

corrupted_data.description:
Indicates whether the alert was triggered by data integrity violations.

When true, this indicates that the monitoring system detected:
- Inconsistent database records
- Invalid foreign key relationships
- Data type mismatches
- Missing required fields
- Encoding errors

Alerts of this type require database-level repair or validation processes.

impact_duration_minutes.description:
Duration of impact in minutes since the alert was first detected.

Calculated as the difference between updated_at and detected_at for alerts with status "active" or "acknowledged".

Used for:
- SLA monitoring and reporting
- Escalation timing calculations
- Incident resolution time analysis
- Performance trend analysis

Values are calculated automatically by the system based on timestamps.

alert_link.description:
URL that directly links to a detailed view of this alert in the admin dashboard.

Generates a permanent, sharable link to the alert's detail page.

Format: "https://admin.shoppingmall.com/alerts/{id}"

Used for:
- Email notifications to on-call teams
- Slack/Teams integrations
- Incident management system integration
- Cross-team collaboration

All generated links use HTTPS protocol and are immutable once created.

IShoppingMallMonitoringAlert.description:
Represents a system monitoring alert for the shoppingMall platform.

This entity captures critical events detected by the monitoring system across various subsystems including payments, inventory, orders, delivery, and security.

Each alert provides comprehensive context about the nature, severity, origin, and status of system anomalies. The schema is designed to support alert lifecycle management from detection through resolution or suppression.

Alerts are written to the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table and are vital for:
- Ensuring platform reliability and uptime
- Identifying recurring failures and system weaknesses
- Enabling proactive system maintenance
- Maintaining compliance with operational standards

The alert system serves both automated response mechanisms and human operators, with information structured to support both machine parsing and administrative review.

Users with admin access can acknowledge, resolve, or suppress alerts through the admin dashboard. Alert lifecycle status transitions are always tracked in audit logs for accountability and compliance.

This schema represents the main entity view - a full representation of all alert data when retrieved via the GET /shoppingMall/admin/monitoring/alerts/{alertId} endpoint.

count.description: The number of cart records successfully cleaned up and deleted from the system. This reflects the total count of expired carts (both authenticated and guest) processed by the system cleanup job.

ICleanupResult.description: Confirmation of the number of cart records successfully cleaned up and deleted from the system. This response type is returned by the cleanup-expiry operation after it has processed all expired carts based on the 30-day inactivity policy.

total_sales.description:
Total revenue generated from all product sales.

Represents the sum of all completed order payments for products in USD, calculated during the current reporting period. This metric reflects the overall financial performance of the product catalog.

Calculated by aggregating the total_amount from all completed shopping_mall_order_payments records associated with products.

This total includes all sales across all channels and seller accounts, providing a comprehensive view of overall marketplace revenue.

average_conversion_rate.description:
Average conversion rate across all products, expressed as a decimal fraction (0-1).

Calculated as the ratio of total sales to total views across all products: (total_sales / total_views).

This metric represents the average effectiveness of product listings in converting visitors into buyers. A higher conversion rate indicates more effective product presentation, pricing, and description quality.

Values are calculated using aggregated statistics from both shopping_mall_product_sales_stats and shopping_mall_product_view_stats tables to ensure accurate correlation between product views and sales outcomes.

top_selling_product_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product with the highest sales volume.

Identifies the single product that has generated the most revenue in the current reporting period.

This field is populated by querying the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table and ordering by total_sales_amount in descending order, then taking the top result.

Used by administrators to identify top-performing products for promotion and inventory prioritization.

top_selling_product_sales.description:
Total sales revenue generated by the top-selling product.

Represents the total revenue generated by the single product with the highest sales volume in the current reporting period, in USD.

This value corresponds to the total_sales_amount field in the shopping_mall_product_sales_stats table for the product identified in top_selling_product_id.

This metric highlights product-level performance and helps administrators identify breakout products that may benefit from increased marketing investment.

IShoppingMallProductOverview.description:
Comprehensive product performance summary containing aggregated sales and view statistics across the product catalog.

This schema represents the response structure for the administrative dashboard product overview endpoint, providing administrators with a holistic view of product performance across the entire e-commerce platform.

The data combines metrics from shopping_mall_product_sales_stats (sales performance), shopping_mall_product_view_stats (customer engagement), shopping_mall_product_reviews (customer feedback), shopping_mall_order_returns (return behavior), and shopping_mall_cart_sessions (checkout behavior) to create a unified performance dashboard.

All metrics are calculated from recent aggregated statistics to ensure timely insights for decision-making. The data refreshes continuously as new sales, views, and customer interactions occur.

Key considerations:
- All monetary values are in the platform's primary currency (USD in this implementation)
- Conversion rates and percentages are expressed as decimal fractions between 0 and 1
- Timestamp-based metrics use the current reporting period as defined by the system's analytics engine
- Product identifiers use UUID format for universal uniqueness across distributed systems
- Inventory thresholds may vary by product category based on seasonal factors and lead times

This comprehensive overview enables administrators to identify top-performing products, detect underperforming categories, optimize inventory levels, evaluate marketing effectiveness, and make data-driven decisions to maximize marketplace profitability.

IShoppingMallPaymentRefund.description:
Payment refund record representing a monetary return to a customer's original payment method. This entity is created when a customer initiates a return or when an order is cancelled, and provides a complete audit trail for financial reconciliation. The refund amount represents the exact monetary value returned, and the status indicates whether the refund is pending, processed, or failed.

All refund records are immutable once created and must be linked to a specific payment transaction in the shopping_mall_payments table. This schema includes both business-critical fields (amount, reason, status) and system-managed fields (timestamps, identifiers) to support auditing, reconciliation, and customer support functions.

Refunds are initiated through the shopping_mall_order_returns table, and this entity serves as the financial counterpart to return requests. The system ensures that refund amounts cannot exceed the original payment total and tracks whether funds were returned via the original payment method, store credit, or bank transfer. This entity is critical for financial reporting, customer service, and regulatory compliance.

Used in payment refund creation (ICreate) and retrieval operations. The refund status transitions from 'pending' to either 'processed' or 'failed' based on the payment gateway's response. Refund reasons must come from predefined categories to maintain consistency in financial reporting and customer service.

id.description: Unique identifier for the refund record. This UUID is auto-generated by the system upon refund request creation and is immutable.

payment_id.description: Reference to the original payment transaction in the shopping_mall_payments table. This links the refund to its corresponding payment record for reconciliation purposes and audit trail.

order_id.description: Reference to the order that triggered this refund. This provides traceability from the refund back to the original purchase transaction and customer context.

amount.description: The exact monetary amount being refunded to the customer. This value cannot exceed the original payment amount and is recorded with full cent precision (two decimal places) for accurate financial reconciliation. Money is always represented in USD.

reason.description: The business reason for the refund, selected from predefined categories. This must be one of: 'item_not_as_described', 'wrong_item_received', 'damaged_item', 'duplicate_payment', 'customer_requested', or 'other'. This standardized categorization ensures consistency in financial reporting and customer analytics. The reason code is used for trend analysis, fraud detection, and improving product quality.

oneOf.description: The current state of the refund processing. Must be one of: 'pending' (refund request received, processing underway), 'processed' (refund successfully completed and funds returned to customer), or 'failed' (refund attempt failed, no funds returned). This status is automatically updated by the system based on payment gateway feedback.

The current state of the refund processing. Must be one of: 'pending' (refund request received, processing underway), 'processed' (refund successfully completed and funds returned to customer), or 'failed' (refund attempt failed, no funds returned). This status is automatically updated by the system based on payment gateway feedback.

The current state of the refund processing. Must be one of: 'pending' (refund request received, processing underway), 'processed' (refund successfully completed and funds returned to customer), or 'failed' (refund attempt failed, no funds returned). This status is automatically updated by the system based on payment gateway feedback.

status.description: The current state of the refund processing. Must be one of: 'pending' (refund request received, processing underway), 'processed' (refund successfully completed and funds returned to customer), or 'failed' (refund attempt failed, no funds returned). This status is automatically updated by the system based on payment gateway feedback.

customer_id.description: Identifier of the customer who requested the refund. This corresponds to the customer_id in the shopping_mall_customers table and is used for customer support and communication tracking.

seller_id.description: Identifier of the seller whose product triggered this refund. This links the refund to the appropriate seller account for financial settlement purposes.

refund_method.description: The method used for the refund disbursement. Must be one of: 'original_payment_method' (funds returned to original payment source), 'store_credit' (funds credited to customer's account balance), or 'bank_transfer' (funds transferred to customer's bank account). This field indicates how the customer will receive their refund.

refund_reference.description: External reference number provided by the payment gateway for this refund transaction. This enables cross-referencing with payment processor records during reconciliation. This field is populated after the refund is submitted to the payment gateway.

comment.description: Optional textual comment provided by the customer or support agent regarding the refund request. This may include additional context, customer concerns, or notes for internal team reference.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this refund request was initially created in the system. This is a system-generated field that cannot be modified and provides the audit timeline for refund processing.

failed_reason.description: Detailed reason for refund failure if status is 'failed'. This may include payment gateway error codes, insufficient funds, invalid account information, declined by bank, fraud flags, or other technical details that explain why the refund could not be completed. This field provides diagnostic information for reconciliation and support

oneOf.description:
Status of connectivity to payment gateways.

Indicates whether the system can successfully establish and maintain connections to configured payment processors. This metric is derived from the most recent successful communication attempts recorded in shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs.

- healthy: All configured gateways responded within acceptable latency thresholds during the last monitoring cycle.
- degraded: Some gateways responded but with increased latency or partial failures, indicating potential network or service issues.
- unreachable: No payment gateways responded to connectivity checks, indicating a complete outage or configuration failure.

Status of connectivity to payment gateways.

Indicates whether the system can successfully establish and maintain connections to configured payment processors. This metric is derived from the most recent successful communication attempts recorded in shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs.

- healthy: All configured gateways responded within acceptable latency thresholds during the last monitoring cycle.
- degraded: Some gateways responded but with increased latency or partial failures, indicating potential network or service issues.
- unreachable: No payment gateways responded to connectivity checks, indicating a complete outage or configuration failure.

oneOf.description:

Represents the utilization of rate limits defined in shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits. This monitors the ratio of current transaction volume to configured maximums to prevent system overload.

- within: Current transaction volume is under 70% of the configured limit, indicating normal operation.
- exceeding: Current transaction volume is between 70-90% of the configured limit, indicating approaching capacity and potential need for scaling.
- critical: Current transaction volume exceeds 90% of the configured limit, indicating immediate risk of request rejection.

oneOf.description:

Compares internal payment records with settlement reports received from payment processors via shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation. This ensures accurate financial accounting.

- balanced: All payment records match with gateway settlements with zero discrepancies.
- minor-discrepancy: Small discrepancies exist (typically 0.1-2% of transaction volume) that may be due to processing delays or fee differences.
- major-discrepancy: Significant discrepancies exist (>2% of transaction volume) indicating potential system errors or fraudulent activity requiring immediate investigation.

- incomplete: Some audit entries are missing, potentially indicating failed logging operations or system errors.
- corrupted: Audit entries exist but contain invalid or inconsistent data (missing fields, invalid timestamps).

- warning: Some non-critical parameters are missing or have unexpected values that may affect functionality but don't prevent operation.
- invalid: Critical configuration parameters are missing or invalid (e.g., undefined credentials, invalid URLs, malformed JSON), preventing payment processing.

healthScore.description:
Composite health score from 0-100 based on all component statuses.

Calculated as a weighted average of gatewayConnectivity (35%), rateLimitStatus (25%), reconciliationStatus (20%), auditLogIntegrity (15%), and configurationStatus (5%).

- 90-100: Excellent health - all systems operating normally
- 70-89: Good health - minor issues detectable but not impacting operations
- 50-69: Fair health - notable issues requiring monitoring and potential intervention
- 0-49: Poor health - critical failures requiring immediate attention

This score provides a quick, holistic view of payment system health.

lastUpdated.description:
Timestamp of when the health status was last calculated and updated.

This field indicates the most recent moment when all health metrics were evaluated based on the current state of the system. It helps operators understand the freshness of the reported status data.

alerts.description:
List of active alerts related to payment system health.

Contains human-readable messages for any outstanding issues requiring attention, such as "Payment gateway timeout detected", "Rate limit approaching threshold", or "Reconciliation discrepancy >5%". These alerts are generated from monitoring rules applied to the system components.

monitoringSources.description:
List of data sources used to calculate this health status.

Specifies which underlying system entities contributed to the health assessment: shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs, shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits, shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation, shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs, and shopping_mall_payment_settings. This transparency helps operators understand how the health score was derived.

suggestedActions.description:
Recommended actions to improve payment system health.

Provides specific, actionable recommendations such as "Verify API credentials for PayPal gateway", "Increase rate limit capacity for Stripe", or "Investigate reconciliation discrepancy with Adyen" based on the current status of each component.

IShoppingMallPaymentHealthStatus.description:
Comprehensive health status of all payment system components, including connectivity, capacity, integrity, and configuration status.

This summary object provides a complete picture of the payment subsystem's operational health, derived from automated monitoring of key entities: shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs, shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits, shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation, shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs, and shopping_mall_payment_settings.

The status is organized into five primary dimensional assessments, each with a categorical status (healthy/degraded/unreachable, within/exceeding/critical, etc.) to provide clear visual indicators of system health. A composite health score from 0-100 is calculated to provide an overall metric, while active alerts and recommended actions give operators immediate guidance on the current state and necessary interventions.

This health status is updated periodically by the payment subsystem monitoring service and is used by administrative dashboards to display system health without requiring direct API interactions with payment gateways

IExportIShoppingMallReview.description:
Exported reviews data in structured format (CSV/JSON) with complete review information. This schema is used for administrative analytics, compliance reporting, and data migration purposes. It includes comprehensive review details along with associated customer and product summary information, while adhering to security best practices by excluding sensitive fields and using ISummary variants to prevent circular references.

The export operation provides a complete dataset of customer feedback for analytical processing, regulatory compliance, and data migration scenarios. This structured data format enables seamless integration with business intelligence tools, data warehouses, and compliance reporting systems.

Each review entry contains foundational data from the shopping_mall_reviews table, enriched with contextual summaries of the associated customer and product entities. The export format avoids embedded arrays of reviews or product variants to prevent unbounded data growth and maintain predictable payload sizes.

All dates are formatted in ISO 8601 for international compatibility, and all text fields are properly HTML-escaped to prevent injection vulnerabilities. The schema ensures that no sensitive user information beyond what is appropriate for administrative data exports under GDPR and CCPA frameworks is exposed.

This export is intended for administrative and analytical purposes only and is restricted to admin actors due to the sensitive nature of customer feedback data. The associated customer and product objects use summary variants (ISummary) to provide necessary context without exposing full profile details or pricing information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the review record in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

rating.description: Numeric rating given by the customer, ranging from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). This value is derived from the rating column in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

title.description:
Title or headline of the review submitted by the customer. This is a brief summary of the customer's experience with the product.

This field is derived from the title column in the shopping_mall_reviews table and is subject to character limits to ensure data consistency.

content.description:
Full textual content of the review submitted by the customer. This field contains detailed feedback about the product, including pros, cons, and overall experience.

The content can be empty if the customer provided only a rating, but if present, it is limited to 10,000 characters to prevent excessive data size in exports.

This field is sourced from the content column in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

- pending: Review has been submitted but not yet reviewed by moderators
- approved: Review has been approved and is publicly visible
- hidden: Review has been hidden from public view but retained for compliance purposes
- rejected: Review has been rejected as violating community guidelines

This field is derived from the status column in the shopping_mall_reviews table.

customer.description:
Summary information of the customer who submitted this review.

Includes basic identification and profile information of the reviewer without exposing sensitive data such as exact email addresses or contact details. This prevents privacy violations while providing context about the reviewer.

This reference follows the relationship pattern defined in the shopping_mall_reviews table's customer_id foreign key to the shopping_mall_customers table.

product.description:

Contains essential product information needed to understand the context of the review, including name, category, and brand, but excludes detailed attributes, pricing, or inventory data.

This reference follows the relationship pattern defined in the shopping_mall_reviews table's product_id foreign key to the shopping_mall_products table.

IShoppingMallSecurityPolicies.description:
System-wide security policy configuration for the shoppingMall platform.

Defines comprehensive security rules governing authentication, authorization, password policies, session management, and compliance settings across the entire platform.

This schema represents the authoritative configuration for security controls applied to all user actors (customer, seller, admin). The policy settings are enforced automatically by the backend infrastructure and affect every system operation.

The configuration includes password complexity requirements, session timeout restrictions, account lockout policies, multi-factor authentication rules, and audit trail retention policies. All values are stored in the shopping_mall_security_policies database table and validated against enterprise security standards.

Changes to these policies require administrative approval and are subject to compliance audits. Violations of these policies trigger system alerts and potential account restrictions.

passwordComplexity.description:
Configuration for password complexity requirements.

Defines the minimum and maximum length requirements, character set rules, and other constraints for user passwords.

This policy ensures strong authentication security by enforcing complex password formats that are difficult to guess or crack.

Includes rules for minimum password length, required character types (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters), and maximum age before password reset is required.

sessionManagement.description:
Configuration for user session behavior and security.

Defines rules for session creation, expiration, renewal, and security within the system.

This policy controls how long users remain logged in, how sessions are managed across devices, and what security measures are applied.

Critical for maintaining secure user sessions throughout the application lifetime.

IShoppingMallProductEnriched.description:
Denormalized product data structure combining base product information with all variants, pricing, inventory, and image data.

This schema represents the complete product offering as returned by GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/enriched, combining all related entities into a single optimized response to eliminate multiple API calls for client-side product display.

The structure includes:
- Base product metadata (title, description, status)
- Product brand and primary category
- Product images gallery with primary flag
- Product tags and secondary categories for discoverability
- All product variants with their unique SKUs
- Variant-specific pricing and inventory levels
- Variant attribute definitions and selected values
- Product view and sales statistics
- Product availability status

This denormalized view ensures the frontend can render a complete product page with no additional API calls required, maximizing performance and user experience.

This schema directly maps to the shopping_mall_products table in the database, with each property corresponding to a field in the product entity. The schema leverages references to other schemas to create a comprehensive, non-redundant representation of product data with related entities.

The schema follows strict business rules: all products must have a status (draft, published, archived), must belong to at least one primary category, must have at least one image, and must have at least one variant. Product analytics (sales_stats and view_stats) are computed aggregates from related tables and are refreshed daily through batch processes. Availability status is calculated in real-time based on inventory levels across all variants.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product entity in the system.

This UUID is the primary key in the shopping_mall_products table and is automatically generated upon product creation using a universally unique identifier algorithm. It remains immutable throughout the product's lifecycle and is used as the core reference key across all related tables, including product variants, images, sales statistics, and customer reviews.

The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and facilitates efficient database indexing and relationship management. This field serves as the foundational reference for all product-related operations, from retrieval and updates to analytics and reporting.

This identifier is required in all product-related API calls and is essential for maintaining data integrity within the e-commerce platform.

code.description:
Global unique code for the product, used in URLs and external references (e.g., /products/{code}). This is the primary key for product lookup across the entire catalog.

The product code is a human-readable, business-critical identifier designed for use in marketing, URLs, and external systems. Unlike the internal database UUID, this code follows SEO-friendly naming conventions and is intentionally designed to be memorable and descriptive.

Production codes must be globally unique across the entire catalog and are typically derived from a combination of category, brand, and serial number (e.g., "iphone-15-pro-256gb-black"). These codes are indexed for fast lookup and are used in all public-facing links, search engine results, and tracking pixels.

The product code cannot be changed once assigned, as it forms part of the product's permanent digital footprint across the internet. External systems (third-party marketplaces, affiliate programs, advertising platforms) rely on this stable identifier for integration purposes.

title.description:
Official product title displayed to customers in listings and product pages.

The product title is the primary marketing text used to attract customer attention in search results, category pages, and featured listings. It must be concise, impactful, and optimized for both human readers and search engine algorithms.

Titles typically follow a structured format: [Brand] [Product Name] [Key Specification] [Variant] (e.g., "Apple iPhone 15 Pro 256GB Black"). They prioritize the most important differentiators first and are limited to 100 characters for optimal display in mobile interfaces.

The title is an editable field controlled by sellers and is distinct from the product code, allowing for marketing flexibility while maintaining stable URLs. Title changes can significantly impact product visibility and conversion rates in search results.

description.description:
Detailed product description in HTML format, including specifications, features, benefits, and usage instructions.

This field contains rich, structured content in HTML format designed to convert browsing customers into purchasers. The description typically follows a hierarchical structure: opening hook, key features, technical specifications, usage scenarios, warranty information, and call-to-action.

Prohibited elements include promotional language like "best" or "#1" without substantiating data, as well as misleading claims against platform policies. Auto-suggested content from AI is reviewed by platform moderators to ensure compliance with truth-in-advertising standards.

The description supports rich HTML elements including headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, images, and embedded videos to enhance comprehension. Search engines index this content for improved product discoverability, and it is displayed on the full product detail page while being truncated for listing views.

oneOf.description:
Current publication status of the product. Published products are visible to customers; draft products are only visible to sellers and admins; archived products are removed from public view but preserved for historical record.

The product status determines its visibility and availability in the marketplace. A 'draft' product is in development mode, created by a seller but not yet published for sale. These remain invisible to customers and cannot be purchased.

A 'published' product is actively available for customers to view, add to cart, and purchase. This status indicates that all required information has been provided, compliance checks have passed, and the product meets platform standards for listing.

An 'archived' product has been removed from public view but maintains its data history for compliance, refund processing, and analytics purposes. Archived products are no longer available for sale but may be restored if needed by admin or seller.

Status transitions are controlled by seller actions with platform moderation oversight to prevent policy violations. Changes trigger audit log entries and notify relevant stakeholders.

brand.description:
Reference to the product's brand entity, providing brand name and logo URL for brand attribution and filtering.

The brand information is represented by a summary reference (IShoppingMallProductBrand.ISummary) to optimize response size while maintaining essential brand identification. This reference connects the product to its official manufacturer or trademark holder, enabling category-based filtering and customer trust building.

Brand associations are validated during product creation to ensure authenticity and prevent counterfeit listings. Brands that have completed the platform's verification process are marked as 'verified' in the brand summary.

The brand logo URL points to a publicly accessible image optimized for display on product cards. This association can be used by customers to filter products by brand and by platform for brand protection, trademark enforcement, and marketing campaigns.

category.description:
Primary category for product organization and navigation. Products belong to exactly one primary category for hierarchical browsing.

The primary category defines the main classification of the product within the platform's taxonomy system. Each product must have exactly one primary category, which serves as its main organizational anchor in the product catalog.

This category is used to determine which filters, attributes, and search parameters are applicable to the product. Products in the 'Electronics' category might have different attributes than those in 'Clothing'. The primary category also determines placement in catalogs, navigation menus, and search results.

The category reference points to a summary representation (IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary) containing essential identifying fields without full category details, ensuring efficient data transfer. The category hierarchy supports multi-level nesting (e.g., Electronics > Mobile Phones > Smartphones).

secondary_categories.description:
Additional categories this product belongs to for improved discoverability and multiple classification paths. Products can belong to multiple secondary categories.

Secondary categories, also known as cross-categories or child categories, allow a single product to be discoverable through multiple classification paths. This enhances product visibility in search results and helps customers find items through alternative browsing contexts.

For example, a "Wireless Earbuds" product might have a primary category of 'Electronics' and secondary categories of 'Health & Fitness' and 'Travel Accessories'. This enables the product to appear when customers browse by any of these categories.

Secondary categories do not affect product attributes or filters; they are purely for discoverability. The platform limits the number of secondary categories to maintain clean taxonomy navigation and prevent categorization abuse.

Each secondary category reference uses the IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary schema to provide consistent representation with minimal payload.

images.description:
Gallery of product images with metadata including URL, order, and primary flag. At least one image is required, with one designated as the primary display image for listings.

The product image gallery contains multiple visual representations of the product from different angles, uses, and contexts. Each image includes metadata for display prioritization (order) and functional designation (primary flag).

The primary image is the default thumbnail shown in search results, category listings, and recommendation widgets. Additional images are displayed in the product detail page carousel. All images must meet platform quality standards (minimum resolution, optimized format) and cannot contain promotional text overlays.

Image metadata includes the original filename and file extension for identification and validation. Multiple images per product support marketing flexibility while maintaining visual consistency. The system auto-generates responsive image variants for different device types.

tags.description:
Tags applied to the product for marketing and search purposes, such as 'on-sale', 'limited-edition', 'new-arrival', etc.

Product tags are keywords or labels assigned to products to enhance discoverability, enable filters, and support marketing campaigns. They represent dynamic, non-hierarchical classifications that provide additional context beyond the categorical taxonomy.

Tags are created and managed by administrators and sellers and are assigned to products through the platform interface. They are designed to be user-friendly, short, and meaningful, often reflecting promotional status, product attributes, or customer sentiment.

Tagging supports multiple use cases: 'on-sale' for sorting during promotions, 'eco-friendly' for sustainability filters, 'best-seller' for social proof, and 'gift-ready' for seasonal marketing. Tags are searchable and filterable in the customer interface, enabling powerful product discovery.

The platform limits the number of tags per product to prevent spam and maintain relevance. Each tag reference provides essential identifying information without full tag metadata, optimizing API response times.

attributes.description:
The list of definable attribute types (e.g., Size, Color, Material) associated with this product. These define the possible configurable properties for product variants.

The attributes list contains the set of definable product characteristics that can have multiple values, enabling the creation of product variants. Each attribute represents a dimension along which the product can differ, such as size, color, material, capacity, or configuration.

Attributes are classified into types (select, text, number, boolean) which determine how they are presented and validated in the frontend interface. For example, color would typically use 'select' type with predefined options (red, blue, green), while performance specifications might use 'text' type for free-form input.

Each attribute in the list is a summary showing the attribute name, type, required status, and ordering. This information enables the frontend to render appropriate UI elements (dropdowns, radio buttons, text fields) for variant selection. Attributes define the 'space' from which variants are instantiated and are immutable after product creation.

variants.description:
List of all product variants, each representing a unique combination of attribute values (e.g., Red/Medium, Blue/Large). Each variant has its own SKU, pricing, and inventory status.

Product variants are the specific, combinable configurations of a product defined by its attributes. For example, a t-shirt product with attributes 'Size' and 'Color' might have variants including 'Small/Red', 'Medium/Blue', and 'Large/Black'.

Each variant contains essential information for purchase decisions: a unique SKU, specific pricing (which can override the product's base price), inventory availability status, and visual representation (images). The variant summary excludes detailed attribute value definitions to prevent redundancy, as those are covered in the parent attributes definition.

The variants array represents the complete set of purchasable configurations available to customers. The system ensures all variants have valid combinations of defined attributes and prevents duplicates. The availability status of each variant is calculated from real-time inventory data, ensuring accurate representation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant.

This UUID is the primary key used to reference this specific variant across all related systems including inventory, pricing, and sales systems.

Variants are uniquely identified by this ID both for internal system operations and external API references.

Generated as UUID v4 to ensure global uniqueness and avoid collisions across distributed systems.

sku.description:
Stock Keeping Unit code for the product variant.

A unique alphanumeric identifier generated for each variant combination to enable unambiguous tracking in inventory, order processing, and warehouse systems.

SKU generation follows a pattern of product family code + variant attribute codes to ensure uniqueness and dimensional clarity.

Used as the primary reference in external systems and distribution channels.

Example: "KBD-MEK-BLK-WIR-TKL" for "Mechanical Keyboard - Black, Wired, Tenkeyless".

name.description:
Display name of the product variant.

The human-readable name that appears in product listings and customer-facing interfaces.

Typically combines the base product name with key differentiating attributes (e.g., 'Mechanical Keyboard - Black, Wired, Tenkeyless').

Used in search results, product pages, and order confirmations.

Must be unique within the product family to avoid customer confusion.

Generated automatically from variant attributes and product base name.

description.description:
Summary representation of a product variant for administrative and customer-facing displays.

Provides a comprehensive overview of a specific product variant with essential metadata, pricing, availability, and performance metrics.

Designed for use in administrative dashboards where quick insights are required, as well as customer interfaces where variant selection is available.

Excludes detailed attribute specifications (available in separate endpoints) and system-level data (like variant audit logs) for efficiency.

All fields represent reconciled information from multiple sources including inventory systems, pricing engines, product catalogs, and customer engagement platforms.

The schema enables responsive displays that load quickly without requiring additional API calls to related entities.

For detailed variant configuration or attribute combinations, use the full IShoppingMallVariant type.

This summary variant is optimized for list views in administration, product discovery, and product comparison features.

price.description:
Current selling price of this specific variant.

The price at which this variant is offered to customers, reflecting any special pricing, discounts, or promotions.

May differ from base product price due to variant-specific cost differences (e.g., premium materials, additional features).

Price values are synchronized from the pricing management system and updated in real-time.

Requires at least two decimal places for currency precision.

Calculated by applying the variant pricing rule: base_price + price_delta + promotional_adjustment.

Implements multi-currency pricing with automatic conversion based on user location.

base_price.description:
Baseline price for the product without any variant-specific adjustments.

The default price of the parent product before any variant-specific pricing changes are applied.

Used as the foundation for calculating variant pricing through the formula: base_price + price_delta + promotional_adjustment.

Only modified when the fundamental price of the product changes across all variants.

Maintained as a reference point to track pricing history and variance impact.

Acts as the authoritative source for pricing consistency across all variants of a product.

price_delta.description:
Price adjustment specific to this variant relative to the base product.

Represents the monetary value added or subtracted from the base product price to arrive at the final variant price.

Positive values indicate premium variants (e.g., higher quality material), negative values indicate discounted variants (e.g., out-of-season colors).

Used for automated pricing calculations rather than storing the final price directly.

Allows for easier management of price changes across multiple variants simultaneously.


Examples:
- +$20: Quartz crystal display variant of a smartphone
- -$15: Colorway difference with lower material cost
- $0: Standard variant with no special pricing modification

Adjustments are applied during product variant creation and can be modified separately from the base price.

currency.description:
Currency code for the variant's pricing.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code representing the currency in which this variant is priced and sold.

May differ from the store's default currency in international markets or multi-currency stores.

Ensures accurate pricing display and financial reconciliation across different regions.

Used in payment processing and financial reporting systems.

Examples: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, CHF, AUD, HKD.

Price stored as numeric value with currency code separately to support multi-currency operations and exchange rate adjustments.

inventory_quantity.description:
Current quantity of this variant available for sale.

The actual physical stock count available in the warehouse or distribution center.

Updated in real-time as orders are placed and inventory is received.

Affects product availability status and may trigger automated restocking alerts when below threshold.

Excludes reserved inventory for pending orders and backorders.

When at zero, variant is typically marked as out of stock in customer interfaces.

Synced with warehouse management systems and inventory counting processes to maintain accuracy.

reserved_quantity.description:
Quantity of this variant reserved for pending orders.

Inventory that has been allocated to active carts or unfulfilled orders but not yet cleared by payment processing.

Prevents overselling by ensuring inventory can't be purchased until payment clears.

Usually held for a short period (15-30 minutes) before automatic release if payment doesn't complete.

Subtracted from available inventory in customer-facing displays to prevent double sales.

Managed by the cart session system with automatic cleanup of expired reservations after 30 minutes.

out_of_stock_threshold.description:
Minimum threshold quantity at which this variant is considered low stock.

When inventory_quantity falls to or below this level, the system triggers low-stock alerts to the product team.

Helps prevent stockouts by giving advance notice to replenish inventory before selling out completely.

May vary by variant based on sales velocity, lead time for restocking, and criticality of the product.

Stock level calculations use: if inventory_quantity <= out_of_stock_threshold, then status = "low_stock".

Typical values range from 1-5 for high-velocity items to 10-50 for low-velocity products, configured by product managers based on historical sales data.

oneOf.description:
Current availability status of this variant.

A computed flag derived from inventory_quantity, out_of_stock_threshold, and product lifecycle stage.

In_stock: inventory_quantity > 0
Low_stock: inventory_quantity <= out_of_stock_threshold && inventory_quantity > 0
Out_of_stock: inventory_quantity = 0
Pre_order: product is not yet available but accepting orders
Discontinued: product is no longer produced or sold

Used to determine display logic in customer interfaces and search result ranking.

is_published.description:
Whether this variant is currently visible to customers.

Controls whether the variant appears in product listings, search results, and category pages.

Useful for rolling out new variants gradually, or temporarily removing variants without deleting them.

When false, the variant will not appear in customer-facing interfaces, even if inventory is available.

Can be toggled independently of inventory status for marketing flexibility.

Admins can publish/unpublish variants to control product market availability separate from inventory constraints.

product_id.description:
Reference to the parent product this variant belongs to.

The unique identifier of the base product entity that this variant is an alternative version of.

Variants are always child entities of a parent product and cannot exist independently.

Used to group related variants for display and management purposes.

Parent product contains shared information (main image, category, brand) while variants provide customization.

This relationship enables SKU-to-product association and maintains product lineage across the catalog.

product_name.description:
Name of the parent product this variant belongs to.

The human-readable title of the base product that this variant modifies.

Provided here for convenience to avoid additional API calls when displaying variant information.

When this variant is displayed in a product listing, the product_name appears as the main title.

Note: This is a reference field from the base product's name and is not directly editable on the variant level.

Represents the product' primary title as configured by product managers and remains unchanged even when variant names are customized.

product_brand.description:
Brand information associated with the parent product of this variant.

This summarizes the brand that manufactures or owns the product line of which this variant is a part.

The brand provides context for product quality, reputation, and target market.

This object contains the essential brand information needed for customer-facing displays without requiring additional lookups.

Projection of the parent product's brand information.

Includes brand ID, name, logo URL, and description for a complete brand context.

Brand information is inherited from the parent product and serves as trust signal during product discovery and sales conversion.

product_category.description:
Primary category classification of the parent product for this variant.

The main category under which this product and its variants are organized in the catalog.

Used for navigation, filtering, and search indexing to help customers discover products.

May differ from secondary categories which provide additional classification.

Includes category ID, name, slug, and hierarchy path to enable full taxonomy representation.

Provides critical context for product positioning and market segmentation.

Category assignment is managed by product managers and drives the product's placement in the site's information architecture.

variant_attributes.description:
List of attributes that distinguish this specific variant from others.

Each attribute represents a configurable feature of the product that creates this unique variant combination.

Examples include color, size, material, capacity, or connectivity options.

This information enables customers to understand the precise characteristics of this variant.

Attributes are standardized across variants for consistency and ensure accurate search filtering.

Contains attribute ID, type, name, value, and display formatting.

Only includes attributes that are actually configured for this variant.

Used in product comparison tools, filtering systems, and variant selection interfaces to allow customers to distinguish between product options.

available_options_count.description:
Number of distinct attribute combinations available for this product.

The total count of all possible variations that can be created from this product's configurator.

Provides customers insight into the breadth of choices available for this product line.

Used in automated merchandising and promotional strategies to promote products with high configurability.

Calculates as: multiply counts of each attribute's option values.

This is a calculated field based on the predefined attribute values and does not change with inventory.

Example: If a product has 3 colors, 4 sizes, and 2 finishes, available_options_count = 3 × 4 × 2 = 24.

reviews_count.description:
Total number of customer reviews received for this specific variant.

Counts all published reviews directly associated with this variant.

Used to calculate the aggregate rating and to signal product popularity and social proof.

Reviews are only counted from verified purchases of this exact variant.

Helps customers assess quality and reliability through peer feedback.

May be used in ranking search results and product recommendations.

Managed through content moderation system to ensure authenticity and compliance with review guidelines.

average_rating.description:
Average customer rating for this specific variant.

The mean value of all numeric ratings provided in customer reviews for this variant.

Ratings are on a 1-5 scale and are calculated with precision (allowing decimal values).

A high average rating is a strong indicator of customer satisfaction and product quality.

Used in product ranking, featured placements, and purchase decision support.

Only reviews with numeric ratings contribute to this calculation.

Implemented using weighted average algorithm that considers review age, reviewer reputation, and verified purchase status.

sales_count.description:
Total number of units sold for this variant across all time.

Counts completed orders for this specific variant since its release.

Key performance indicator for market demand and inventory planning.

Used to identify top-selling variants for promotional emphasis and stock optimization.

Excludes canceled orders and returns in the count.

Syncs with daily sales analytics system and is recalculated nightly based on confirmed orders.

visibility_score.description:
Algorithmic score determining this variant's prominence in search and recommendations.

A composite metric calculated from multiple factors including sales velocity, review count, rating, inventory levels, and freshness.

Used by the search and discovery engine to rank variants in search results and recommendation lists.

Higher scores result in better placement in search results, "trending" lists, and "best sellers" sections.

Automatically recalculated nightly based on current performance data.

Normalized to 0-1 range for consistent ranking across diverse product categories.

Formula: 0.4 × (normalized sales) + 0.3 × (normalized ratings) + 0.2 × (normalized inventory) + 0.1 × (recent updates).

variant_tagged.description:
List of predefined tags assigned to this variant for marketing and merchandising.

Tags are manually or automatically assigned to categorize variants for promotional purposes, discovery, or categorization.

Examples: "hot selling", "new arrival", "best value", "limited edition", "top rated".

Used for automated filtering, featured banners, and targeted promotions.

Business users can add or remove tags based on marketing strategy.

Tags are semantic labels, not searchable keywords - they're used for classification, not search.

Generated through a combination of automated analysis (e.g., high sales velocity) and manual curation by marketing team.

location_zones.description:
Geographic zones where this variant is currently available for sale.

Defines the regions or countries where customers can purchase this variant.

Used to manage regional availability, compliance requirements, and shipping restrictions.

May differ from the parent product's availability zone.

Typical zones: "North America", "Europe", "Asia Pacific", "Global".

When empty, indicates the variant is available in all regions where the parent product is sold.

Managed by compliance and logistics teams to ensure adherence to regional regulations and distribution agreements.

A meta description optimized for search engines that succinctly describes key benefits and specifications.

adminUserCount.description:
Total number of active administrative users in the system. This count represents all admin actors with elevated privileges who can access administrative interfaces and perform governance operations.

Computed from the shopping_mall_admins table, excluding deactivated accounts. This metric provides insight into the size of the administrative team responsible for platform operations and security.

systemHealthStatus.description:
Current system health condition represented as a status code. Valid values include: 'healthy', 'warning', 'degraded', and 'critical'.

This status is calculated by analyzing real-time monitoring alerts from shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts, database connection health, payment gateway availability, and server resource utilization metrics. The status reflects the overall operational health of the platform infrastructure.

pendingVerificationCount.description:
Number of seller accounts awaiting verification. These are new or updated seller registrations that require manual review before becoming active.

Based on the shopping_mall_seller_onboarding_completion table where verification status is pending. This metric helps identify bottlenecks in the seller onboarding process and resource needs for compliance teams.

transactionVolumeLast24H.description:
Total number of completed transactions (orders) processed in the last 24 hours.

Calculated from the shopping_mall_order_events table where event type indicates successful order completion. This metric is critical for understanding platform activity levels and identifying unusual patterns that may indicate fraud or system issues.

pendingOrderCount.description:
Number of orders in 'processing' or 'payment_pending' status awaiting completion.

Based on the shopping_mall_order_events table with specific status types. This metric indicates operational workload and potential fulfillment bottlenecks that may require attention from customer service or logistics teams.

sellerPerformanceRatingAverage.description:
Average performance rating across all active sellers on the platform, on a 1-5 scale.

Computed from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_metrics table using weighted averages of fulfillment speed, customer satisfaction ratings, and dispute resolution rates. This metric indicates overall marketplace quality and seller reliability.

suspiciousActivityAlerts.description:
Number of system-generated security alerts for suspicious or potentially fraudulent activity.

Based on the shopping_mall_monitoring_alerts table with alert categories including duplicate accounts, abnormal login patterns, payment fraud indicators, and bulk listing activity. This metric helps the security team prioritize investigation priorities.

configurationChangesSinceLastCheck.description:
Number of system configuration changes made since the last overview update.

Tracked from the shopping_mall_config_history table with timestamps. This metric indicates system stability and helps identify if recent configuration changes may be contributing to any observed anomalies.

Configuration changes include feature flags, payment gateway settings, shipping rules, or other system-wide parameter modifications.

totalReviewsCount.description:
Total number of product reviews submitted by customers across the entire marketplace.

Aggregated from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table. This metric provides insight into customer engagement levels and the volume of feedback being generated on the platform.

lowStockProductsCount.description:
Number of product variants with inventory levels below the predefined threshold.

Calculated from the shopping_mall_product_variant_inventory table using configured minimum inventory levels. This metric helps inventory managers identify which products may need replenishment.

pendingRefundsCount.description:
Number of refund requests waiting for processing or approval.

Based on the shopping_mall_order_refunds table with status indicating pending or awaiting review. This metric indicates potential customer service workload and financial liability.

activePaymentGateways.description:
Number of payment methods currently active and available to customers.

Counted from the shopping_mall_payment_methods table where enabled status is true. This metric ensures payment infrastructure reliability and helps identify if payment processing capabilities are reducing.

disputeCount.description:
Number of active payment disputes from customers, typically related to chargebacks or unauthorized transactions.

Based on the shopping_mall_payment_disputes table. This metric is critical for financial risk management and indicates the effectiveness of fraud prevention systems.

complianceRecordsCount.description:
Total count of official compliance documentation records maintained for regulatory requirements such as GDPR, CCPA, and tax compliance.

Based on the shopping_mall_compliance_records table. This metric ensures the platform maintains proper legal and regulatory documentation for all jurisdictions it operates in.

auditLogEntriesLast7Days.description:
Total number of administrative audit log entries generated in the last 7 days.

Based on the shopping_mall_audit_logs table. This metric helps assess administrative activity levels and ensures proper audit trail maintenance with appropriate granularity.

dataExportRequestsCount.description:
Number of outstanding data export requests initiated by administrators for reporting or compliance purposes.

Based on the shopping_mall_data_exports table with status indicating pending or processing. This metric tracks administrative sourcing of bulk data and ensures timely completion of data requests.

IShoppingMallAdminOverview.description:
Comprehensive administrative dashboard overview containing aggregated metrics for platform governance, security monitoring, and operational efficiency.

This schema represents the key performance indicators and system state information presented to platform administrators on the admin dashboard. It consolidates data from multiple sources including administrative user accounts, system monitoring alerts, payment systems, seller performance metrics, order management, and compliance records.

The dashboard provides a 360-degree view of platform health with actionable insights for administration, including system stability indicators, financial metrics, security concerns, compliance obligations, and operational workload. All metrics are aggregated and anonymized to protect individual privacy while still providing complete operational visibility.

Developers should note that this object does not contain any personally identifiable information (PII) of individual users or sellers; it exclusively contains aggregated metrics, status codes, and counts suitable for administrative reporting.

This overview is designed to be consumed as an initial dashboard loading state, with more granular data available through separate endpoint calls for detailed investigation (GET /audit/logs, GET /system/metrics, etc).

IShoppingMallReviewModeration.IRequest.description:
Moderation action details for reviewing a product review, including the action type and optional comment. This schema is used exclusively in administrator-initiated review moderation operations to record decisions on product reviews that violate platform guidelines.

This request DTO specifies the mandatory moderation action to be taken on a product review and allows optional contextual commentary from the administrator. When submitted, the system creates an immutable audit log entry in the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table that records the administrator's action, timestamp, and any provided comment.

All moderation actions are subject to strict authorization controls that restrict usage to administrators only. The system validates that the referenced review exists and is in a modifiable state before processing the request. This interface ensures a standardized, auditable approach to content moderation while allowing administrators appropriate discretion in their decisions.

This schema directly maps to the administrative function provided by the endpoint: PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/reviews/{reviewId}/moderate.

oneOf.description:
The moderation action to be taken on the review.

- "approve": Accept and publish the review. This removes any pending flag status and makes the review visible to all users.
- "reject": Remove the review from public view. The review is hidden from customers but maintained in the system for audit purposes.
- "flag": Mark the review for further review by moderation team. This preserves the review's visibility while indicating it requires additional human assessment.

The action field is mandatory and must be exactly one of the three permitted values. This enum ensures consistent moderation workflows and prevents ambiguous or unsupported actions.

These action types correspond directly to the moderation workflow defined in business requirements and are constrained to these three specific values to maintain audit trail integrity and prevent misuse.

- "flag": Mark the review for further review by moderation team. This preserves the review's visibility while indicating it requires additional human assessment.

The action field is mandatory and must be exactly one of the three permitted values. This enum ensures consistent moderation workflows and prevents ambiguous or unsupported actions.

These action types correspond directly to the moderation workflow defined in business requirements and are constrained to these three specific values to maintain audit trail integrity and prevent misuse.

comment.description:
An optional comment provided by the administrator explaining the moderation decision.

This field allows administrators to document their reasoning for a moderation action, which can be used for training purposes, internal reference, or customer communication (if appropriate). The comment is stored in the moderation log but is not displayed to customers.

Length is limited to 500 characters to ensure comments remain concise and focused while providing sufficient context for administrators to justify their decisions. Comments should be professional, objective, and reference specific policy violations when applicable.

This field is optional and can be omitted if no additional explanation is needed.

oneOf.description:
Current status of the delivery estimation process.

Indicates the stage of the order's delivery lifecycle. Status transitions occur automatically based on shipment events and carrier tracking data.

- "processing": Order has been placed but no shipment has been created yet. No delivery estimate available.
- "shipped": Shipment record created with carrier and estimated delivery window, but carrier tracking has not yet commenced.
- "in_transit": Carrier has accepted the package and tracking data is being received. Estimate is dynamically updated as location data becomes available.
- "out_for_delivery": Package has arrived at the final delivery hub and is scheduled for delivery on the estimated date.
- "delivered": Package has been successfully delivered and confirmed by the recipient or carrier.
- "delayed": Estimated delivery date has been exceeded due to carrier issues, weather, customs, or other unforeseen circumstances.
- "cancelled": Delivery has been cancelled by customer, carrier, or seller.
